articles.content: Edited by John Hendryx in epub , .mobi & .pdf formats Since faith is infinitely beyond all the power of our unregenerated human nature, it is only God who can give the spiritual ears to hear and eyes to see the beauty of Christ in the gospel. God alone disarms the hostility of the sinner turning his heart of stone to a heart of flesh (2 Cor 4:4-6). It is God, the Holy Spirit, alone who gives illumination and understanding of His word that we might believe; It is God who raises us from the death of sin, who circumcises the heart; unplugs our ears; It is God alone who can give us a new sense, a spiritual capacity to behold the beauty and unsurpassed excellency of Jesus Christ. The apostle John recorded Jesus saying to Nicodemus that we naturally love darkness, hate the light and WILL NOT come into the light (John 3:19, 20). And since our hardened resistance to God is thus seated in our affections, only God, by His grace, can lovingly change, overcome and pacify our rebellious disposition. The natural man, apart from the quickening work of the Holy Spirit, will not come to Christ on his own since he is at enmity with God and cannot understand spiritual things (1 Cor 2:14). Shining a light into a blind man's eyes will not enable him to see, because eyesight first requires a set of healthy eyes.
articles.content_zh: 由John Hendryx在Epub编辑, . 惟有上帝解除了罪人将石心变成肉心的敌意(2 Cor 4:4-6). 只有真主,即圣灵,能照亮和理解我们的信仰; 真主使我们脱离罪恶之死,他割取我们的心;他揭开我们的耳朵; 只有上帝才能给我们一种新的感官,一种精神能力,来见证耶稣基督的美丽和无比杰出。 使徒约翰录制了耶稣对尼克德穆斯说,我们自然地热爱黑暗,憎恨光明并不会进入光明(John 3:19,20). 既然我们对上帝的顽强抵抗 被放在我们的慈爱中 只有上帝能以他的恩惠 慈悲地改变 克服并平息我们的叛逆 自然之人,除了"圣灵"的快活活外,不会独自来到基督,因为他对上帝怀有敌意并无法理解精神事物(1 Cor 2:14). 把一盏光照入一个盲人的眼中不会让他看到,因为视力首先需要一组健康的眼睛.

Our hearts are like fortresses under attack, and we must guard them accordingly. Most people will diligently guard their fortunes and homes, which are of temporal value, but they are very careless about guarding that which is of eternal value their very souls! articles.content: by Louis Berkhof In ePub , .mobi and .pdf formats You may also download the separate Introductory Volume to Systematic Theology here. Professor Berkhof, who was the President of Calvin Seminary and professor of Systematic Theology at the same in the first half of the twentieth century, has given us an excellent compendium of Reformed theological thought in this hefty volume. The subject is treated in the classical style, moving through the Doctrines of God, Man in Relation to God, the Person and Work of Christ, the Application of the Work of Redemption, the Church and the Means of Grace, and the Last Things. For decades, Louis Berkhof’s Systematic Theology has remained one of the most important and widely-used systematic theologies. It provides the clearest and most succinct articulation of Reformed theology. From its first publication in 1932, Berkhof’s work was revised, reprinted, and translated into Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, and Portuguese, and it had become a standard theological text by 1950. It has gained near-universal use in seminaries and Bible colleges across the world, and is widely cited and used by pastors, theologians, and students of nearly all denominational affiliations.
articles.content_zh: 由路易·伯克霍夫(Louis Berkhof)撰写 在ePub,.mobi和.pdf格式中 您也可以在此下载系统神学的单独入门卷 。 贝尔克霍夫教授曾于20世纪上半叶担任卡尔文神学院院长和系统神学教授,在本书中为我们提供了一份出色的改革神学思想简编. 主题以古典风格来对待,通过"上帝的理论","人与上帝的关系","基督的人与工作","救赎之作的应用","教会与恩赐的手段","最后的事情"等来进行. 数十年来,路易·伯克霍夫的"系统神学"仍然是最重要和被广泛应用的系统神学之一. 它为改革神学提供了最清楚和最简洁的阐述。 从1932年的首次出版起,伯克霍夫的作品被修改,再版,并被翻译成了中文,日文,韩文,西班牙文和葡萄牙文,到1950年已经成为标准的神学文本. 它在世界各地的神学院和圣经学院获得了近乎普遍的使用,并被牧师、神学家和几乎所有教派派别的学生广泛引用和使用。

articles.content: by Thomas Manton in ePub , .mobi & .pdf formats SUCH is the divine matter and admirable order of the Lord’s Prayer, as became the eternal wisdom of God, that composed and dictated it to his disciples. In it are opened the fountains of all our regular petitions, and the arguments contained to encourage our hopes for obtaining them. In our addresses to men, our study is to conciliate their favourable audience; but God is most graciously inclined and ready to grant our requests, therefore we are directed to call upon him by the title of ‘Our Father in heaven,’ to assure us of his love and power, and thereby to excite our reverent attention, to raise our affections, to confirm our confidence in prayer. The supreme end of our desires is the glory of God, in conjunction with our own happiness: this is expressed in the two first petitions, that ‘his name may be hallowed,’ and ‘his kingdom come,’ that we may partake of its felicity. In order to this, our desires are directed for the means that are proper and effectual to accomplish it. And those are of two kinds — the good things that conduct us, and the removal of those evils that obstruct our happiness.
articles.content_zh: 由托马斯·曼顿(Thomas Manton)在ePub所著, . 它打开了我们所有正常请愿书的泉源,并包含了鼓励我们获得这些请愿书的希望的论据。 我们在对人的讲话中,研究是调和他们的好听众;但上帝最慷慨地倾向于并准备同意我们的请求,因此我们奉“我们天上之父”之名号召他,向我们保证他的爱和力量,从而激起我们的敬爱,提高我们的爱心,确认我们对祈祷的信心。 我们欲望的最高目的,是上帝的荣耀,与我们自己的幸福相配合:这在最初的两件请愿书中都有所表述:"他的名字或许是神圣的","他的国来临了",以便我们分享它的荣耀. 为此,我们的愿望是找到适当和有效的手段来实现这一目标。 这些有两种—— 引导我们的好东西, 以及消除那些阻碍我们幸福的邪恶。

articles.content: by Louis Berkhof in ePub , .mobi & .pdf formats This volume is a prolegomena for Berkhof's SystematicTheology . In it he defines the concept of dogmatic theology, theology, apologetics, ethics, and science. He also explains the Reformed doctrine of revelation and inspiration. It exxplains what is a theology and how should it be defined? Is theology necessary? What is the task of theology and what are the methods which it should use? What is religion? Is it possible for God to reveal himself to human beings, and how? How can we know if the Bible is the Word of God? For those who are considering going to Seminary, to be pastors or simply Christians with ample knowledge of their faith, this is a good book to begin with. This is a very helpful volume in understanding the foundational matters of theology, ranging from the nature of Dogmatics, to the grounds of our knowledge of God, to the doctrines concerning scripture. Berkhof spends a fair amount of time discussing the differing theologies of Rome, Schleiermacher, Barth, etc. but he does it to show how they contrast with the true and full Christian Theology, namely the Reformed tradition. ----- TABLE OF CONTENTS Preface The Idea and History of Dogmatic Theology I. articles.content: J. C. Ryle "My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand. My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all. No one is able to snatch them out of my Father's hand." (John 10:27-29) About the first part of this text, beloved, I spoke to you this morning. I told you then that this passage contains two things—first the character of true Christians, and secondly their privileges—first what they are to their Savior, and secondly what their Savior is to them. Let me, then, remind you what the text says of their character. "My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me." (John 10:27) 1. God's children, His real believing people, are compared to sheep , because they are gentle, quiet, harmless and inoffensive; because they are useful and do good to all around them; because they love to be together, and dislike separation; and lastly because they are very helpless and wandering and liable to stray. 2. Jesus calls them " My sheep ," as if they were His peculiar property. "Mine," He would have us know, by election, "Mine" by purchase, and "Mine" by adoption. 3. Christ's sheep hear His voice, they listen humbly to His teaching, they take His word for their rule and guide. 4. Christ's sheep follow Him, they walk in the narrow path He has marked out, they do not refuse because it is sometimes steep and narrow--but wherever the line of duty lies they go forward without doubting.

articles.content: by Archibald Alexander In ePub , .mobi and .pdf formats On the basis of fifty years as a pastor, preacher and professor at Princeton Theological Seminary, Archibald Alexander (1772-1851) deals with the subjective work of the Holy Spirit in the heart in all its phases, from the new birth until final preparation for heaven. There are two kinds of religious knowledge which, though intimately connected as cause and effect, may nevertheless be distinguished. These are the knowledge of the truth as it is revealed in the Holy Scriptures; and the impression which that truth makes on the human mind when rightly apprehended. The first may be compared to the inscription or image on a seal, the other to the impression made by the seal on the wax. When that impression is clearly and distinctly made, we can understand, by contemplating it, the true inscription on the seal more satisfactorily, than by a direct view of the seal itself. Thus it is found that nothing tends more to confirm and elucidate the truths contained in the Word, than an inward experience of their efficacy on the heart. It cannot, therefore, be uninteresting to the Christian to have these effects, as they consist in the various views and affections of the mind, traced out and exhibited in their connection with the truth, and in their relation to each other.
articles.content_zh: 由Archibald Alexander In ePub , .mobi 和.pdf格式编辑 。 在担任普林斯顿神学院牧师,传道人和教授50年的基础上,阿奇博尔德·亚历山大(1772年-1851年)处理从新出世到最后准备上天等各个阶段的心灵圣灵的主观工作. 宗教知识有两种,虽然作为因果关系有着密切的联系,但仍可加以区分。 这些是《圣经》中所揭示的真理的知识;以及真理在人心上所留下的正确捕捉的印象。 第一种可以和封印上所刻的铭文或图像相提并论,另一种可以和蜡上所刻的封印的印象相提并论. 当这种印象清楚而明显地形成时,我们可以通过考虑它来理解印章上的真正铭文,比直接看到印章本身更令人满意。 因此,人们发现,最能证实和阐明《言语》中包含的真理的莫过于内在的内心体验。 因此,基督教徒对这些影响不能不感兴趣,因为这些影响包含在思想的各种观点和感情中,在他们与真理的关系上,以及在他们与彼此的关系上,被追溯和表现出来。

But, alas! after our utmost and most diligent inquiries, we must say, How little a portion is it of him that we can understand! His glory is incomprehensible, and his praises are unutterable. Some things an illuminated mind may conceive of it; but what we can express in comparison of what it is in itself, is even less than nothing. articles.title_zh: 时髦人士和其他世俗主义者的护教学
articles.content: "Although They Knew God ... They Suppressed the Truth..." The opportunities are wide open for Christians to speak with secular people these days, especially if you live in a metropolitan area. The average hipster you may meet in the medium to big sized city is a secularist who may listen to NPR, has a liberal, ecological, and/or anti-capitalist political ideology ... wears vintage clothing from a thrift store and consumes ethically. He or she often either rides a bike, uses public transportation or even may be driving a hybrid or bio-diesel vehicle. This person is deeply concerned with the ethical treatment of animals, is strongly against slavery, torture, racism and political oppression against women. In other words, he takes morality very seriously. Another characteristic of this individual is that he/she thinks Christianity is irrelevant at best. Since we deeply care about the eternal destinies of such individuals how should we go about reaching such a person with the gospel? Where would you start? Once of the more effective ways, I have found, is to remember that that your secular friend already knows God exists. He/she knows God exists and lives as if He does. In Romans chapter 1 Paul clearly teaches this about all people when he says, "For although they knew God" (verse 21) "...by their unrighteousness suppress the truth" (verse 18). But how can we demonstrate to your friends that they already believe in God, when intellectually they deny His existence? While there are many ways this could be done, I would like to suggest one way that I have found to be quite persuasive: The knowledge of God through their own morality.

Here, in an accessible format, is Lye’s explanation of his seven-part method. While some of the advice relates to his published version of the catechism, the seven basic steps or rules may be widely applied. The reader should note that Lye was so accustomed to catechising people by means of a ‘question and answer’ method, that even his instructions concerning catechesis are communicated in sequential questions and answers! Introducing the Rules for Catechizing Q. 1. Are there any rules proposed to be observed in catechizing? A. Yes. Q. 2. Is there a title to those rules? A. Yes. Q. 3. Which is the title to those rules? A. A form of examination according to the rules or method proposed to be observed in catechizing. Q. 4. Is catechizing an ordinance? A. Yes. Q. 5. Whose ordinance? Is it God’s? A. Yes. Q. 6. How do you prove it? A. I prove it out of Proverbs 22:6: ‘Train up (or catechize) a child in the way that he [or she] should go, and when they are old they will not [or at least they should not] depart from it.’ Q. 7. How many rules are there to be observed in catechizing? A. Seven. Rule 1: Read and Return Q. 8. Which is the first rule to be observed in catechizing? A. Let the question be barely propounded, and the answer returned. Rule 2: Yes or No? Q. 9. What is the second rule? A. Try the child’s understanding, whether he (she) doth discern truth from falsehood. Q. 10. How shall the child manifest that? A. Only by saying Yes or No, to such short questions as may be raised from the preceding answer. Q. 11. Where are they set down? A. Next to the answers. Q. 12. Why is this necessary? A. Because to repeat words, and not to understand the truths contained in them, is but to act the parrot, and profits very little. Q. 13. But how must the child be made to say Yes or No? A. Without book only. Q. 14. Why then do we use to read them? 2 A. For two reasons. 1. Because we should learn to read them exactly. 2. Because the oftener we do read them, and the better we do consider them, the more capable we shall be to answer them truly without book, if we should (at any time) be so examined. Rule 3: Check the Words Q. 15. What is the third rule? A. Try the child’s ability to express his (or her) knowledge of the meaning of every hard and difficult word or phrase in the preceding answer. Q. 16. What reason is there for this? A. Because we cannot rightly apprehend truths, unless we clearly understand the meaning of those words in which truths are wrapped up. Q. 17. What may be of special use for an help to the child herein? A. The Alphabetical Table at the end of this catechism Q. 18. How may I find any difficult word in the Table? A. Mark with what letter it begins, and then look for it under the same letter in the Table. Q. 19. How may I know the difficult words in the answers? A. Note, that every difficult word explained in the Table is printed with a black English character in every answer. Rule 4: Prove the Point(s) Q. 20. What is the fourth rule? A. Draw the whole answer into several doctrinal propositions (if it contains more than one) and bid the child prove each or either of them by Scripture. Q. 21. Why should the answer be drawn into several doctrinal propositions? A. For two reasons: 1. Because there are several distinct truths contained in several answers of the catechism. 2. Because the more distinctly and particularly any truth is proposed, the more capable the child’s understanding is to apprehend it. Q. 22. Why must the child prove each of these doctrinal propositions by Scripture? A. Because the Holy Scriptures are the only foundation and proof of infallible and saving truth. Rule 5: Observe the Scriptures Q. 23. What is the fifth rule? A. Take the several Scriptures annexed to the answer, and in order propose them distinctly to the child:

A. 我从 " Proverbs " 22:6中证明: " 训练(或授精)一个儿童,以便他(或她)去,当他们老了,他们不会[或至少他们不应该]离开。 " 问题7. 分类时要遵守多少规则? A.七. 第1条:阅读和返回问题8. 哪些是第一条在编目中遵守的规则? A. 让问题几乎不提,答案就回来了。 规则2:是还是否? A. 试看孩子的理智,无论他从谎言中辨别真理。 问题10. 孩子怎么表现? A. 没有书。 问题14. 为什么我们用它来读? 2 A. 原因有两个。 1. 因为我们应当学习准确阅读。 2. 因为我们越经常地阅读,而且我们越看好,如果我们(在任何时候)接受这样的审查,我们就越有能力在没有书的情况下真正回答这些问题。 第3条:检查"字"Q. 第三个规则是什么? A. 尝试儿童表达(或她)对前一个答案中每个困难和困难的词或短语含义的了解的能力。 问题16. 这有什么原因? A. 因为我们不能正确地抓住真理,除非我们清楚地理解那些掩盖真理的文字的含义。 问题17. 向儿童提供帮助有何特别用? A. 本目录末尾的字母表 Q 18. 我怎么才能在桌子上找到任何困难的词? A. 标出它开始的字母,然后在表格的同名字母下查找. 问题19. 我怎么会知道答案中的困难? A. 注意,表格中解释的每个困难字,每个答案中都用黑色的英文字符打印出. 第4条:证明问题20。 第四个规则是什么? A. 将整个答案归纳为几个理论性建议(如果包含一个以上),并让儿童通过《圣经》证明每个或其中之一。 问题21. 答案为何应纳入若干理论性建议? articles.content: Next week marks the launch of a new video and audio resource from the Banner— Westminster Wednesdays . Each week our Communications Manager, Joshua Kellard, will be joined by a special guest for an in-depth conversation on the questions and answers contained in the Westminster Shorter Catechism. Here Joshua answers some questions about what viewers and listeners can expect from the series: Are these podcasts just for Presbyterians, or for a wider audience who may not be as familiar with the Shorter Catechism? These podcasts most certainly are for Presbyterians, but not exclusively so! The Westminster Shorter Catechism is an accessible and crisp statement of the Christian faith as it was recovered and clarified at and shortly after the Reformation. Therefore, I would venture to say that any true believer in the Lord Jesus who takes up the Shorter Catechism will find it to be a document that is rich, biblically rooted, encouraging, and edifying. We hope that these podcast episodes are all these things, too. And, I might add, not all our guests are Presbyterians! The point is to use the Shorter Catechism to help us understand and apply Scripture’s teaching What does each episode include? How long will each episode last? Each episode of Westminster Wednesdays begins with a reading of the question and answer for that week (sometimes there are two or even three, depending on the topic). Then we have an in-depth conversation on the biblical teaching covered by the question and answer with a special guest—usually a local church pastor, but we have a scattering of seminary teachers represented as well. Above: Some of the Westminster Wednesdays guests. The point is to use the Shorter Catechism to help us understand and apply Scripture’s teaching, especially with a view to helping all who listen to teach others in turn. We will often pause, for example, to ask how a father or mother might teach the truths covered on a given week to their children. The episodes are about 15 to 20 minutes in length. There is minimal ‘fluff’—we try to get straight to the topic at hand. How might the series help listeners in their devotions, and as they serve in the church? All biblical truth, seen by the light of faith, should motivate us to thank, praise, and love the Lord more. Given that the Shorter Catechism summarizes scriptural truth for understanding and for devotion, we should be able to see reasons to thank, praise, and stand in awe of God every week. That said, no merely human document should ever take the place of hearing and reading Scripture. The more time anyone spends in a confession or a catechism, the more they should be motivated to return to the Scriptures with fresh perspective and deeper hunger. We also hope the series will be a blessing to churches. For one thing, well–taught Christians are a blessing to the church. They can and should find ways to build up other members in the faith. It may also be the case that we have some pastors and elders watching or listening in. If so, we hope and trust they will be encouraged to consider whether catechesis could be part of their approach to teaching their congregations. Churches that practice both expository preaching and steady catechesis have often found these modes of teaching to be mutually reinforcing. Why did you choose to use the Shorter Catechism as a framework? There are quite a few Reformed catechisms out there, but only a handful are in frequent use today. The Shorter Catechism has the advantage of broad scope (there are 107 questions and answers in this ‘shorter’ document!) coupled with memorable expression. And, as Dr Chad Van Dixhoorn shares in our bonus historical episode Behind the Scenes at the Westminster Assembly (releasing 28 October), each of the questions and answers is a stand-alone unit—one doesn’t have to have read the whole document to understand what is being asked and answered. articles.content_zh: 下星期将推出来自班纳-威斯敏斯特星期三的新视频和音频资源。 我们的通讯经理Joshua Kellard 每周都会有一位特邀嘉宾参加, 深入讨论威斯敏斯特短卡捷主义的问答。 在这里,约书亚回答了一些关于观众和听众可以从系列中期待什么的问题: 这些播客只是给长老会的,还是给那些可能不太熟悉"更短卡通"的更广大的观众的? 这些播客当然是长老会的, 威斯敏斯特·肖特克·卡特克主义(Westminster Shorter Catechism)是基督教信仰的一种易懂而简洁的表述,因为它在改革期间和之后不久被恢复和澄清. 因此,我冒昧地说,任何真正相信耶稣主的人,如果接受更短的卡德克主义,就会发现它是一份富饶、圣经根基、鼓励和启发性的文件。 我们希望这些播客节目也是这些东西。 还有,我想补充一下,不是所有的客人都是长老会的! 关键在于运用更短的卡德主义来帮助我们理解并应用圣经的教导, 每集会持续多久? 每集"威斯敏斯特周三"以阅读该周的问答开始(有时根据话题的不同会有两集甚至三集). 然后,我们与一位特别的来宾——通常是一位当地教会牧师——深入讨论了问答中包含的圣经教义问题,但我们也有众多神学院教师的代表。 上:一些西敏周三来宾. 重点是利用"更短的卡德克主义"帮助我们理解并应用"圣经"的教义,特别是为了帮助所有倾听者依次教导他人. 例如,我们往往会停下来问,父亲或母亲如何向其子女传授某一周的真相。 剧集长度约15至20分钟. 我们尽量直截了当, 该系列如何帮助听众的奉献,以及他们在教堂中服役? 所有的圣经真理,由信仰之光所见,应该激励我们感谢,赞美,更爱主. 鉴于 " 更短的卡特克主义 " 为理解和奉献总结了文字上的真理,我们应该能够每周看到感谢、赞扬和敬畏上帝的理由。 尽管如此,绝不应仅以人类文件取而代之的是听取和阅读《圣经》。 任何人在忏悔或阴道中花费的时间越多,就越应该以新的视角和更深的饥饿来激励他们回到"圣经". 我们也希望这一系列会给教会带来祝福. 首先,教好基督徒是教会的福分。 他们能够而且应当找到办法,在信仰中培养其他成员。 也可能是有些牧师和长老在看或听。 如果是这样,我们希望并相信,将鼓励他们考虑,天主教会能否成为他们教会的一部分。 既进行说明式传道,又进行平稳天主教的教会往往发现这些教学方式是相辅相成的。 你为什么选择用"更短的卡特主义"作为框架? 那里有很多改革式的天主教,但今天只有很少的宗教经常使用。 Shorter Catechism具有广泛的优势(本文"shorter"文件中有107个问答), 而正如Chad Van Dixhoorn博士在威斯敏斯特大会(10月28日放出)的《幕后新闻》中分享的, 读者常常被俗称神学或牧业所震撼。

articles.title_zh: 讲道中的陷阱：一封关于申请的信
articles.content: The following letter was published in the December 2025 issue of the Banner Magazine. It is published here at the request of a reader who found it helpful, in the hope that its counsel might be blessed to others also. You can also listen to a reading of this letter on the Banner Podcast. Dear J______, Following our conversation about application in preaching, I thought I would send along some thoughts I have had over the years on the subject. I want to point out some pitfalls you may want to keep in mind as you train R______. The only reason I know about them is from spending too much time in them myself! There has been a lot of self–examination and repenting over the years for me in this matter. The first thought is that too often (even in some of the best books on preaching) we hear that the text drives the sermon. This is a half-truth. A potentially dangerous half-truth. I have seen a man so intent on expositing his text well (and he did it very well) that he did not seem to notice or care that a third of the people in the room walked out before he finished preaching because he went on so long and the last meal of the conference was being served to meet the constraint of local train times. A wrong type of focus on the text and its explanation can make us oblivious to the very people the text is for. A preacher who stands up to preach having spent ninety per cent of his sermon preparation time in the week concentrating on the biblical text has not sufficiently realized what preaching actually is. In their book Letters Along the Way D. A. Carson and John Woodbridge put it this way: A chief reason why so much of what passes for evangelical expository preaching is so boring and irrelevant is that the preacher has spent a vastly disproportionate amount of preparation time in exegesis and outlines, and so little in thinking through how the Word of God is to wound and heal (to use the language of Hosea). 1 So preaching is about people. Preaching is about what God has to say to people about their lives . The text for a sermon is what God has to say to people . So the text of a sermon is like the recipe for a dish. A good cook would never be so focused on a recipe that she did not stop to realize that this was not at all the type of food her guests would need or appreciate. She would have her guests in mind from the start. After all, the goal of a good cook is not simply a matter of a recipe or a certain dish. It is feeding and feasting people . People drive the sermon. People are the reason God has given us the message in the biblical text. The biblical text leads the preacher to what the people need to hear from God. But the biblical text is only a means . The goal is people—to bring them somewhere that God wants them to go. To enlighten them, change them, help them, console them, correct them, train them to worship and serve God. People-oriented preaching comes from a God-centred, loving interest in them . Text-oriented preaching may simply come from the preacher’s love for preaching, for exegesis or for theology. A physician may be fascinated by medical treatments. But the good physician’s real interest is not treatments but people whose suffering has called for those treatments. Just so, true preaching is about people. That brings me to a second, related thought. We are often told that in preparing a sermon the key is finding the main idea of the text. To consider this as the key is not a people-oriented point of view and does not produce good preaching. It produces preaching with lots of emphasis on ideas and little emphasis on application. The key to preparing a sermon is not to find the main idea of the text. It is to find the main goal of the text. Not ‘What does the biblical text mainly say?’ But rather ‘What does this text intend to mainly do for people?’ What does the text intend mainly to effect in the lives of people? What does this text aim to move the people to believe, to do, to become? Application! A. T. Pierson, i
articles.content_zh: 以下信件发表于"班纳杂志"2025年12月号. 它应一位读者的要求在这里出版,他觉得它很有帮助,希望它的律师也能得到他人的祝福。 也可以在"班纳·波德克特"上收听对这封信的读取. 亲爱的J-,在我们讨论申请布道后,我想,我将提出一些多年来我对这一问题的看法。 我想指出一些陷阱 你可能想记住 当你训练R. 我了解他们的唯一原因 就是自己花太多时间在他们身上 多年来,我一直以来都在自责自悔。 第一种想法是,太多时候(即使在一些关于布道的好书中),我们听到文字驱动布道. 这是半个事实。 一个潜在的危险 半真相。 我见过一个男人如此有意地公开他的文字(他做得非常好),他似乎没有注意到或关心房间里有三分之一的人在他完成布道之前就离开,因为他走了这么长一段时间,会议的最后一餐是用来应付当地火车时间的限制。 错误地注重案文及其解释会使我们忘记案文所要为的人。 一位挺身而出进行传道的传道者,在一周里,他90%的布道准备时间都集中在圣经文本上,但是他没有充分意识到实际的传道内容。 在他们所著的"沿着路"(Letrys A. A. Carson)和"约翰·伍德布里奇"(John Woodbridge)一书中这样写道: 传福音的宣讲之所以如此之多,实在是无趣而无关紧要的一个主要原因是,传道人花费了大量的不相称的准备时间来解剖和提纲,在思考"上帝之道"是怎样去伤口和愈合(使用"霍西"的语言)时却很少考虑. 1个 故传道以人为事. 意义在于上帝要对人们说 他们的生活 讲道的文字是上帝要对人们说的话。 所以布道的文字就像菜谱。 一个好厨师永远也不会把注意力集中在一个配方上,以至于她不禁意识到这根本不是客人需要或欣赏的食物类型. 她一开始就想着她的客人 毕竟,一个好厨师的目标不仅仅是一个菜谱或某种菜肴的问题. 它在给人们提供食物和盛宴。 人们驱使布道。 人们是上帝给我们圣经文本中的信息的原因。 圣经文本将传道人引向人们需要从上帝那里听到的. 但圣经文本只是一个手段。 目标是人们,把他们带到上帝要他们去的地方去。 为了启蒙他们,改变他们,帮助他们,安慰他们,矫正他们,训练他们去崇拜并服务于上帝. 以人为中心的布道来自以上帝为中心, 以文字为取向的传道可能只是来自传道者对传道、开教或神学的热爱。 医生可能因治疗而着迷。 但好医生的真正兴趣不是治疗,而是那些遭受痛苦需要治疗的人。 所以,真正的传道是关于人的。 这让我想到另一个相关的想法。 我们经常被告知,在准备布道时,关键在于找到案文的主要想法。 将此视为关键不是以人民为导向的观点,也不产生好传道. 它产生许多强调思想的布道,很少强调应用。 准备布道的关键不是找到文本的主要想法. 它是为了找到案文的主要目标。 而非"圣经主要说些什么?" 但更确切地说,“这个文本主要是为了什么?” 案文主要打算如何影响人们的生活? 这个文字的目的是要促使人们相信,去做,变成什么? 申请! A. T. 皮尔逊,i

articles.content: The following excerpt is from James Walker’s The Theology and Theologians of Scotland , which we have just typeset and republished in a clothbound edition. Walker is here responding to the criticism of Scottish Christianity which faults it for being too doctrinal: Then, again, I think the idea has taken possession of many in our day, that Scotch religion is a religion of speculative dogma, with little in it of the personal Christ. Now it seems to me there is a great deal said at present about Doctrine or Dogma which means nothing. How can you act in regard to or feel about a thing, save as you have some conception and some opinion concerning it? You must have some opinion about the person of Christ, if He is to be an element in your practical life. How can He act on you otherwise? And, therefore, as you are Trinitarian, or Arian, or Unitarian, or Humanitarian, or something else, so will be the effect on you. And, in fact, the man who abuses dogmas is as much a dealer in dogmas as his neighbours. What is it but a dogma—generally asserted, indeed, with a fierce and contemptuous fanaticism, and carried out with a remorseless logic—that there should be no dogmas? Like scepticism, this sort of thing kills itself. Say what men will, all action, all organization, all religious or irreligious fellowship, is based upon a Credo. In regard to many who bring the accusation most readily about Scottish doctrinalism, I assert that there are none more doctrinal than themselves. The Broad Churchman maintains the doctrine of the Divine Fatherhood; puts that doctrine into definite conception; argues on the basis of that doctrine to immense conclusions, which make illusive a large amount of the deepest and most powerful experiences of Christian history. The Unitarian maintains the doctrine of the Divine Unity, and evolves therefrom proposition after proposition, overthrowing, as he thinks, all the life-giving Christian beliefs. The real truth is that orthodoxy is chary of the speculative. Mystery is one of its fundamental ideas. The Theosophic 1 belongs far more to heterodox Alexandrianism than orthodox Augustinianism. I do not think that it can be affirmed of Calvin, that he was as supreme in the metaphysical or speculative as in all else. Certainly our Scottish theology is not in any proper sense a metaphysical system, though there has been often a cloud or a halo of metaphysics about it, but the product in the main of an honest study of the Bible and a practical religious experience. The doctrines which have been prominently taught among us, such as the atonement of Christ, justification, the new birth, the indwelling of the Holy Ghost, are not in any sense speculative human reasonings, but transcendent facts,—mysteries which, according to all experience, tell with prodigious power on the human soul, and take hold of the deepest convictions of the least philosophical and cultured. articles.content_zh: 以下摘录出自詹姆斯·沃克的"苏格兰神学与神学",我们刚刚对它进行打字并重新以布满的版本出版. 沃克在此回应苏格兰基督教的批评, 然后,我再说一遍,我认为这个想法在我们这个时代已经占有了许多人, 苏格兰宗教是一种投机教条的宗教, 很少包含个人的基督。 现在,在我看来,目前关于理论或道格玛的说法很多,这毫无意义。 除了你对某件事有某种概念和看法之外,你怎么能对某件事采取行动或感觉呢? 如果上帝要成为你实际生活中的一个要素,你一定对基督的人有些看法. 怎么会 他对你另当别论? 因此,既然你是三硝基亚人,或亚利安人,或统一人,或人道,或别的东西,那么,对你们的影响也会是这样。 事实上 虐待教条的人 和邻居一样是教条商人 除了一个教条外,什么是不应该有教条的? 教条一般是用一种激烈而可鄙的狂热主义来断言的,并且以毫无悔恨的逻辑来进行。 类似怀疑,这种东西会自杀。 说男人的意志,所有的行动,所有组织,所有宗教或非宗教的研究金,都是建立在克里多之上的. 对于许多最容易指控苏格兰教条主义的人,我断言,没有什么比他们自己更多的教条了。 Broad Churchman坚持了神之父的教义;将该教义置于明确的概念之中;基于该教义而论证了巨大的结论,这些结论使基督教历史上大量最深刻和最强大的经验变得虚幻。 统一主义者坚持"神通统一"的学说,并从中演化出在命题后的建议,推翻了他所想的,所有赋予生命的基督教信仰. 真正的事实是,正统性是投机性的魅力。 神秘主义是其基本思想之一. 相较于正统的奥古斯丁主义,"神话一"更属于异体的亚历山大主义. 我并不认为卡尔文能被证实 他在物理或推测方面 和所有其他方面一样至高无上 当然,我们的苏格兰神学在任何适当的意义上都不是一个元物理系统,尽管关于它经常有云或光环的元物理,但主要产物是对"圣经"进行诚实研究并实践宗教经验. 在我们中间受到突出教导的理论,如赎罪、辩护、新诞生、使圣灵安息等,从任何意义上讲,都不是推测人类的推理,而是超越的事实,根据所有的经验,这些神话以对人类灵魂的超乎寻常的力量加以说明,并信奉哲学和文化最低的信念。 沃克17和18世纪的苏格兰神学和神学家,詹姆斯价格28.00美元 原价:28.00美元 现价:25.20美元 " 在自己的部门里学习更多的加进纸板描述认可 " 。 – NICK NESTHAM Book Direct James Walker(1821–1891)属于能够掌握一个国家神学文献的这一稀有阶层。 这本珍贵的书里有水果... articles.title_zh: 与安息日相关的「良心案例」
articles.content: The following is an excerpt from Walter J. Chantry’s Call the Sabbath a Delight (pages 96–102). When some Christians come to believe that it is their duty to keep the Sabbath Day holy, they become very fearful lest they engage in the wrong activities on the Lord’s Day. Such apprehension often takes the form of wanting very specific answers from a minister or a counsellor. May I go bicycle-riding on Sunday? Is it all right to go jogging on the Lord’s Day? Should I purchase medicine for a child with a sore throat? It is as if the believer is collecting a large list of items, next to which he is writing ‘do’ or ‘don’t’. This sort of inquiry regarding explicit details of behaviour is, unfortunately, encouraged by a type of church leader who feeds his ego by promoting himself as a kind of ethical guru. Wishing to be the ideal elder or conscientious teacher, this ‘leader’ offers direction in minute particulars of living. His style of handling practical issues of living makes his people utterly dependent upon his counsel. His people become incapable of coping with decisions unless the ‘oracle of wisdom’ has decreed exact permission or prohibition. Momentarily, it may seem wonderfully good fortune to have such an involved counsellor giving precise directives, but in the end it makes dependent children of those who ask. At the head of this chapter is printed Paul’s prayer for the Philippians. He asked the Lord to increase his flock’s knowledge and depth of insight. These gifts he desired for them so that they would be able to discern what is best when confronted with any decision. It was never intended that God’s people be given exhaustively itemized delineation of what to do in every circumstance. He did not place elders in leadership so that they might dictate what specific course to follow in every particular. He does not give divine revelation as to which alternative to choose at a given moment. Our Lord has given us the great principles of his word. Also, he has sent the Holy Spirit to assist our understanding, so that, in any given set of alternatives requiring judgment, the individual saint will be exercised in spirit. Only by inner wrestlings will he increase in discernment of what is best. In Hebrews 5:14 we are told that ‘solid food is for the mature, for those who have their powers of discernment trained by constant practice to distinguish good from evil.’ It may seem comfortable to have a list to tick off without thought. However, the truth is that such practice atrophies the mind and heart. General principles from God’s word are adequate guidelines to equip a Christian, aided by the Holy Spirit, to face every eventuality. The Sabbath Day is to be kept in mind. It is to be devoted with joy to the worship and service of God. This day is special and is not to be cluttered with our work or with the employment of others, except so far as will serve in God’s worship, in man’s necessities, and in showing mercy to our fellow human beings. God’s word is a sufficient guide. All that is needed is for the individual Christian to exercise his personal discernment as to what is best. Thus he trains himself to distinguish good from evil. Included in this exercise is the necessity of becoming independent of others. The fear of man’s opinion regarding your application of these principles must not keep you from applying the principles before God. This is a freedom of conscience given us in Jesus Christ. It must not be surrendered to anyone. Being subject to our Lord and his word demands that we keep ourselves free from the tyranny of human opinion, even ‘expert’ opinion. Many of the particular questions men and women ask cannot be given a definite answer. More rests upon motive and intent than upon the outward acts we do on the Sabbath. ‘May I go bicycle-riding on Sunday?’ Because younger children are not equipped to discern their own heart motives or the application of general principles, parents must make some rules for their households.
articles.content_zh: 以下是Walter J. Chantry的《安息日称为欢乐》(第96-102页)的摘录。 当一些基督教徒相信安息日是他们的责任的时候,他们就非常害怕在主日从事不义的活动。 这种担心往往表现为希望部长或顾问作出非常具体的答复。 我可以星期天骑自行车吗? 在主节去慢跑可以吗? 我应该买药给喉咙痛的孩子吗? 似乎信徒正在收集一大堆物品, 不幸的是,这种关于明确行为细节的询问受到某种类型的教会领袖的鼓励,他们通过宣传自己是一种道德的教义来养活自己的自我。 希望成为理想的长辈或良心老师, 他处理生活的实际问题的风格使他的人民完全依赖他的律师。 除非`智慧之神'下达确切的许可或禁止令,否则他的人民将无法应付决定。 暂时来说,让这样一个参赞提供精确的指示似乎是极好的运气,但最后却使那些提出要求的人有受抚养的子女。 保罗为菲利浦人祈祷。 他要求上帝增加他的羊群的知识和洞察力。 他想要给他们这些礼物,以便他们在面对任何决定时能够辨别什么是最好的。 从来没有打算让上帝的子民在每一情况下都详细分门别类地划分应做什么。 他没有安排长辈担任领导职务,以便他们能够决定每一具体过程中应遵循的具体方针。 他没有透露在特定时刻可以选择哪种选择。 我们的主给了我们他所说的伟大原则。 另外,他还派遣了"圣灵"来协助我们的理解,这样,在任何一套需要判断的既定选择中,单个圣人将会在精神上行使. 只有通过内在的摔跤,他才能提高辨别什么是最好的。 在希伯来语:5:14中,我们被告知,`坚固的食物是给成熟的人的,对于那些有辨识能力的人来说,他们通过不断的练习来区分善与恶。 有一份清单可以不经思考地删除,这似乎很舒服。 然而,实际情况是,这种做法会损害心灵和心灵。 从上帝的言语来看,一般原则是适当的准则,可以使一个基督教徒在圣灵的帮助下面对每一次事件。 安息日要记住。 其能以欢喜而奉献于神通之所礼拜及事. 这一天是特别的,我们的工作或他人的工作不会受到干扰,除非在上帝的崇拜中、在人类的必需品中和在对我们的人类同胞表示怜悯中服务。 真主的话足为引导。 需要的只是基督徒个人对什么是最好的个人认识。 于是他训练自己 以区分善与恶。 这项工作包括必须独立于他人。 人类对于你应用这些原则的意见的恐惧,决不能妨碍你在上帝面前应用这些原则。 这是耶稣基督赋予我们的良心自由. 绝不能向任何人投降。 服从我们的主及其言辞,要求我们远离人类观点的暴政,甚至 " 专家 " 观点。 男人和女人提出的许多具体问题不能得到明确的答案。 更多的取决于动机和意图,而不是我们安息日的外在行动。 我星期天可以骑自行车吗? 由于年幼儿童没有能力辨别自己的心脏动机或适用一般原则,父母必须为家庭制定一些规则。

articles.summary_zh: 我们都需要对上帝对所有众生和事件的主权统治有更大的敏感性。亚历山大·卡森（ Alexander Carson ）的研究《圣经所体现的天意的历史》（ The History of Providence as Manifested in Scripture ）可以帮助我们培养这种敏感性。以下是耶利米书第14章中他对犹大饥荒主题的评论：由于饥荒的存在， […]犹大的饥荒后：上帝的普罗维登斯显示首先出现在美国真理的旗帜上。
articles.title_zh: 犹大饥荒：神的普罗维登斯显现
articles.content: We all need a greater sensitivity to God’s sovereign rule over all beings and events. Alexander Carson’s study, The History of Providence as Manifested in Scripture can help train us in such sensitivity. Here are his comments on the subject of famine in Judah from Jeremiah 14: FOR the existence of plenty as of famine, the wisdom of this world looks no higher than to what are called second causes. God, it is considered, is no farther concerned in these matters than as the author of certain general laws. He has set the machine a-going, and it continues to work by its own construction, without any regulation of a superintending hand. Climate, soil, cultivation, need, it is confessed, favourable seasons, but any divine direction of weather is supposed to be unnecessary. Timely rain—or the want of it, is a matter below the attention of the Ruler of the world. The blight and the mildew, the wet and the caterpillar, are enemies with which the farmer is to struggle; but they are never considered as armies of devastation sent into the fields by a righteous Providence. The history of the Old Testament gives us a key to Providence in the production of famine or of plenty. God regulates the supplies of the children of men as exactly as if each individual of the human race had his rations assigned him by the angels of heaven every rising sun: ‘The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning the dearth. Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground; and the cry of Jerusalem is gone up. And their nobles have sent their little ones to the waters: they came to the pits, and found no water; they returned with their vessels empty: they were ashamed and confounded, and covered their heads. Because the ground is chapt, for there was no rain in the earth, the ploughmen were ashamed, they covered their heads. Yea, the hind also calved in the field, and forsook it, because there was no grass. And the wild asses did stand in the high places, they snuffed up the wind like dragons; their eyes did fail, because there was no grass. O Lord, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name’s sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against thee.’—Jer. 14:1–7. As in creation and in Providence, so in redemption, God hides himself in the midst of a blaze of light. In all his works he reveals himself, yet the enmity of the human heart will not allow men to see him. And what is most strange, the savage sees a divine hand in the works of Providence; it is unseen and denied by philosophical wisdom. The illiterate peasant hears God in his voice of thunder and storms, and acknowledges divine wrath in pestilence, sword, and famine. But the philosopher perceives nothing in all these but the course of nature. The wisdom of man makes itself ignorant of what the very beasts seem to feel. articles.content_zh: 我们都需要更加关注上帝对所有生命和事件的主权统治。 Alexander Carson的研究, 《普罗维登斯的历史》, 以下是他从耶利米14号对犹大饥荒主题的评论: 对于饥荒时存在的富足,这个世界的智慧看起来并不比所谓的"第二原因"更高. 据认为,与某些一般法律的制定者相比,上帝在这些事务上没有更多的关切。 他把机器设为正常运行,它继续按自己的构造运作,没有任何管制的上司手. 气候,土壤,种植,需要,是承认的,有利的季节,但是任何神圣的天气方向都应该是不必要的. 及时降雨——或者说,这是世界统治者不关心的问题。 荒凉和温和的、湿润的和毛毛的,是农民要与之斗争的敌人;但他们从未被视为正义的普罗维登斯派入田地的毁灭军队。 "旧约"的历史为我们提供了普罗维登斯产生饥荒或富饶的关键. 真主为世人的给养而加以管理,犹如每个人的给养,每逢太阳升起,就奉天天神所赐给每个人一样。 犹大哀悼而其中的城门枯萎;他们已变成黑色的;耶路撒冷的呼声已升起。 其贵人又将小人送入水中去:来入坑中去,又无取出水来;又以器物入空而回;自惭而自愧,自蒙而出. 因为地是分明的,因为地上没有下雨,犁地人感到羞愧,就把头盖了起来. 有之,后人又以地为牛,而弃之,因有草而去. 野驴们的确站在高处,他们像龙一样把风扑倒;他们的眼睛确实衰败了,因为没有草. 主啊!我们的罪过虽能证明我们的罪过,但求你为你的名字而行之;我们的背负是多的;我们确已犯罪了。 与创造和普罗维登斯一样,在救赎中,上帝将自己隐藏在一束光芒中. 在他的所有作品中,他都暴露了自己,然而人心的敌意却不允许人见到他. 最奇怪的是,野蛮人看到普罗维登斯的作品中有神之手;它是看不见的,被哲学智慧所否定. 文盲农民在雷和风暴中听到上帝的声音,在瘟疫、剑和饥荒中承认神圣的愤怒。 但是哲学家在所有这些事物中,除了自然的走向,什么也看不出来. 人类的智慧使自己对野兽的感受一无所知. 更多信息:卡森所著"普罗维登斯的历史"(The History of Providence As Expressed in Books by Carson, Alexander price from: $ 13.50 学习更多选择选项描述) 基督教徒最感兴趣的话题。 以天经为阅读者,并举出真主赐予信士们的慰藉。 264pp. Featured Photo(当作品在社交媒体上分享时可以看见),

articles.title_zh: 让苦涩的东西变甜的上帝
articles.content: The Israelites had just walked between the walls of the water of the Red Sea and watched as the Lord washed away the whole Egyptian army. They sang a song of triumph on the far shore of the sea, rejoicing in the fear that had fallen on the surrounding nations (Ex. 15:14-16) and looking forward to taking possession of the Promised Land in the near future (Ex. 15:17). But within three days they raised a very different kind of sound—a chorus of grumbling against Moses because there was no water to drink at Marah (Ex. 15:22-26). I wonder what they expected would happen after the Red Sea. A straight, unhindered journey to the land flowing with milk and honey? Instead the first thing the Lord does is to lead his people to the undrinkable water of Marah. There is no question that the Lord is the one who led them there—it is easy enough to take a wrong turn when you are following Google Maps, but not when you are following a towering pillar of cloud or fire! So why did God lead Israel to Marah? Is it because he is sadistic and cruel and takes delight in watching his people suffer dehydration and fear? Is it because he is really bad at geography? Of course not! In fact we’re told why he brought Israel to Marah in Ex. 15:25: There the Lord tested them. In fact, the whole wilderness is a place of testing. That’s the significance of the wilderness—it’s a hard place. Deuteronomy 8:15 calls it ‘the vast and dreadful wilderness, that thirsty and waterless land, with its venomous snakes and scorpions.’ God is training his infant son to trust him—and training is always painful. There are no short cuts, whether in the physical training of our bodies to make them stronger and faster, or in the mental training of our minds to increase our knowledge and understanding, or in the spiritual training of our souls to grow in godliness. Learning to trust God is not something we can do lounging on the sofa. It means being put into situations that are stressful, confusing, messy and complicated, when we don’t understand what is going on or see any answers. Anyone can trust God when things are easy; the real test is if you will trust God when things are tough. Israel’s failure Marah was Israel’s first test and they failed. They have been travelling for three days and haven’t found any water. Supplies are running low. Perhaps as they saw the waters of Marah in the distance they finished up their last reserves: ‘It’ll be OK—we can refill very soon!’ Imagine the relief and joy as the first to reach Marah fall down and scoop the water to their mouths. And imagine them spitting it out as they discover it is foul and undrinkable. They’re not just disappointed—they’re horrified . Panic seizes them. ‘What shall we drink?’ (v. 24) This is not like someone in a restaurant complaining that their steak is a bit on the tough side or that the soup is a tad cold. They are exhausted and dehydrated and they can’t see any way of getting water. Suddenly life is hanging by a thread. There is nothing unreasonable about their concern. That is not why they fail the test. They fail the test because of their attitude. They grumble: the word means ‘hostile complaining, verbal attacks of dissatisfied people.’ Why do they grumble? There are at least two reasons: Faithlessness . They do not trust God. They don’t trust his power (that he can take care of them) or his goodness (that he wants to take care of them). They should have gone to the Lord with their needs, humbly asking him to provide what they needed. And this lack of faith was due to… Forgetfulness . This is the diagnosis of Psalm 78:40ff: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and grieved him in the desert! … They did not remember his power or the day when he redeemed them from the foe , 43 when he performed his signs in Egypt and his marvels in the fields of Zoan. The people had such short memories! It has only been three days since they walked through the Red Sea! It has been just a few weeks since they witn
articles.content_zh: 以色列人刚刚走入了红海的水墙之间,看着上帝冲走整个埃及军队。 他们在远海岸上唱了一首"胜利之歌",欣喜地感受到了降临于周边民族的恐惧(Ex. 15:14-16)并期待着在不久的将来占有所承诺之地(Ex. 15:17). 但他们在三日内,举出一种非常不同的声音,一种对穆萨抱怨的合唱,因为在马拉没有水可饮(前15:22-26). 不知道红海之后他们会怎样 直走无阻地去 充满牛奶和蜂蜜的土地? 取而代之的是,主所行之事,是引其民入于马拉所出不可饮之水也. 毫无疑问,主是带领他们到那里去的——当你遵循Google地图时,很容易错转,但当你遵循高耸起的云柱或火柱时,就不是了! 那么为什么上帝带领以色列找到马拉? 是不是因为他是虐待狂和残忍的,在看着他的人民遭受脱水和恐惧时感到愉快? 是不是因为他在地理上很不好? 当然不是! 事实上我们被告知他为何在前15:25将以色列带到马拉:上帝在那里测试过他们。 事实上,整个荒地都是试验地. 这是荒野的意义, 8: 15 脱胎手术称之为:"大而可怕的荒野, 渴而无水之地, 有毒蛇和蝎子. 真主正在训练他的儿子,以便他信任他。训练确是痛苦的。 无论是身体锻炼,使其更强而更快,还是心灵修炼,以增进我们的知识和理解,或是心灵修炼,以在教化中成长,都没有任何短短的削减. 学会相信上帝不是我们能在沙发上做的事 这表示当我们不明白发生了什么情况或看到答案时, 当事情变得容易的时候,任何人都可以信任真主;真正的考验是,如果事情变得艰难的时候,你们要信任真主的话。 以色列的失败马拉是以色列的第一个考验, 他们已经旅行了三天, 补给不足。 也许当他们看到马拉的海水, 想象一下,解脱和欢乐是第一个到达马拉的人倒下,把水灌入口中. 想象一下他们发现它肮脏而不可饮用时就吐出它. 他们不仅失望, 恐慌抓住他们。 我们喝什么? (v.24) 这不像餐馆里有人抱怨 他们的牛排有点硬 或者汤有点冷 他们已经精疲力竭并脱水, 突然间,生命被一丝一缕地挂起 他们的关切没有什么不合理的。 这并不是他们失败的原因。 他们因为态度而未能通过测试. 他们抱怨道:这个词的意思是“敌意抱怨, 他们为什么抱怨? 至少有两个原因:失信。 他们不相信上帝。 他们不相信他的能力(他能照顾他们)或善良(他想照顾他们), 他们应该带着自己的需要去主那里,谦卑地要求他提供他们需要的东西. 缺乏信心是因为... 这就是对"诗经"78:40ff的诊断:他们在荒野中频繁地反抗他,在沙漠中为他悲伤!...... 他们不记得他的威力,也不记得他从敌人手中赎回他们的那一天,43岁时他在埃及行过他的迹象,他在Zoan地上行过他的奇事。 人们记忆很短! 他们从红海走过才三天! 几周前他们才开始

articles.summary_zh: 费丝·库克（ Faith Cook ）的《麻烦之旅》（ Troubled Journey ）讲述了她作为OMF中国传教士的女儿的早期经历。为了表彰父母的信仰、勇气和自我牺牲，她还富有同情心地揭示了与父母长期分离所带来的家庭剥夺。下面的摘录是该书的第11章，其中[…]邮政父母：传教士儿童的经历首先出现在美国真理旗帜上。
articles.title_zh: 邮政父母：传教士儿童的经历
articles.content: Faith Cook’s Troubled Journey narrates her early experiences as the daughter of OMF missionaries to China. Honouring the faith, courage, and self-sacrifice of her parents, she also shines a compassionate light on the family deprivations brought about by long periods of separation from them. The excerpt below is Chapter 11 of the book in question, which cover Faith’s childhood between the ages of fourteen and eighteen. A passage on the P & O Carthage was booked for Stanley and Norah [Faith’s parents—Ed.] in early January 1952, only eight months after our family had first arrived back from China. It was a subdued Christmas we spent together that year, the last for some years to come. Frantic packing followed, purchasing school uniform and preparing for the long outward journey back to the Far East, this time by sea. A round of speaking engagements filled the days for my parents and seemingly eased the ache of the forthcoming separation. As the day of parting drew ever nearer, I noticed a new tenderness in their attitude towards me – a tenderness that only added to my distress. And at last came the day of departure. It would be four years before we would see them again. Photographs were taken on the steps of the mission headquarters, as all joined to wish the departing missionaries well. Norah’s expression told a story, as did fifteen-year-old Christopher’s forced smile, for in reality, the boy’s spirit was at breaking point. On we went to the station where our parents would board a train to Southampton. A large contingent of missionary personnel followed, for this departure was highly significant for the entire future of the mission, urgently seeking a new role for its operations now the door to China was closed. I found myself thrust to the back of the crowd as the train slowly moved off. Suddenly one more thoughtful friend spotted the irony of the situation and pushed me to the front to catch the last glimpse of my parents as they stood waving at the window of the train, my mother looking tense and tearful, and my father strained. Back at the mission home once more, we were at a loose end. No guardian had yet been appointed to care for us, although one or two kindly adults helped out if I asked for assistance. The Spring term would soon begin and I was glad. Some of my new clothes were too long and needed altering, and I discovered with alarm that the shoe repairer considered my school shoes beyond his skills to patch up. Never handy with a needle, I tried my best to turn up the hems myself. At last the third week of January arrived and I was on the train back to my well-loved school – a place I now regarded as home. Although soon immersed once more in all the trivia of boarding school life, I found time each week to write a letter to my parents. The first few letters were addressed to ports en route for Malaysia where the P & O Carthage would call: Aden, Penang and then to Singapore to await their arrival. Stanley and Norah treasured these schoolgirl epistles, storing them all up, until at last my father would present his married daughter with a shoe box crammed with letters dating from January 1952 until the time that he and my mother finally retired from missionary service in Malaysia more than twenty years later. These letters form a unique commentary on the development of a postal relationship with my parents that would form the bedrock of my security and development from a young teenager to womanhood and beyond. Faithfully my parents replied to each letter, commenting on my progress, chiding when they could sense my behaviour was becoming erratic, and offering advice as well as they were able. Not long after arriving back at the mission headquarters in London at the end of the spring school term, I discovered that a middle-aged couple had been appointed as guardians for the children of the missionaries: Louis and Nancy Gaussen. Understanding and kindly, they were well-suited to care for the children. ‘Mr and Mrs Gaussen
articles.content_zh: Faith Cook的"麻烦之旅"讲述了她作为OMF传教士去中国的女儿的早期经历. 她以对父母的信仰、勇气和自我牺牲的敬意,也为长期与父母分离所带来的家庭贫困而发出同情之光。 下面的节录是该书第11章,其中涵盖了费斯14至18岁的童年. 1952年1月初,我们一家刚从中国回来才八个月,为斯坦利和诺拉(Faith的父母——Ed.)预订了P & O迦太基号上的一段。 那年是我们一起度过的圣诞 几年来的最后一天 紧随其后的弗朗克包装,购买了校服并准备了远东的漫长出行旅程,这次是海上出行. 一轮的演讲为我父母提供了时间,似乎缓解了即将到来的分居的痛苦。 随着离别日的临近,我注意到他们对我的态度出现了新的温柔,这种温柔只会使我更加痛苦。 终于到了出发之日 四年后我们才能再见到他们 对特派团总部的步骤进行了拍照,因为所有人都希望离开的传教士们一切顺利。 Norah的言论讲述了一个故事,15岁的Christopher被迫微笑也讲述了一个故事,因为实际上,这名男孩的精神正在崩溃。 我们去了车站 在那里,我们的父母 会登上火车到南安普顿。 随即派出了大批传教人员,因为这次出走对传教团的整个未来都具有重大意义,因此紧急寻求为传教团的行动起新的作用,现在中国的大门已经关闭了。 我发现自己被推倒 在人群的后部 当火车慢慢地离开。 突然又有一位深思熟虑的朋友发现情况具有讽刺意味,把我推到前面,以抓住我父母站在火车窗前挥手的最后一眼,我母亲看起来紧张而泪流满面,而我父亲也感到紧张. 回到了任务之家, 我们处在一个松散的结局。 目前还没有指定监护人来照顾我们,不过,如果我想得到帮助,一两个成年人会帮助我们。 春季学期即将开始 我很高兴 一些我的新衣服太长,需要更换,我惊恐地发现,修鞋者认为我的校鞋超出了他的能力来补补补. 我从不用针指手画脚,我尽力自己把螺丝弄大 终于在一月的第三个星期抵达, 我坐上火车回到我深爱的学校, 虽然我很快再次沉浸在寄宿学校生活的三难之中,但我发现每周都有时间写信给我的父母。 最初的几封信是寄给前往马来西亚的港口,P&O迦太基会称这些港口为:亚丁,槟城,再到新加坡等他们到达. 斯坦利和诺拉珍藏了这些女学生的表皮, 把它们全部储存起来, 直到最后我父亲会向他的已婚女儿展示一个鞋盒, 里面塞有1952年1月的信件, 直到他和我妈妈20多年后终于从马来西亚的传教士退休。 这些信件构成了关于与我父母发展邮政关系的独特评论,这将构成我从青少年到妇女时代及以后的安全和发展的基石。 诚然,我的父母每一封信都回信,评论我的进展,当他们能感觉到我的行为变得不规则时,他们就会发号施令,并尽可能地提供建议。 在春季学期结束回到伦敦的使团总部不久后,我发现一对中年夫妇被指定为传教士子女监护人:路易和南希·高森. 理解和友善,他们很适合照顾孩子。 高森夫妇

articles.summary_zh: 六个帖子中的第四个帖子包含了阿尔伯特· N ·马丁（ Albert N. Martin ）在1984年旗帜青年大会（ Banner Youth Conference ）上给出的教学内容，展示了基督教生活的基本圣经神学。在基督徒的生活中，没有承诺或命令的危机经历是必不可少的元素。一些关于基督徒生活的教导断言， […]《基督徒生活中没有必要的危机经历》一文首先出现在《美国真理旗帜》上。
articles.title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有必要的危机经历
articles.content: The fourth of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. There is no crisis experience promised or commanded as an essential element in living the Christian life. Some teaching on the Christian life asserts that only a low level of Christian experience can be realized by the person who has not had a crisis experience subsequent to regeneration, or at least subsequent to conversion and to the beginning of conscious Christian experience. Furthermore, it is asserted that the crisis experience is both commanded and promised by God as the entrance into a qualitatively new dimension or level of spiritual experience, reality and power. Throughout the history of the Christian church there have been many different strands of this crisis teaching. There is what we might call ‘classic Wesleyan perfectionism,’ which concentrated particularly upon sanctification and spoke of a baptism of purifying fire, or of coming into a state of perfect love. It concentrated not so much on power for service or upon inward feelings, but on a crisis experience in which the power of indwelling sin was to all intents and purposes negated. I have read enough of classic Wesleyan theology to know that there are different opinions as to what John Wesley himself taught on the subject. But in a general descriptive manner this, I believe, is an accurate representation of old-style classic Wesleyan perfectionism. Then, too, there is ‘the old Pentecostalism’ in which the emphasis was upon a baptism in the Holy Spirit, generally subsequent to conversion, and invariably manifested by speaking in tongues: the way you knew that you had this baptism of power was that, when it came to you, you spoke in tongues. The primary focus in old classic Pentecostalism was the matter of power for service. Thirdly, there is the modern ‘charismatic movement.’ Like classic Pentecostalism, its teachers use many of the same passages in the Book of Acts to support their theory of this necessary crisis. So they emphasize that in most cases—although there are different schools among modern charismatics—it will be manifested by the speaking in tongues. Some are content to believe you have ‘got it’ if you have a season of holy laughter. Others, however, say that you have not spoken in tongues because you have some psychological hold-ups, and if these can be removed the tongues are there. You just have not given them utterance. Here the emphasis is not so much on a baptism of purifying fire (as in the case of old classic Wesleyan perfectionism), or the baptism of power (as in the case of old classic Pentecostalism), but more upon a baptism of joyful praise-filled experience. I have been speaking of generalities, but I believe they are accurate. Fourthly, there are the various forms of ‘higher life’ teaching. What they have in common is this: you are simply converted, simply united to Christ, simply regenerated, and then you come to a crisis of surrender and faith, in which ‘you let go and let God’ and appropriate the indwelling life of Christ. The common denominator is that it is a crisis without any external manifestation of tongues or holy laughter or shouting or jumping, but the end result will be new power to live a holy life—the emphasis falls upon the ability to be more efficient in the path of holiness. Fifthly, there is a kind of teaching which has both old and modern proponents. It focuses on assurance, and has been expressed in terms of the biblical language of a ‘sealing of the Holy Spirit.’ Some of the Puritans—Thomas Goodwin, for example—taught this. There have been certain preachers in our own day who have believed this very strongly and emphasized it repeatedly. The basic concern in this teaching is that, subsequent to regeneration and conversion, there is a crisis experience in which the believer enters into a qualitatively new dimension of assurance by
articles.content_zh: 阿尔伯特·N·马丁在1984年班纳青年会议上发表的包含教学内容的六篇文章中的第四篇,介绍了基督教生活的基本圣经神学. 没有任何危机经历作为过上基督教生活的一项基本要素得到承诺或接受。 一些关于基督教生活的教义主张,在再生后,或至少是在皈依后,以及自觉的基督教经历开始后,没有危机经历的人,只有低水平的基督教经验才能实现. 此外,有人断言,危机经历既是上帝的旨意,也是上帝的允诺,是精神经历、现实和力量进入一个全新的层面或层次的。 在基督教会的历史上,这种危机教育有许多不同的内容。 我们可能称之为“经典的卫斯理完美主义 ” , 它不是把精力集中在服务或内在感情上,而是集中在一种危机经历上,在这种经历中,罪恶的威力是所有意图和目的所否定的。 我读了足够多的经典的卫斯理神学,知道对于约翰·卫斯理自己教授的这个主题,有不同的看法. 但从一般的描述方式来看,我认为,这是对老式经典的卫斯理主义的准确表述. 也存在“五旬节派”的旧现象, 重点是圣灵中的洗礼, 通常是在皈依之后, 古老的经典五旬节主义的主要焦点是服务的权力问题. 第三,有现代`魅力运动'。 和经典的五旬节主义一样,它的老师们也用"行动书"中的许多同名段落来支持他们对这个必要危机的理论. 所以他们强调,在多数情况下,尽管现代魅力中存在着不同的学校,但用舌头说话将表明这一点。 如果你有一个圣笑的季节, 然而,其他人说,你没有说出舌头,因为你有一些心理障碍,如果这些障碍可以取出,舌头就在那里。 你只是没说 这里强调的不是净化火的洗礼(如旧经典的卫斯理完美主义),也不是权力的洗礼(如旧经典的五旬节主义),而是更强调充满欢乐的赞美经验的洗礼. 我一直在谈论泛泛而谈,但我认为它们是正确的。 第四,有各种形式的 " 更高的生活 " 教学。 他们的共同点是:你们只是皈依正教,只是与基督联合,只是再生,然后你们遭遇了投降和信仰的危机,你们在危机中“放手,放任真主出征”,而顺从基督永生。 共同的分母是,这是一场没有外在表现出舌头或圣笑或叫喊或跳跃的危机,但最终结果将是新的力量来过上圣生活——强调在圣道上更有效率的能力. 第五,有一种教学既有老的也有现代的支持者。 它侧重于保证,并用圣经中的"封圣"来表述. 一些清教徒——例如托马斯·古德温——教授了这个。 在我们这一天里,有一些传道者非常强烈地相信并反复强调这一点。 该教学的基本关注是,在再生和转生之后,存在着一种危机经历,信仰者通过下列方式进入了保证的质的新层面:

articles.summary_zh: 伊恩· H ·穆雷（ Iain H. Murray ）的《艾米·卡迈克尔：灰烬之美》（ Amy Carmichael: Beauty for Ashes ）是对爱尔兰传教士前往印度的非凡生活的简短复述。接下来是该标题的第4章， “艰难的日子和黄金岁月。“如果说艾米·卡迈克尔的生活有任何模式的话，那就是令人耳目一新的时代，然后是考验的时代，令人兴奋的‘攀登’的时代[…]艾米·卡迈克尔的帖子：令人耳目一新的时代和考验的时代首先出现在真理美国的旗帜上。
articles.title_zh: 艾米·卡迈克尔：令人耳目一新的时代和审判的时代
articles.content: Iain H. Murray’s Amy Carmichael: Beauty for Ashes is a short retelling of the remarkable life of the Irish missionary to India. What follows is Chapter 4 of that title, ‘Hard Days and Golden Years.’ If there was any pattern to Amy Carmichael’s life it was of times of refreshing then of trials, of exhilarating ‘climbing’ then of walking in dark ravines. In part her explanation was that demonic activity follows the work of the Holy Spirit. As she quoted from George Bowen, When Christianity assumes an aggressive attitude the first result is a great exhibition of Satanic power. Satan’s power to be manifested must be assaulted. 1 Such an understanding does not come so readily to us who do not live, as she did, within sight of demon possession, or within hearing of tom-tom drums calling devotees to idols. Shortly before Walker 2 had left on his last mission, he had been sitting with Amy and others in deck chairs under the stars. ‘We had been talking’, she later wrote, of work and workers, and of those (to me) most wonderful women, who seemed perfectly self-reliant, needing no strong arm alongside. I remember how, suddenly startled at the bare thought of working alone, in the sense of all the burden of responsibility, I exclaimed that I never could do it. Mr Walker laughed. ‘Well, you don’t have to’, he said. 3 Amy was the weaker when her ‘strong arm’ died at the age of fifty-four. What she owed to Walker’s ‘courageous championship’ of the children’s work, ‘through its first very difficult years, no words can tell, nor can words tell how he is missed’. 4 At times, as she faced her loss, she would need to say to herself, ‘Don’t give up, don’t be afraid: go on.’ Prayer for ‘fortitude’ entered her life. There were unsympathetic neighbours who observed the work at Dohnavur who supposed that Amy would now be more vulnerable. One of these was a lawyer who, soon after Walker’s death, wrote with the demand that current work on the building of a wall around the compoundbe stopped, and that a half-built nursery should be pulled down. They were using ground, he claimed, to which they did not have legal title. ‘He had waited till Mr Walker’s death had left us, as he thought, defenceless, almost desolate, and sure to be easily cowed by threats of court trouble.’ The wall building had been prompted by the passage of a tiger through the compound at night; and the new nursery was necessitated by the growing numbers of children for whom Dohnavur had become home. Amy ignored the letter and heard nothing more of the threat. The Dohnavur family of seventy children and grown-ups in 1906, had doubled itself by this date, and the need of more helpers was pressing. Mrs Catherine Carmichael was never able to return. She died on July 14, 1913. A few weeks earlier a letter from her to Amy began with the words, ‘My own most precious earthly possession’. While Amy did not lament her mother’s death—for no Christian death was to be ‘lamented’—in the days ahead she needed to preach to herself, ‘I must remind myself to live in the joy of those gone, not grovel in the sense of my loss.’ Mrs Carmichael had been a constant supporter and representative for Dohnavur in Britain. She acted as the home secretary to whom gifts could be sent, and helped to make her daughter’s books more widely known. In 1912 those books had been noted by Queen Mary, wife of King George V, who expressed her thanks for them. While Amy was busy in 1913 writing Walker of Tinnevelly , there came the possibility of the loss of her closest female friend and helper, Ponnammal, who had been with her ever since, as a young widow, she had come to new life through Walker’s preaching. She now needed surgery for cancer and Amy went with her to a Salvation Army Hospital at Neyyoor for a period. In their absence from Dohnavur (forty-six miles away), and the absence of Mabel Wade who was on furlough, 70 of the children were ill. The need for more medical facilities at Dohnavur itself was evident. After much s
articles.content_zh: 伊恩·H·默里所著的"艾米·卡迈克尔:爱希斯的美人"(Amy Carmichael: Beautiful for Ashes)是爱尔兰传教士到印度的出众生的短篇回忆. 下面是该标题的第4章: " 艰难的日子和黄金年 " 。 如果Amy Carmichael的生活有任何规律的话, 她的部分解释是,妖魔活动遵循了圣灵的工作. 正如她从乔治·博文所引述的那样,当基督教采取侵略态度时,第一个结果就是撒旦力量的伟大展览. 必须攻击撒旦的力量。 1 对我们来说,这种理解并不像她那样活在恶魔拥有的目光下,或者在听到汤姆·通鼓呼唤献给偶像的人面前。 在行走者2号执行上个任务前不久,他一直和艾米等人坐在星空下的甲板椅上. 她后来写道:‘我们谈过了',内容是工作和工人,以及那些似乎完全自力更生、不需要任何坚强的手臂的妇女。 我记得,我突然对独自工作的赤裸裸的想法感到惊奇,因为我肩负着所有的责任,我感到惊叹,我永远做不到。 华克先生笑了 他说,你不必这么做。 3 Amy在54岁时死亡, 她对沃克的“勇敢的冠军”儿童工作所负的责任是,“在第一个非常困难的岁月里,言语无法分辨,言语也无法分辨他是如何被错过的”。 页:1 有时,当她面临损失时,她需要对自己说: " 不要放弃,不要害怕:继续吧。 " 祈求`宽恕'进入她的生活。 有不同情的邻居在多赫纳武尔观察作品,他们认为艾米现在会更加脆弱. 其中一个是一位律师,他在Walker死后不久写道,他要求停止目前在大院周围建造一堵墙的工作,应当拆除一个半建的托儿所。 他声称,他们使用了他们没有合法所有权的地盘。 他一直等待着沃克先生的死像他所想的那样离开我们,他手无寸铁,几乎是荒凉的,而且肯定很容易被法庭麻烦的威胁吓倒了。 墙上建筑的动因是一只老虎在夜间穿过大院;新的托儿所是因越来越多的儿童成为家而必需的。 艾米无视信件,没有听到更多的威胁. 1906年有70个孩子和成年人的多赫纳武尔家族,到这时已使自己翻了一番,迫切需要更多的帮助. 凯瑟琳·卡迈克尔夫人一直没能回来 她于1913年7月14日去世. 几周前,她给艾米的一封信开头写道,“我拥有自己最珍贵的地产”。 Amy没有为她母亲的死感到悲哀——因为没有一个基督徒的死是`在她需要为自己传道的几天里感到悲伤',`我必须提醒自己生活在那些死去的人的欢快中,而不是在我失去的意义上的忧郁'。 卡迈克尔夫人一直是英国多赫纳武尔的支持者和代表。 她担任家庭秘书,可以向她寄送礼物,并帮助使她女儿的书更广为人知。 1912年,这些书被乔治五世国王的妻子玛丽王后所注意到,玛丽王后对之表示感谢. 在1913年艾米忙于写作"Tinnevelly"的Walker(Walker of Tinnevelly)时,出现了失去她最亲密的女性朋友和助手Ponnammal(Ponnammal)的可能性,她从那时起就一直与她在一起,作为一个年轻的寡妇,她通过Walker的传道而来到了新的生活. 她现在需要手术治疗癌症,艾米和她一起去内约尔的救世军医院住了一段时间. 在他们离开多克纳武尔(相距四十六里外),而当时在放假的马贝尔·韦德(英语:Mabel Wade (film))不在的情况下,70个孩子生病了. Dohnavur本身显然需要更多的医疗设施。 这么多之后

articles.title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有摆脱紧张的途径
articles.content: The second of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. Principle 2: There is no escape from tension and conflict in living the Christian life. I do not say that the Christian life is all tension and all conflict. The kind of teaching I am attempting to expose as fallacious is as follows: At a conference a speaker takes a text out of context to which he attaches or from which he extracts a shibboleth – perhaps the shibboleth of Christ living his life through us, or the saving life of Christ, or the abiding life. Then the preacher, having expounded his theory of the Christian life, gives an appeal like this: ‘Child of God, are you weary of the tension of wrestling with your remaining sin? Are you tired of struggling in prayer? Are you weary of having to battle with impure thoughts and thoughts of envy and pride and jealousy? Are you tired of this incessant conflict?’ And every true Christian sits there with his fangs dripping, saying, ‘Oh God, you know I am tired, I would give anything to have one day, one day in which I did not have to battle with dullness of heart and distraction of mind and the seductions to sin that come from without and from within’. And the speaker then says ‘Ah, if you are tired of the tension, weary of the conflict, if you will but take these steps, then Christ will so live his life through you that it will be a life marked by the negation of tension and conflict. You will be so filled with the Spirit, so taken up in the Spirit, that tension and conflict for all intents and purposes will be a thing of the past as long as you maintain the posture of the abiding life. The moment you feel tension and conflict, it is because you slipped out of that life, back to your old ways.’ Now that is not a caricature, that is spelled out in page after page, book after book. Beware of the writings of Watchman Nee! Beware of some of the writings of such as Norman Grubb and Hannah Whithall Smith. Beware of these writings, because if you take them seriously they could drive you either into a world of unreality or into a world of scepticism. Now what proof do I offer from the word of God for that proposition? 1. Because of the reality of indwelling sin with its incessant and powerful actions upon us. Galatians 5:17: ‘The flesh is lusting against the Spirit and the Spirit against the flesh and these two are contrary the one to the other, so that you may not do the things that you would’. And Paul does not go on to say that there is a way to be utterly, totally delivered from that conscious­ness of tension and conflict. He does tell us that we need not be dominated by the flesh: ‘Walk in the Spirit and you shall not fulfil the lusts of the flesh’. articles.title: A Daring Suggestion for Netflix
articles.summary: Netflix appears to have fallen on hard times and I have some suggestions that I'd like to think would help it: cut the sex, nudity, and profanity, and gain back the viewers it's long been alienating. See Also A La Carte (April 28) A La Carte (October 22) Netflix’s Biggest Competition
articles.summary_zh: Netflix似乎陷入了困境，我提出了一些我认为会有所帮助的建议：减少性、裸露和亵渎，并赢回长期以来一直疏远的观众。另请参阅点菜（ 4月28日）点菜（ 10月22日） Netflix最大的比赛
articles.title_zh: 对Netflix的大胆建议
articles.content: Netflix appears to have fallen on hard times. The company’s co-CEOs recently announced they would be laying off around 1,000 employees, the deepest round of cuts in years. A day later, the chief content officer made a sudden exit and was immediately replaced. Just a week after that, the market responded unfavorably to Netflix’s Q3 results, causing the stock to drop sharply. There are many reasons for Netflix’s woes, not the least of which are increasingly heavy competition for viewers and its failure to land marquee shows—the kind of shows that convince people to maintain their subscription instead of canceling it in favor of Disney+, Prime Video, or one of the many other options. While there’s little doubt that Netflix will make it through this challenge, it may never regain the market dominance it once held. I have a daring suggestion for Netflix that I’d like to think could help it: make more shows that are clean and suitable for family viewing. To frame it another way, stop putting sex, nudity, and harsh profanity in nearly every show. There are many potential subscribers who are eager to be entertained, but not by shows they deem unsuitable or inappropriate. I’ll grant that Netflix has viewing data that probably shows its TV-MA content is especially popular, but data can only count the people who watched a show, not the ones who never pressed play in the first place. It’s also can’t tell whether the sex and swearing are essential to those who watch it, or whether they’d watch it even if it was much cleaner. Perhaps you could think about it this way: a single explicit sex scene in a series is unlikely to gain more viewers than it will lose. What I mean is that a content warning on IMDb or Common Sense Media stating that a show contains an explicit sex scene is enough for me and many others to skip that entire show. But I very much doubt the opposite is true—that a person will learn that there is no sex scene and decide to skip it on that basis. Some of us simply have no interest in viewing such things and will guard both ourselves and our families from seeing them. For those who don’t believe me, I’m sure I can put them in touch with a thousand people who will affirm what I’m saying. I am convinced there is a deep desire for shows and movies we can watch without cringing, without feeling violated, and without knowing we are watching what we consider not only unsuitable but immoral. It’s not that we’re prudes or opposed to sex—we’re all for it. It’s that we think sex and nudity are for private contexts , not public ones, and that some matters are to be kept between a husband and wife rather than displayed for all the world to see. Sex is so good and powerful that making it public diminishes it rather than elevates it, which means we deliberately avoid shows and movies that feature it. I would say something similar about language . Does a show need to drop hundreds of F-bombs across just a few hours of runtime? Does it need to constantly use the name of God as a swear word? It doesn’t need any of this. Once again, is it more likely that people will not watch shows unless they are profane, or that they will avoid them if they are? I think the answer is obvious: many more people will be driven away by swearing than drawn by it. If I had to offer one more piece of advice, it would be to stop tampering with beloved intellectual properties to make them consistent with modern sensibilities. Why not just make adaptations that are faithful to the vision of the original creators and let us deal with the differences between their context and today’s? Have the courage to let the stories stand on their own without inserting modern messaging. I strongly believe this would do more to provoke good thinking and spur important conversations. There’s no need to be so heavy-handed. To summarize, I think Netflix has been going about this all wrong and has been creating content that alienates an eager audience rather than drawing it in. So Netfl
articles.content_zh:
Netflix似乎陷入了困难时期. 公司联合首席执行官最近宣布将解雇约1000名员工,这是多年来最大幅度的削减。 一天后,首席内容官突然退出,立即被替换. 仅仅一周后,市场对Netflix的Q3结果反应不佳,导致股票急剧下降.

Netflix的悲哀有许多原因, 更是观众竞争日益激烈, 以及它未能登陆马奎节目,

Netflix虽然毫无疑问会渡过这个挑战,但可能永远无法恢复它曾经占据的市场支配地位。 我对Netflix有一个大胆的建议, 我想可以帮助它: 做更多干净、适合家庭观看的节目。 以另一种方式设定它,停止把性,裸体,以及苛刻的淫秽在几乎所有的节目中.

有许多潜在的订阅者渴望娱乐,但并不是通过他们认为不合适或不适当的展示。 我同意Netflix的收看数据可能显示其TV-MA内容特别受欢迎,

也无法分辨性与誓词对于观看者是否至关重要, 也许你可以这样想: 系列中一个单一的显性场景不太可能获得比它失去的更多的观众.

我的意思是,一个内容警告 互联网电影数据库(IMDb)上或Common Sense Media上 声明,一个节目包含一个明确的性场景,足够我和许多其他人跳过整个节目. 但我非常怀疑相反的情况是真实的——一个人会得知没有性场景,并据此决定跳过.

我们中有些人根本不关心看这些东西,并将保护我们自己和我们的家人不看到它们。 我敢肯定, 我可以和一千人联系,

我深信,人们非常渴望看一些节目和电影,而无需相信,无需感到被侵犯,也无需知道我们正在看我们认为不合适和不道德的东西。 我们不是故意或反对性爱,

我们觉得性与裸体是私人事务, 性是如此的美好和强大, 使它公开 减少它而不是提升它, 这意味着我们故意避免 节目和电影 我会说类似的东西的语言。

演出需要投下数百枚F炸弹吗? 难道它需要不断使用上帝之名作为誓词吗? 它不需要这些。 复次,是人不看秀,非有妄言,或避之不见,更何况?

我认为答案是显而易见的:更多的人会因为宣誓而被驱逐,而不是被它吸引。 如果我不得不再提一个建议,那就是停止篡改所爱的知识产权,使之符合现代的敏感性.

为何不只做忠实于原始创造者愿景的改编,让我们处理他们的背景与今天的不同? 要有勇气让这些故事独立存在,而不插入现代信息。 我坚信,这将更有助于激发良好的思维,刺激重要的对话。 也不必如此粗暴。

总结一下,我认为Netflix一直把事情搞错了,并创造出让热心的观众疏远的内容,而不是把它引进来. 所以说网友

articles.content: Good morning. The God of peace be with you today. Sales & Deals Some of today’s noteworthy Kindle deals include Al Mohler’s reader-friendly commentary on Hebrews, Julie Lowe’s guide to safeguarding our homes, and Marty Machowski’s family Christian devotional. Recommended Reading Discerning Between Godly and Worldly Grief. I think we all sometimes have to try to determine whether a person is displaying godly grief or worldly grief. Sam Crites offers three marks to help us make that determination. Harvest in Fearful Times. Here’s Melissa Edgington on trusting the Lord with an uncertain future. “I’ve seen various types of hand-wringing over the past week about governments and militaries and potential power grid disruptions. I watched one video, and then social media began showing me a different side of the internet, where cowboy hat-wearing men hand out ‘top secret insider knowledge’ from the front seat of their pickup trucks. In fact, I saw individuals from all sides of the political spectrum worrying out loud about how much water they should have on hand, how many weeks’ worth of prescriptions, how many canned goods and what types of communication devices would be best.” Can I Love My Enemies While Addressing Wrongs and Protecting Myself? “Practically speaking, how then should we demonstrate godly love for our enemies—the kind of love that redeems and restores instead of perpetuating sin and injustice? Let’s consider three implications of godly love that help answer this question…” Jeremy Oliver offers counsel on a sensitive matter. Is Missions Too Costly for Kids? I think a lot of people wonder whether life on the mission field could cost their children too much. Jessica B. writes from experience. “Are my children also called to this? As a mama missionary, I wonder about our fitness for the task when our family of eight clogs airport security and labors in language study and ministry like a well-meaning circus. Will my kids catch a deadly virus from the airport carpet? Will beans be lunch every day? How can we possibly replace years spent with grandparents and a vibrant children’s church? Will they become healthy adults when this calling cuts not only us but them?” How AI Brought a Mathematician to Ecclesiastes. This is an especially interesting article from Alan Noble. “Nobody—not even the most informed futurist—knows the effect AI will have on careers in the future. Some predict we’ll mostly adapt and find new vocations. Some predict we’ll all be living lives of leisure in a hyper-abundant economy while robots do all the labor. But if I had to guess, I’d predict that some people are going to have at least some of their valuable labor replaced by AI in the near future. And when that happens, people will have a crisis of meaning.” Don’t Stock the Pantry With Temptation. Darryl Dash warns against stocking the pantry with temptation. “We are used to preparing for almost everything. We prepare our clothes, our food, our vacations, and more. Paul is saying that whatever you do, do not prepare to sin. Instead, actively take steps to cut temptation out of your life. Deliberately arrange your life so that sinful desires are harder to satisfy. Avoid certain environments. Put a filter on your phone. Cancel that streaming service. Throw away those books. Cut out influences that tempt you toward sin.” Headlines Here are just a couple of interesting headlines from Christian news outlets. Christianity Today reports that Churches Face a Shortage of Worship Leaders . “A growing shortage of worship leaders has researchers, educators, and pastors wondering if it’s time to rethink music ministry recruitment and preparation.” Maybe some churches will ask whether they actually need a worship leader, since I have often wondered whether it’s a necessity for many of them. Across the pond, Evangelical Times considers the government’s proposal to ban conversion therapy and says Secular Press Wakes Up to the Danger of Labour’s Plan to Criminalise Conve

articles.content: The following is the substance of a pamphlet published by Archibald G. Brown, a student and then great ally of C. H. Spurgeon in the cause of the gospel in London. Brown here draws attention to a practice that was gaining ground in the churches of his day: that of holding ‘amusements’ of various kinds, which obscured, diverted from, and in some cases replaced the proper ministry of local churches. Brown was savagely attacked in the wake of the publication of the pamphlet, derided as ‘a kill-joy,’ ‘a morbid pietist,’ and ‘a sour bigot.’ His meaning, however, had been deliberately misrepresented. 1 Brown nowhere objects to all amusement per se , but amusement which masquerades as ministry, distracting the church and deceiving needy sinners. While the context in which Brown wrote may be different from ours, we need to hear his burden for a Church—and for Christians—to make a decisive break with the world and its practices. An Evil in the Camp of the Lord DIFFERENT days demand their own special testimony. The watchman who would be faithful to his Lord and the City of his God has need to carefully note the signs of the times and emphasize his witness accordingly. Con­cerning the testimony needed now, there can the little, if any, doubt. An evil is in the professed camp of the Lord—so gross, so brazen in its impudence—that the most short-sighted of spiritual men can hardly fail to notice it. During the past few years it has developed at an ab­normal rate, ever for evil. It has worked like leaven until now the whole lump ferments. Look which way you may, its presence makes itself manifest. There is little if any­thing, to choose between Church, Chapel, or Mission Hall. However they may differ in some respects, they bear a striking likeness in the posters that figure upon and dis­figure their notice boards. Amusement for the people i s the leading article advertised by each. If any of my readers doubt my statement, or think my utterance too sweeping, let them take a tour of inspection and study “the announce­ments for the week” at the doors of the sanctuaries of the neighbourhood; or let them read the religious advertise­ments in their local papers. I have done this again and again, until the hideous fact has been proved up to the hilt, that “amusement” is ousting the preaching of the gospel as the great attraction: “Concerts,” “Entertain­ments,” “Fancy Fairs,” “Smoking Conferences,” “Dramatic Performances,” are the words honoured with biggest type and most startling colours. The burden of the Lord is upon me in this matter The Concert is fast becoming as much a recognised part of church life as the Prayer Meeting, and is already, in most places, far better attended. “Providing recreation for the people” will soon be looked upon as a necessary part of Christian work and as binding upon the Church of God, as though it were a Divine command, unless some strong voices be raised which will make themselves heard. I do not presume to possess such a voice, but I do entertain the hope that I may awaken some louder echoes. Anyway, the burden of the Lord is upon me in this matter, and I leave it with Him to give my testimony ringing tone, or to let it die away in silence. I shall have delivered my soul in either case. Yet the conviction fills my mind that in all parts of the country there are faithful men and women who see the danger and deplore it and will endorse my witness and my warning. Gratifying the Flesh and Retaining a Comfortable Conscience It is only during the past few years that “amusement” has become a recognized weapon of our warfare and de­veloped into a mission. There has been a steady “down grade” in this respect. From “speaking out,” as the Puri­tans did, the Church has gradually toned down her testi­mony; then winked at and excused the frivolities of the day. Then she has tolerated them in her borders, and now she has adopted them and provided a home for them under the plea of “reaching the masses and getting the ear of the

以下是阿奇博尔德·G·布朗(Archibald G. Brown)出版的一本小册子的实质内容,他是一个学生,后来成为了C·H·斯普亨在伦敦福音书事业中的重要盟友. Brown提醒大家注意他当时的教会日益盛行的一种做法:举行各种 " 纪念会 " 的做法,这种做法模糊不清,转移了注意力,有时还取代了当地教会的适当部会。

Brown在小册子发表后遭到野蛮攻击, 然而,他的意思被蓄意歪曲。 1 布朗无处反对所有娱乐本身, 但娱乐伪装成牧师, 分散教会的注意力 欺骗需要的罪人。

虽然布朗写作的背景可能与我们不同,但我们需要听取他对于一个教会——以及基督徒——的责任,以便同世界及其做法决裂。 魔王营里的恶魔 要求他们自己作证

忠于他的主和他所崇拜的城市的守望者,必须仔细记取时代的迹象,并相应地强调他的见证. 在现在所需要的证词中,可以有一点怀疑。 主所宣示的营中,有恶行;主的营中,有恶行;主的营中,有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行;有恶行。

在过去几年里,它以异常的速度发展,永远是邪恶的。 直到现在,它一直工作着,就像离开一样。 看看你们可以走哪条路,它的存在就变得明显了。 教会、礼拜堂或传教堂之间几乎没有任何选择。

然而,它们在某些方面可能有所不同,它们在海报上带有惊人的相似性,这些海报上显示它们的通知板并毁容。 为人民提供娱乐 我是每篇广告的主要文章

如果我的读者怀疑我的发言,或者认为我的言论过于笼统,让他们巡视视察,在附近圣所门口研究“一周的公告”;或者让他们在当地报纸上阅读宗教广告。

在令人发指的事实被证实之前,我一再这样做,即“辱骂”正在驱使福音的传道成为伟大的取景:“关注”、“参与”、“盛会”、“吸烟会”、“戏剧表演”是用最出名和最令人惊叹的颜色表达的言论。

主的重担在我这里 音乐会正迅速成为教会生活中 公认的部分 与祈祷会一样 并且已经,在大多数地方,

“为人民提供娱乐”将很快被视为基督教工作的必要部分,对上帝的教会具有约束力,似乎这是神的命令,除非有人发出强烈的声音,让自己听到。 我并不认为拥有这种声音,但我确实希望能够唤起一些更响亮的回声。

无论如何,上帝的重任 由我负责这件事, 我留给他 让我的证词响亮的语气, 或者让它静静地死去。 无论哪种情况,我都会送出我的灵魂 然而,这一信念使我满怀信心,即全国各地都有忠实的男女看到这种危险并对此感到痛惜,并将赞同我的证人和我的警告。

修行并保持舒适的良知 直到过去几年,“暴行”才成为我们战争的公认武器并发展成一个特派团。 这方面的“级别”稳步下降。 正如普里坦人所做的那样,教会从“大声疾呼”开始,逐渐淡出她的遗言;然后轻视并原谅了今天的纷争。

然后,她在边境上容忍他们,现在她收养了他们,在“影响群众,让人民听到他们的声音”的恳求下,为他们提供了家园。
