articles.content: May the Lord be with you and bless you today, my friends. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a couple of Christmas devotionals, a Greg Koukl classic, and Seth Lewis’s Dream Small , among others. In case it’s of interest, Audible continues to offer a great deal—three months of service plus a $20 bonus for $0.99/month. You can unsubscribe at any time. Recommended Reading A Manifesto for Phone-Free Church. This article offers a lot to think about when it comes to the consequences of using our phones in church. “Distractions in worship will be with us always, but that does not mean we ought to go out into the highways and the hedges and invite as many distractions as possible. And here, we should note that there are good distractions in church—I am thinking of those babies that cry and fuss and laugh at all the wrong moments. Good distractions remind us that church is more than our personal ‘alone time’ with God. We are part of a family.” The Missing Piece in John Mark Comer’s Quiet Time. I think Matthew Bingham’s review of John Mark Comer’s book is bang on in both what it praises and what it criticizes. “Though Comer identifies as a Protestant, he relies on numerous quotations from ‘desert fathers and mothers,’ medieval mystics, and modern Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox theologians to justify his cafeteria approach to spirituality. As in his previous work, he engages with few heirs of the Reformation. Comer insists that Scripture is essential, but, for him, it doesn’t stand alone. Consistent with this non-Protestant mystical tradition, the book strongly emphasizes subjective, immediate communication from God apart from God’s inspired words in Scripture.” Free Chick-fil-A For a Year. Did you know that Midwestern Seminary is home to Spurgeon College, which is an undergraduate school that exists to equip students for the Kingdom? This November, they’re giving away a year’s supply of Chick-fil-A! Head over here to enter to win and discover other opportunities to grow deeper in Christ this month! (Sponsored) The Pull of Rome and the Promise of Grace. Chris Castaldo writes about those who are drawn to Rome. “A member of your small group confesses, seemingly out of the blue, that he’s been attending Mass. Next, you hear a deacon wonder aloud if we really needed to break with Rome. Then a family member announces that she has ‘crossed the Tiber,’ meaning she has converted to Roman Catholicism. Such conversations seem to be happening with greater frequency in Protestant circles. But why?” 4 Misconceptions About Spiritual Warfare. Costi Hinn outlines four fairly common misconceptions about spiritual warfare. “There is a short list of Christian beliefs that have as much mystery as spiritual warfare. While some things are really clear in the Bible regarding demons and demonic activity, there is a supernatural element to the unseen realm that humbles even the most educated theological student! At the same time, it seems that many people have a variety of opinions based on their experiences, which is not necessarily a negative thing, but it can lead to a lot of misconceptions.” Slouching Toward Narnia. Personally I’ve been enjoying reading all the different perspectives on the growing information we have about the forthcoming Narnia film(s). I think Nicholas McDonald’s article is one of the best so far. He explains his formula for a successful film adaptation (Faithfulness to Theme + Thoughtful Innovations = Great Film Adaptation) and tells whether he’s feeling hopeful as he considers The Magician’s Nephew in that way. Four Corrections to Make When You Feel Guilty About Your Giving. I think most people feel guilty about their giving from time to time. When that’s true of you, here are some ways you can correct the way you think and act. What I’m Enjoying Every week I ask the readers of this site to tell me what they are enjoying and, therefore, what they recommend to others. Sometimes I like to give my own perspective on it. A Retr

愿主与你同在,今天祝福你,我的朋友们. 销售与交易今日的Kindle交易包括几个圣诞奉献,一个是格雷格·克克(Greg Koukl)经典,以及赛斯·刘易斯的"梦想之小"等. 如果有兴趣,Audible继续提供大量服务——3个月服务,再加上0.99美元的20美元奖金。 随时可以取消订阅.

推荐阅读无电话教会宣言. 这篇文章对于在教堂使用我们的电话的后果,提供了很多思考的机会. “崇拜中的分裂将永远与我们同在,但这并不意味着我们应当走进高速公路和树篱并尽可能多地分散注意力。

在这里,我们应当注意到,教会中有一些良好的分心——我想到那些婴儿哭出大惊小怪并嘲笑所有错误的时刻。 良好分心提醒我们,教会不仅仅是我们与上帝的"单独时间"。 我们是家庭的一部分。” 约翰·马克·科默尔的"安静时间"中的"失踪的碎片".

我认为马修·宾汉姆对约翰·马克·科梅尔(John Mark Comer)书的评论, 无论是赞美还是批评, 都令人振奋。 “尽管科默确定自己是一位新教徒,但他依靠许多来自`沙漠之父和母亲'、中世纪神秘论以及现代罗马天主教和东方东正教神学家的引文来证明他对精神的食堂方法是合理的。

和他之前的作品一样,他与改革派的少数继承人交往. 但对于他来说, 这并非孤立无援。 这本书与这种非抗议性的神秘传统一致,除了《圣经》中上帝所启示的文字外,大力强调主观的、与上帝的直接沟通。 一年免费小鸡

你知道中西部神学院是斯普琴学院的所在地吗? 斯普琴学院是一所为王国培养学生的本科学校。 今年十一月, 头到这里进入赢 并发现其他机会 在基督这个月更深了! (赞助)罗马的拉动和恩典的承诺.

克里斯·卡斯塔多(Chris Castaldo)写道那些被引向罗马的人. “你们小团体的一名成员承认, 接下来,你听到一个执事 大声问我们是否真的需要 与罗马决裂。 她已经皈依了罗马天主教。

这种对话似乎在新教圈子里更加频繁地发生。 为什么?” Costi Hinn概述了对精神战争的四个相当普遍的错误认识。 “有一份基督教信仰的简短清单,其神秘之处与精神战一样多。

虽然《圣经》中有些关于恶魔和恶魔活动的内容是十分清楚的,但是在幽灵世界中却有一种超自然的元素,即使最受过教育的神学学生也是谦卑的!

同时,看来许多人根据自己的经历有各种观点,这不一定是负面的东西,但会导致许多误解". 向纳尼亚走去 我个人一直喜欢阅读关于纳尼亚电影的不断增长的信息,

articles.content: I regret to inform you, dear reader, that heaven tourism is back. The genre possibly never went away entirely, but it did at least disappear from the bestseller lists for several years. Sadly, it has returned in Gabe Poirot’s 18 Days in Heaven , which was one of the bestselling Christian books last month and even made its way to the New York Times list of bestsellers—a feat most authors can only dream of. Out of sheer magnanimity (and perhaps a morbid sense of curiosity), I read it so you don’t have to. 18 Days in Heaven Gabe Poirot Before I tell you what it’s all about, here’s a brief history of heaven tourism. Don Piper kicked off the genre in 2004 with 90 Minutes in Heaven , and it proved a surprise hit that quickly dominated the sales charts, eventually tallying upwards of 8 million copies sold. Todd Burpo’s Heaven Is for Real followed in 2010 with over 10 million copies sold. That same year brought Kevin and Alex Malarkey’s The Boy Who Came Back from Heaven , which sold more than a million copies before Alex recanted his story and the publisher pulled it. The genre went on to deliver many more heaven books and a handful of less-popular hell books like Bill Wiese’s 23 Minutes in Hell , though none ever reached the same heights as the first few—no pun intended. My contribution to the genre was little more than reviewing several of the books and coining the snarky phrase “heaven tourism,” which, much to my delight, soon caught on . The genre inevitably ran its course, but has now returned in Gabe Poirot’s 18 Days in Heaven: I Left My Body. I Met Jesus. What He Told Me Will Alter Your Eternity . Sadly, but not surprisingly, it is just as bad as its predecessors, mixing truth with errors and documented facts with spurious speculations until it is as confusing and unreliable as any of them. 18 Days in Heaven follows the standard pattern by beginning with an account of a terrible accident—in this case, a head injury that resulted from a skateboarding mishap. Poirot, a young evangelist with a sizable YouTube following, was rendered comatose and remained hovering between life and death for 18 days. But while his body was inert, his soul was transported to heaven, where it experienced heavenly wonders, not the least of which was spending time with Jesus. What did he see and experience there? Many things, of course, some of which he is able to describe and many of which he insists he cannot, either because God told him not to or because they defy description. What can he describe? Jesus’s eyes, in which “I saw all the colors that had ever existed or could exist, all in one. He was the deepest ocean of liquid love that had no end. A spectrum of intensity that only increased the longer I stared. His eyebrows, hair, jawline, arms, chest, heart, stature, ears, forehead, eyelashes, teeth, mouth, skin, and complexion all said the same thing: I love you, I love you, I love you.” He describes Jesus’s scars which “were like an ocean that had no floor,” and had the name “Gabriel” written immediately above them. He learned from them that Jesus has completely and eternally forgotten his sins so that he could no longer remember them even if he wanted to. He smelled Jesus and observed that his “fragrance wasn’t like the humidity of the Florida Everglades. No, this was something eternal—an everlasting fountain of fire, not just surrounding me but burning into me. Wrapping around me like a robe, like a living garment of pure, unending presence. It felt burning hot and freezing cold at the same time.” He heard Jesus say many words and noted that his “words were not just a separate entity that He ‘released.’ They were like the sharpest spears that went right into the core of my very being. But these spears were not separate from Him—they were Him.” Poirot even saw his own conception: “The light from Father God united with the earthly seed from my father and the egg of my mother in that moment, and I began my existence on earth. I was not born just on

不幸的是,它回到了Gabe Poirot的"天堂18天"中,这是上个月最畅销的基督教书籍之一,甚至走进了纽约时报畅销书榜,这是大多数作者只能梦想的功绩。 我读了这篇文章,

同年,凯文和亚历克丝·马拉克的"从天堂回来的男孩"(The Boy Who Came from Heaven)也带来了,后者在亚历克丝收回他的故事并被出版商拉出之前就售出超过一百万份. 虽然没有人能达到与前几本书相同的高度,

我对这个流派的贡献不过是回顾几本书, 但现在又回到了Gabe Poirot在天堂的18天:我离开了我的身体。 我遇见了耶稣。 他告诉我 Will 改变你的永恒

可悲但并不令人惊讶的是,它同其前身一样糟糕,把事实与错误相混淆,把有记录的事实同虚假的猜测相混淆,直到它同其中任何一个都一样令人困惑和不可靠。 18天的"天堂"遵循了标准模式,首先讲述了一起可怕的事故——在此情况下,由于滑板出事而造成头部受伤.

Poirot是一位年轻的福音传播者,他带着一个庞大的YouTube跟随,因此被昏迷并徘徊在生与死之间长达18天. 但虽然他的身体是惰性的,他的灵魂被运到了天堂,在那里它经历了天堂的奇事,其中最起碼是和耶稣一起度过. 他在那里看到了什么? 体验什么?

当然,许多事情,有些是他能够描述的,有些是他坚持不能描述的,要么是因为上帝告诉他不要描述,要么是因为他们藐视描述。 他能描述什么? 耶稣的眼睛,其中,“我看到了曾经存在或可能存在的所有颜色,都是一种颜色。 他是无尽的液体爱最深的海洋

他从他们那里得知,耶稣已经彻底地,永远地忘记了自己的罪过,这样即使他愿意也再也记不住了. 他闻到耶稣的气味并观察到他的"香气不像佛罗里达埃弗格拉德河的湿润. 不,这是永恒的东西, 一个永恒的火焰喷泉, 不仅包围着我,而且燃烧在我身上。

缠绕我就像长袍一样 像纯洁无尽的活衣 它同时感到被烧得发热而冷冻。” 他听到耶稣说出许多话,并指出他的"词不仅是一个他‘释放'的独立实体. 他们就像最锋利的长矛 直入我生命的核心

articles.content: Good morning. I’ve got A La Carte and a regretful book review for you today. Over the weekend you’ll find Saturday’s Weekend A La Carte plus Sunday’s Works & Wonders, which shares content that is just right for a Sunday morning. I hope you enjoy reading it all as much as I have enjoyed putting it together. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals are headlined by Joel Beeke’s A Radical, Comprehensive Call to Holiness . You may also be interested in a book about women who overcame a difficult past or a biography written for a younger audience. Recommended Reading Selfies Are Not the Self: Forming Embodied Youth in a Disembodied Age. This article from Harvest USA has some helpful insights about young people and their mobile devices. “Increasingly, research shows that teenagers know their technology is making them miserable. They don’t love their phones, but they hate missing out. They know the noise is making them sick, but they’re terrified of the silence. When teenagers are so thirsty for connection and validation that they’ll go to a well they know is poisoned just to get a drink, what an amazing opportunity we have as the church to offer something better, something truly beautiful. We don’t want our youth ministries to be known for what they lack. We want them to be known for their abundance.” Can’t You Just Love Everyone? Jeremy Walker addresses churches that think their calling is to “just love everyone.” “Why not just love one another? Why build walls, make distinctions, establish boundaries, and draw lines? Why confront sins? Why not welcome all equally? Can’t you just love everyone?” 4 Applications for the Order of Love—From the Home to the Ends of the Earth. Speaking of love, Alex Kocman addresses the necessity of rightly ordering our love. “Augustine’s idea of ordo amoris —the ‘order of love’—reflects the Scriptural pattern of directing our affections to first love God, then to love our families, and then to extend that love outward to others. This theme of ordered love has wide-ranging implications—from the home to the ends of the earth. But just as preaching without application is lifeless, so too is a study of love without practical exhortation. Here are four admonitions…” Effective Altruists and the Spreadsheet Gospel. Writing for TGC, Nathan Leamer addresses the effective altruism ideology that is so influential in Silicon Valley. “Over the past decade, an emergent secular philosophy has taken root in Silicon Valley. It now drives many conversations around politics and technology, particularly as its ideas shape how our society approaches artificial intelligence. Known as ‘effective altruism,’ this worldview is having a moment. The Economist recently called the philosophy ‘this century’s biggest idea’ and labeled the movement as ‘admirable, but dangerous.'” Your Thoughts Are Shaping Your Life. “Your thoughts are shaping your life.” That might sound like the kind of thing Joel Osteen or a New Age practitioner would say, but there is truth to it. “Our thought life matters more than we often realize. The conversations we replay in our minds, the offenses we revisit, and the fears we entertain can shape how we see our circumstances and respond to the people around us. I know how easily my thoughts can become consumed by something that has happened or something I fear might happen. Before long, I find myself responding to the present through the lens of thoughts I have been rehearsing.” Don’t Despise the Red Flags. Katie Laitkep writes to those who are dating, and to young women specifically, to warn them not to ignore or despise the red flags. “When we see signs marking a dangerous road, we respond immediately, knowing we need to find a different path. But when it comes to red flags in dating relationships, we don’t always view the warning signs as clearly.” Reviews I like to share the occasional reminder that it is tremendously helpful to authors if you post even brief reviews of their books at Amazon. articles.content: Welcome to Weekend A La Carte. I hope you find something here, whether a longform article, a reader recommendation, or something else entirely, that makes your weekend just a little bit better. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several newer and older books that are all worth at least thinking about. If you’re interested in doing some theological reading, Westminster Books is offering up to 57% off the three-volume set of Warfield’s works. Also, I haven’t reviewed it yet, but did want to briefly recommend the new graphic novel adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress . It seems to be priced just about equally at Westminster Books and Amazon (for me, at least). Recommended Reading Canada’s Maclean’s magazine has an interesting article about the Hutterites and their caution when it comes to modern technologies. The author, like so many of us, is alarmed by the ways technology overtakes our lives, and sees that the Hutterites may have a healthier relationship to it. Most of us—including me—are worried that we’ve all become desensitized to the manifold and multiplying ways technology is negatively affecting our lives. Social media has been blamed for rising rates of political polarization and radicalization, damaging young people’s ability to form relationships and eroding mental health. And we’re all trying to figure out what to do about it. Slick startups sell devices you tap with your phone to “brick” it (that is, blocking distracting social media, apps and internet access). There are apps to remove short-form videos from social media feeds. There are now social media bans in place for youth in Australia, in parts of Europe and Asia and, this June, proposed in Canada. Sales of dumbphones and flip phones have grown in the past few years. Even landlines are trendy again. But this is like pushing back the tide with a broom. For most of us, technology feels like a force of nature that will wash over us whether we want it to or not. The Hutterites are more optimistic. They think if they can keep their distance from the wider world, and adopt the right set of rules around technology, they can hold onto its positive features and simply seal out what they don’t like. Read: The Hutterites’ Guide to Technology. The New York Times was in touch with many Gen Zers and explains how their entry into the job market is much different from previous generations. I think it’s easy for those of us who are older to act as if Gen Z is lazy or otherwise not putting in much effort, but this article ought to give us some compassion. They described a process that is lonely, opaque and impersonal, in which it is hard to tell whether one is being rejected by a hiring manager or an A.I. screener. The problem is not just that hiring has slowed across the labor market, or that the specter of A.I. is threatening entry-level positions, they said. It was that they could not get a real, live human being to speak to them. Ever. About anything. The same language came up over and over in their responses: They felt as if they were throwing their applications into “the void.” Some of them opted for slightly different terminology — a “black hole” or an “abyss” — but they painted a similar picture of the application process as a swirling vortex where aspirations and cover letters vanish, unlikely to be retrieved. One part that jumped out to me was the person who insists on they/them pronouns. I would imagine that is a huge red flag for people in charge of hiring! Read: Searching for Jobs, Gen Z Feels Like It’s Staring Into ‘The Void’. The Verge has a lengthy article that describes the bizarre and heterodox gospel according to Peter Thiel. It’s a time of apocalyptic worldviews in Silicon Valley. The latest AI doom cycle is driven by effective altruism (EA), a philosophy that has lurked around the fringes for years but recently burst into the mainstream because its adherents are embedded across the AI industry, from Anthropic to newly appointed AI safety watchdog METR. articles.content: In my weekly Works & Wonders column, I combine a brief devotional with other interesting and uplifting bits and pieces I gleaned throughout the week. I hope you enjoy this week’s collection! It includes: His Will Will Be Done Photomicrography Come, Thou Fount (×3) The Brain-Injured Musical Genius Grain from an Attic Prepare Him Room (Live) 1. His Will Will Be Done To have power is to have ability and strength. This is true whether the power belongs to human beings or to God himself—to creatures or to the Creator. Of course, our power is derived from God’s, but his is inherent. We are accountable to God for the way we use our power, but God is accountable only to himself. Our power is always small and incomplete, but God’s is always unbounded and unlimited. To say we are powerful is to say we possess the ability to do some of the things we desire some of the time. But to say God is powerful is to say God always possesses within himself the means necessary to bring about whatsoever he wills—to execute all his plans, to execute them all the way to perfect completion, and to overcome any and all resistance. This guarantees that God’s will will be done, for as the psalmist says, “Our God is in the heavens; he does all that he pleases” (Psalm 115:3). The God we worship today is the God for whom this is true: Whatever his will resolves and however his wisdom directs, his power will accomplish. 2. Photomicrography Shall we look at the results of another photography competition? Why yes, we shall. This week it’s Nikon’s Photomicrography Competition . “What is photomicrography you ask” (other than a word that is almost impossible to type correctly the first time, or even the fourth, in my case)? It is taking photos of microscopic objects and, in that way, opening a view to a world that is otherwise far too small for us to see. I think you’ll enjoy browsing the winners, which include spiders, pens, neurons, and inkjet printers. 3. Come, Thou Fount (×3) I really enjoy The National Parks and their delightful, easy-to-listen-to folk-Americana music. It’s my understanding that they grew up Mormon but have spoken openly about leaving that faith, but I am not aware of them becoming Christian. I was surprised, then, to see they had released a version of “ Come, Thou Fount .” It’s quite a good one. I’m not sure what motivated them to record it, but perhaps it was the same thing that motivated Marcus Mumford of Mumford & Sons, who has also recorded and performed it several times—I assume it was just the sheer beauty of the song. Mumford was raised in a Christian home, though later left the faith. His version is also wonderful. Another favorite rendition, sung by Christians, is this one by Celtic Worship . 4. The Brain-Injured Musical Genius The New York Times had an amazing feature this week, and it was amazing in two ways. First, it was beautifully put together with animated graphics and other visual elements. Second, it told a remarkable story—the story of a man who suffered a terrible brain injury but, through it, became a musical genius. I think you’ll enjoy reading The Brain Injury That Made a Middle School Teacher a Musical Genius . 5. Grain from an Attic Here’s a fun story from Italy that pastors may want to hang on to for future sermon illustrations. In the early 1990s, a farmer in Parma found some old seeds in his attic. He assumed they were useless, so he tossed them on the manure pile. Much to his surprise, they sprouted into a form of grain he had never seen before. I’ll leave you to read the story, look at the pictures, and consider the many possible illustrations and applications. Photo credit: Clara Vannucci 6. Prepare Him Room (Live) A couple of days ago, a friend told me that his children had begun listening to Christmas music, and we discussed whether it’s still too early in the year for that. We agreed that you don’t want to begin listening too early lest you grow tired of the relatively limited catalog of songs before Christma

articles.content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Moody Publishers and adapted from The Unstoppable Gospel by Karl Clauson. It’s impossible to disciple lost people. That sounds obvious. Maybe too obvious to even say out loud. But when the church dilutes or neglects the good news, devastation is left in its wake. After forty years of ministry, this is the most sobering truth I’ve learned about the Western church: We do not merely have a discipleship problem today. We have a gospel problem. Before we ever became weak at disciple-making, we began redefining conversion itself. We slowly traded supernatural regeneration for human decision. Salvation became a prayer to repeat, a card to sign, an aisle to walk, while millions were assured of heaven without ever being transformed by the power of God. We didn’t offer them a belief lacking power, we offered them a powerless belief. The result is a generation that has been deeply Christianized but not necessarily changed. They know the language. They know the songs. They know when to stand, when to sit, when to say amen. They have been immersed in church culture, yet many have never been brought from death to life. We have filled churches with people who have learned how to function in and around “Christianity” without ever truly following Christ. And when that happens, discipleship collapses under the weight of human effort. When evangelism centers on human decision, discipleship inevitably becomes self-powered. Following Jesus is reduced to behavior management, moral striving, and “try harder next time.” The supernatural life Christ promised is replaced with self-help dressed up in religious garb. Dallas Willard spoke of “the Great Omission,” the church’s failure to make disciples. He was right. But I believe something even deeper has happened. Before we omitted discipleship, we compromised the very gospel that births disciples in the first place. That is the crisis. That is the great deception. And until we recover the true faith that changes everything, we will continue trying to disciple people who have never truly been made alive. We have, sitting in our church chairs and pews every weekend—even in good, Bible-teaching churches—vast numbers of people who believe themselves to be saved but possess no power beyond their own efforts and whose lives show only surface evidence of new birth. People assume what they have is all God has for them, not knowing they are cultural Christians, so close yet so far from God. People who have been taught a version of Christianity divorced from repentance, from surrender, from the cost of discipleship and, tragically, from the power that makes the gospel unstoppable. Many profess Christ but don’t possess Christ. We’ve left people needing more, wanting more, and settling for too little. The great deception must end. There is life for the spiritually dead. There is surrender that leads to life instead of loss. There is repentance that produces the rhythm of a flourishing soul. There is discipline that flows from grace instead of fear or performance. And there is deep, liberating, unmistakable freedom when Christ becomes everything. This is why truth must be championed. Not as an idea, but as a reality that cuts, clarifies, and calls us forward. Because when truth becomes really clear, it doesn’t just inform you. It changes you. It brings you out of the fog, out of the confusion, out of the illusion—and into a life that is grounded, whole, and fully alive with God. This is the gospel that birthed the early church. This is the gospel that turned the world upside down. This is the gospel that sustains God’s kids under brutal persecution today. This is the gospel the church has forgotten and the good news it desperately needs. This is the gospel that still changes everything today. Learn more about how we’ve embraced a version of the gospel that falls short of the life Jesus promised, and how you can go from powerless belief to a true faith that changes everything. Get

救世主成为了重复的祷告,签字的名片,行走的走道,而数百万人则得到天堂的保证,永远没有被上帝的力量所改变. 我们并没有给他们一个没有权力的信仰, 其结果是一代人被深深地基督教化,但不一定改变. 他们知道语言。 他们知道歌曲。

articles.title_zh: 如果你的教会唱希尔松歌，而你希望它不会唱，该怎么办？
articles.content: A few weeks ago, I explained why my church does not sing songs by Hillsong , and, by the same convictions, songs by Bethel and Elevation. I tried to be clear that I do not understand this to be a matter of clear right or wrong, but rather a matter of wisdom and conscience. While this is a decision we have made for our church, I would not look down on churches that choose differently. I wish I had addressed a related matter at that time: what should you do if you see this issue in the way I do, but the leaders of your church do not? In other words, what should you do if your church sings Hillsong, but you wish it wouldn’t? I want to offer just a few thoughts on that. In general, I would suggest you just sing the songs, provided they do not require you to sing anything that is unbiblical. And thankfully, the majority of the songs by Hillsong, Bethel, and Elevation will not force you to sing error. That said, there are a few songs that may come close, or whose lyrics are imprecise enough that they could be understood in different ways. For example, Hillsong’s “So Will I (100 Billion X)” has these words in its second verse and the chorus that follows it: All nature and science Follow the sound of Your voice And as you speak A hundred billion creatures catch your breath Evolving in pursuit of what you said If it all reveals your nature so will I The most natural reading of those words is an affirmation of some kind of theistic evolution. I could not sing that, and I understand that you may not be able to either. Bethel’s “Reckless Love” continually ascribes recklessness to God. Oh, the overwhelming, never-ending, reckless love of God Oh, it chases me down, fights ’til I’m found, leaves the ninety-nine I couldn’t earn it, I don’t deserve it, still You give Yourself away Oh, the overwhelming, never-ending, reckless love of God It is difficult for me ( and for John Piper , as it happens) to find a sense in which the word “reckless” is a fitting word for God. I think I know what the songwriters were hoping to convey with the word, but “reckless” is not suitable when speaking of God’s love and purposes, and I understand why many Christians could simply not permit themselves to sing it. I couldn’t either. But apart from those songs and a few others, most do not contain lyrics that are false or wrong. If your elders have deemed these songs suitable for your church, then it’s probably best to sing them in submission to the people whose leadership you have decided to follow. There is no “followership” in this world, other than following Christ, that does not at times involve submitting our own preferences to the preferences of our leaders. It would probably be a good time for a reminder that you just can’t have it all on this side of glory. Every pastor, every eldership, and every church will have both strengths and weaknesses. Too many Christians (who are also a bewildering collection of both strengths and weaknesses, of course) spend their whole lives searching for a perfect church, never quite grasping that it’s a futile effort. They go to the church with great preaching, but find that its evangelism is disappointing; they head for the church with great evangelism, but find its polity is poor. They soon switch again, this time choosing the church with their preferred polity, only to discover that it’s lacking in fellowship. They never learn the joy of settling into an imperfect church, in which they can rejoice in the strengths while bearing with the weaknesses. Sometimes accepting those weaknesses means singing songs or tolerating musical styles that are not aligned with their preferences, even when that’s hard to do. But what if the church does sing those songs that have actual errors in them? In the moment, I’d suggest you simply stop singing and refrain from making a big deal of it. You don’t need to make a fuss or storm out. But afterward, it would be wise to speak with your pastors to address your concerns, humbly, of course, and w
articles.content_zh:
几周前,我解释了为什么我的教堂 不唱山歌, 和同样的信念, 由贝瑟尔和Elevation的歌曲。 我试图表明,我不理解这是一个明确对错的问题,而是一个智慧和良心的问题。 虽然这是我们为我们的教会所做的决定,但我不会轻视那些选择不同的教会.

我希望当时我已谈到一个相关的问题:如果你以我的方式看待这个问题,但你们教会的领导人却不这样做,那你们应该怎么做? 换句话说,如果你的教堂唱山歌, 我只想就此提出几点想法。

一般来说,我建议你只是唱 歌曲,只要它们不要求你 唱任何非圣经。 谢天谢地,希尔松,贝瑟尔和Elevation的歌曲大多不会强迫你唱出错误. 虽然如此,也有几首歌可能接近,或者歌词不够精确,以至于可以以不同的方式被理解.

例如,Hillsong的"So Will I (1000亿 X)"的第二首诗中有这些词,下面的合唱: 所有自然和科学都跟着你的声音 当你说话时,一千亿生物 抓住你的呼吸 进取地追求你说的 如果这一切揭示你的本性,我也会 这些话最自然的读取是肯定某种神论

ution. 我无法唱出这首歌 我理解你也可能无法唱出这首歌 贝瑟尔的"无颈之爱"不断将鲁莽归咎于上帝.

我无法挣取的九十九分钱, 我并不配得到, 你还是放弃你自己。 我很难找到一种感觉,即“无畏”一词对上帝来说是合适的。

我想我知道那些作曲者希望用这个词表达什么,但是在谈论上帝的爱和宗旨时,“无畏”并不合适,我理解为什么许多基督徒不能允许自己唱出它。 我也不能。 但除这些歌曲和少数其他歌曲外,大多数歌曲没有包含虚假或错误的歌词.

如果你的长辈认为这首歌适合你的教会, 那么, 这个世界除了追随基督之外,没有“追随者”有时并不涉及我们自己对我们领导人的偏好。

可能是时候提醒大家, 每个牧师,每个长老,每个教会都会有优缺点. 太多的基督徒(当然,他们也是充满了优缺点和优缺点的令人困惑的集合者)毕生都在寻找一个完美的教堂,从不完全理解这是一个徒劳的努力。

他们带着伟大的传道去教堂,但发现其福音派令人失望;他们带着伟大的福音派去教堂,但发现其政体贫乏. 他们很快又转了身, 这次是用他们喜欢的政体选择教会,

他们永远无法学会安顿在一个不完善的教堂中的欢乐,在教堂里,他们可以在承受弱点的同时为长处而欢喜. 有时接受这些弱点意味着唱出歌曲或容忍不符合其喜好的音乐风格,即使这很难做到。 但是如果教会确实唱了那些有实际错误的歌呢?

我建议你别再唱歌, 你不需要大惊小怪, 但事后,明智的做法是与你的牧师们交谈 解决你的顾虑,当然,谦卑,和W

articles.title_zh: 点菜（ 11月9日）
articles.content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several excellent biographies from Crossway. Each of them is good, but I’m partial to the one on R.C. Sproul. Note that these biographies are typically priced between $22 and $40. In case you missed it on the weekend, Westminster Books is offering a deep discount on the new graphic novel adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress . Recommended Reading Christianity Under the Progressive Gaze. Kyle Borg: “What interests me more than politics is the apparent cultural strength and growing respectability of progressive Christianity. In fact, a headline in The Guardian boldly declared: ‘A progressive understanding of Christianity won in the US elections.’ In a society where historic Christian convictions — and I don’t just mean Reformed confessionalism but basic creedal Christianity — is often treated with suspicion, if not hostility, some expressions of ‘Christianity’ seem to be enjoying a rather warm reception.” Counterfeit Providence: Why Christians Must Reject the Conspiratorial Mind. Mitchell Bahnsen explores the conspiratorial mind and explains why it’s so important for Christians to reject it. “None of this requires Christians to become gullible or naive. Psalm 2 describes kings taking counsel together against the Lord, and the crucifixion itself was a conspiracy carried out jointly by religious and governmental authorities. True connivance does occur, and wisdom to discern the truth is necessary in a complex and fallen world. However, we must defend against a totalizing hermeneutic of suspicion, lest it become its own form of faith.” Wise People Strive To Be Wiser. Justin Huffman discusses a principle that may be obvious, but is also important. “The wise person is always seeking to become wiser still. The truly spiritual person recognizes his or her constant need for spiritual growth.” The Pro-Life Movement’s Midterm Reckoning. First Things allows everyone to access several free articles per month, and this one from Jonathon Van Maren is worth one of the quota. He considers how the battle against abortion is likely to look very different after the midterm elections. “‘It’s impossible to sugarcoat it,’ Marjorie Dannenfelser of Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America wrote in a memo issued on November 3. The 2026 midterm election results ‘are a disaster for the unborn, for their mothers, and for the country as a whole. Democrats are on track to control two of the three pieces they need to legalize taxpayer-funded abortion on demand, up until birth, in all fifty states—something they promise to start pushing as soon as they take office in January.'” How Evil Works. John Piper helpfully explains how evil works. “At the center of Satan’s purpose is to deceive on earth and to accuse in heaven. If he can deceive you about God and Christ, you will perish. If he can successfully accuse you of unforgiven sin in heaven, you will perish. And Jesus calls him ‘a murderer from the beginning’ (John 8:44). So, the deception and the accusation and the eternal death that results from unforgiven sin is a way of destroying people and opposing God.” Preaching in Paragraphs. This may be helpful for preachers to read as they let last week’s sermon fade into the past and begin to think about the next one. “Every preacher knows the terror of a blank screen. It is Tuesday morning—or even worse, Saturday afternoon—and the preacher sits and stares at his laptop. He has opened a new document in his word processor, and now the cursor stands idling on the page, patiently blinking. And the words aren’t coming.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. What books, products, videos, sites, or other experiences do you recommend to others who read this blog/newsletter? Let me know, and I’ll share a collection on Saturday. (If you’re reading this via email, you’ll need to visit my site to fill out the form. Go here to read last week’s recommendations.) Submit

维斯敏斯特书社(Westminster Books)对朝圣者进步的新平面小说改编提供了深刻的折扣。 推荐阅读基督教 在进步的盖兹。 Kyle Borg:“我比政治更感兴趣的是进步基督教明显的文化力量和日益受人尊重。

事实上,《卫报》的一篇头条大胆地宣称:`对基督教的进步理解在美国选举中获胜了'。 在一个历史基督教信仰 — — 我并不只是指宗教改革, 而是基本的信仰基督教 — — 往往被怀疑(如果不是敌对的话)的社会里, 伪造

普罗维登斯:为什么基督徒必须拒绝阴谋思想. Mitchell Bahnsen探讨阴谋论, “没有任何一项要求基督徒变得狡猾或天真。

"诗经"2描述了国王们联合起来向主提出反对的意见,而被钉十字架本身是宗教当局和政府当局联合进行的阴谋. 真正的纵容确实发生了,在一个复杂而衰落的世界中,辨别真相的智慧是必要的.

然而,我们必须为彻底的怀疑行为辩护,以免它成为自己的信仰形式。” 智者努力成为智者。 Justin Huffman)讨论了一项可能显而易见但也很重要的原则. “智者总是力求更加明智。

真正精神的人认识到他或她不断需要精神成长。” 亲生命运动中期评估。 首先,每个人都可以每月查阅几篇免费文章,这个来自Jonathon Van Maren的文章值得配额之一。 他认为,在中期选举之后,反对堕胎的斗争可能看起来非常不同。

Susan B的Marjorie Dannenfelser在11月3日发表的一份备忘录中写道, 2026年的中期选举结果“对未出生者、母亲和整个国家来说,

在五十个州,民主党人正在控制他们需要的三起堕胎中两起, 邪恶是如何起作用的。 约翰·皮珀(John Piper)有益地解释了邪恶是如何起作用的. " 撒旦的中心目的是在地上作弄欺骗,在天上指责.

如果他能欺骗你 关于上帝和基督, 你将毁灭。 如果他能成功地指控你在天堂的罪孽,你就会被毁灭. 耶稣称他为"从一开始的凶手"(John 8:44). 因此,欺骗、指控和由未免的罪恶所生的永恒死亡,是毁灭人民和反对上帝的一种方式。” 传入各段.

这或许有助于传道者阅读, “每个传教士都知道空白屏幕的恐怖。 今天是星期二早晨,甚至更糟糕的是,星期六下午,牧师坐着盯着他的笔记本电脑。

他在文字处理器中打开了一个新的文档,现在光标站在页面上,耐心地闪烁. 这些话不会传来。 读者建议 每周一次 我想问问你喜欢什么 推荐什么 你推荐哪些书籍、产品、视频、网站或其他经验给阅读博客/通讯的其他人? 让我知道,

articles.content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I like to let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. It is a quieter week than the last one, but it brings a revised edition of B. B. Warfield’s Biblical and Theological Studies, Alex Duke’s guided tour of Exodus (for which I provided a foreword), and two Crossway editions marking 500 years since William Tyndale’s English New Testament. On the academic side, you’ll find several noteworthy titles, including the New International Commentary on the Old Testament volume on Daniel 7–12. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. Books for Everyone Zondervan From Silence to Sinai A Guided Tour of Exodus Alex Duke Publisher’s description What adjectives would you use to describe the Bible? Inspired. Amazing. Unique. Authoritative. Perfect. Pure. Life-changing. Those descriptions are all deserved. Your pastors and parents and Sunday School teachers were right. There’s no book like God’s Book. Here’s another adjective: confusing. The Bible can be confusing, especially certain parts of the Old Testament. Moments after coming across something inspiring and encouraging, you’ll read something that makes you wonder, What is even happening right now!? The book of Exodus is no exception. This sequel to Genesis begins with God’s surprising silence. What a stark contrast to Genesis, where God’s words set everything in motion. It then tells the story of God’s miraculous liberation of his people, complete with frogs falling from the sky and life-saving blood being painted over doorways. Finally, for the last half of the book, the action slows down as the people of God gather at the mountain of God to receive the Law of God in order to engage in the worship of God. From silence to Sinai, that’s the story of Exodus. To understand it all, most of us will need a guide. We’ll need some help. That’s what From Silence to Sinai is for. Alex Duke walks readers through the book of Exodus to show that nothing in God’s story is wasted—not the silence, not the ten signs, and not even the confusing parts. In Exodus, God is not absent, random, or unclear. He is revealing himself, redeeming his people, and teaching them how to live in his presence. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . B&H The First Five Beating the Odds and Thriving as a Ministry Leader Kyle Worley and Joseph Worley Publisher’s description Is it possible to do more than survive in ministry leadership? Could you actually thrive? The alarming reality is that most ministry leaders will not make it more than five years in leadership. Burnout, lack of training, and an absence of coaches are all pitfalls on the road to sustainable ministry leadership. But there is a different roadmap for those willing to learn. In The First Five , Joseph and Kyle Worley present a pathway for thriving in ministry leadership. With over sixty years of experience, across churches of every size and shape, they provide a biblically rooted and tested approach to the personal, professional, and pastoral dynamics of ministry leadership. The First Five is designed to be a manual for new ministry leaders and those leading them. Don’t just read this book—use it! You can do more than survive as a ministry leader. We believe you can thrive. Buy it at Amazon . Preorder · releases Wednesday, November 11 P&R Biblical and Theological Studies Revised and Enhanced Benjamin B. Warfield, edited by John J. Hughes Endorsed by: Vern S. Poythress, Thomas R. Schreiner, R. Scott Clark, Donald Macleod, and Richard C. Gamble Publisher’s description Classic articles from Warfield, enhanced for ease of reading, explore God, predestination, the supernaturalism of Christianity, the antiquity and unity of the human race, mysticism, and the prophecies of Paul. 每一次,我都包括出版商的描述。 从沉默到西奈的图书, 你用什么形容词来形容圣经? 发菩提心. 厉害 独一无二 专权性. 不错 纯净. 改变生活。 这些描述都是值得的。 你的牧师和家长 以及星期日学校的老师是对的

没有像上帝的书那样的书。 以下是另一个形容词:令人困惑。 圣经可以令人困惑,特别是旧约中的某些部分. 在经历了一些鼓舞人心和鼓舞人心的事情之后, 你会读到一些让你感到奇怪的东西, 出家经卷亦无例外. 创世纪的续集开始于上帝令人惊讶的沉默。

与创世纪的鲜明对比,上帝的言语让一切动起来. 它讲述了上帝奇迹般地解放其人民的故事,最后是青蛙从天而降,在门道上画出拯救生命的鲜血。

最后,在书的后半段,随着上帝的百姓聚集在神的山上接受神的律法,以从事对神的崇拜,这一行动放缓了. 从沉默到西奈,这就是出埃及的故事。 为了了解这一切,我们大多数人都需要一个指南。 需要帮助。 从沉默到西奈,

articles.content: Let me take a moment to remind you of some of the features of this site you may not know about. I have a growing page of Liturgies meant to help the local church in its worship. I also offer Book Recommendations across many categories and a list of the Best Commentaries for each book of the Bible. And if you like the quote graphics I share day by day, you can find them all at SquareQuotes.church where they are free to download. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several of the “Heart Talks” mini books that are meant to help women with common concerns: feeling like failures in parenting, husbands who lead poorly, doubt, and so on. You’ll also find Greg Gifford’s Lies My Therapist Told Me and several other titles. Recommended Reading Beer, Beef and Player’s Navy Cut. This is a brilliant article about C.S. Lewis and the vices that dogged him throughout his life—a three-pack-a day smoking habit, eating habits that bordered on gluttony, and far more alcohol than anyone should consume. “In case you really are new here and you mostly know Lewis from the kid’s books, let’s state the obvious: the man we universally honor as one of the 20th Century’s great saints smoked, ate and drank like he was a sponsored athlete of consumption. He sinned frequently through overindulgence. What do we do with this information?” How to Graciously Say No. You have probably run into the same conclusion I have: it’s often far harder to say no than to say yes. Yet sometimes the best thing we can do for ourselves and for others is to say no. Reagan Rose offers some thoughts on that (for those who have the ability to say no, of course, since in many occupations saying no isn’t an option). Can’t You Let Me Just Attend? “We live in a chronically noncommittal society. No wonder, then, that this has been dubbed the age of anxiety. Surely, covenant relationships aren’t the only cure, but it might surprise us how much stability of soul comes from deep, reliable, unflighty fellowship.” David Mathis explains why commitment to a particular church is so important, even if it’s extremely countercultural. When Morningness Is Confused With Godliness. I always enjoy an article that provides an alternate view of something we almost take for granted. That’s the case with this one from Cole Mizel, who is concerned that we may be too quick to imply that the best Christians do their daily devotions in the morning. “But is it really more virtuous to be a morning person than a night owl?” Everyone Doesn’t React the Same Way. J.V. Fesko makes a simple but wise point here: everyone doesn’t respond to preaching the same way. Because that’s the case, we should not assume that those who display a lot of emotion are necessarily being impacted more than those who do not. “Tears are not the sacrament of a changed heart, the visible sign and seal of an anguished and healed soul.” Evangelising With a Dog. I enjoyed reading Peter Barnes’s account of evangelizing with a dog. “My doctor, who is half my size, suggested as tactfully as he could, what was obvious to all – that my squash days were over, and that I should take to walking the dog in the morning and at lunchtime. So this has become my nod to the need for daily exercise. Being one of the few beings on the planet who still buys a hard copy of a daily newspaper, I take my hound – a cocker spaniel with unusually short legs – with me of a morning. articles.content: Tuesday is the day most Christian publishers release their new books, so each week I let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. This week brings Andrew Walker’s diagnosis of our prodigal culture, a graphic-novel edition of The Pilgrim’s Progress , and Samuel James’s Scroll Less, Live More . On the academic side, you will find reference works and commentaries. You may also want to consider Trevin Wax’s liturgy for daily prayer. For each book, I’ve included the publisher’s description and its list of endorsers. Books for Everyone Crossway Prodigal Culture A People in Ruins and the Way Back Home Andrew T. Walker Endorsed by: R. Albert Mohler Jr., Carl R. Trueman, Allie Beth Stuckey, Seth Dillon, and Kristen Waggoner Publisher’s description We have forgotten what it means to be human. American men and women are feeling the despair of a counterfeit culture, one where polarization has replaced conversation, pornography is chosen over true intimacy, and marriage and family are postponed indefinitely. The resulting isolation has forced us to confront the truth: individualism and worldly systems cannot take the place of God’s design for humanity. This scholarly yet accessible study examines the effects of secularism, nihilism, and barbarism on culture today, and explains why a biblical worldview is essential for human flourishing. Andrew T. Walker skillfully confronts 10 pressing issues—including loneliness, sexual confusion, anti-institutionalism, and identity. Affirming that shared norms grounded in creation order are the solution to social decline, he champions a return to biblical standards of freedom, human nature, and purpose. Walker compares Western culture to the prodigal son in Scripture—a culture that has squandered its inheritance and must now decide whether it will return to the Father or continue living in squalor. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . Crossway Scroll Less, Live More 10 Healthy Tech Habits for Teens Samuel D. James Endorsed by: Paul David Tripp, Matt Smethurst, and Whitney Newby Publisher’s description Nearly every teenager carries a smartphone in their pocket. What was once an innocent tool, providing a quick escape and a promise of connection, has now become a world that holds us captive. Looking up from the tiny pixels and refraining from the incessant scrolling may be the rest that our souls need. Scroll Less, Live More offers teens and families 10 practical habits for navigating the world of technology from a Christian perspective. From the author of the Christian Book Award winner, Digital Liturgies, tech-realist Samuel James applies his ideas into action steps to help teenagers keep digital tools in their proper place. By addressing how technology affects our social interactions, sleep patterns, critical thinking, and much more, James helps readers see the wisdom in God’s perfect design and, as a result, resist the temptations prevalent in the smartphone age. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . Zondervan Get to Work Seeing Your Daily Grind as God’s Good Gift Jonny Ardavanis Endorsed by: R. Kent Hughes, R. articles.title_zh: 点菜（ 11月3日）
articles.content: Grace and peace to you, my friends. I’ve got a list of great links for you to consider reading today, then a brief look at some of this week’s new Christian books (plus a link to discover many more). Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals are excellent! Concise Reformed Dogmatics is a great deal, since the list price is $40. Also consider Nancy Guthrie’s devotional resource to help you pray for your children. The Discipline of Grace is one of my all-time favorite books. Over at Westminster Books, you can get the best pricing on Dissecting the Heart , a book that “brings some of David Powlison’s best insights to a new generation that is struggling to deal with its relationship to secular psychology and spiritual formation.” Recommended Reading May God Be Gracious to Us: A Prayer Before Election Day. As America heads to the polls, Christian voters may benefit from reminding themselves of the truths in this article and praying the prayer it provides. “On May 17, 1776, John Witherspoon stepped into the pulpit at Princeton on a day of fasting the Continental Congress had appointed for all the colonies. War had already begun and independence was less than two months away. Witherspoon, a Presbyterian minister and soon-to-be signer of the Declaration of Independence, called the occasion a ‘day of solemn humiliation.’ Before he said a word about the conflict, he turned his hearers’ eyes to the sovereign providence of God. He closed with a prayer: ‘God grant that in America true religion and civil liberty may be inseparable, and that the unjust attempts to destroy the one, may in the issue tend to the support and establishment of both.'” Looksmaxxing: The Normalizing of Vanity. Jacob Crouch: “To say it plainly, Christians don’t looksmaxx. However much we may be into fitness or beauty, we reject looksmaxxing on three levels: our worth, our temporality, and our purpose. Our beauty is temporary; and all our beauty is for His glory. Our beauty does not determine our worth, because our value is fixed in Christ.” A Wretch Like Me. This is a very well-written article about John Newton and the reason he chose to describe himself as a wretch. “When Newton wrote what would become one of the best-loved hymns of the Christian church, he was looking back on a life that had taken him to rock bottom – and into the horrors of the Atlantic slave trade. Reading ‘Amazing Grace’ is like witnessing a confession. You are invited into someone’s life, and its darkest parts are laid bare before you. But the hymn doesn’t only dwell on the wretchedness of sin; it celebrates the deep, satisfying transformation of its author. And what a transformation it was!” The Belly Dancer Grandmas. This writer tells about the unfortunate experience of seeing belly-dancing grandmothers and relates it to his experiences on the frontiers of missions. “I remember once seeing a Facebook post from a Melanesian friend, commenting on an American pro-transgender news report. A direct translation of her comment would be, ‘Look at this – the whiteskins have lost their minds!’ Now, it wasn’t that long ago, perhaps even as recently as her great-grandparents’ generation, that her own society was a cannibalistic one, trapped in its own temporary insanity.” Thankfully, God so often interrupts that temporary insanity. On the Naming of Death. Andrew Roycroft has a strong and moving article about the naming of death. “In this short piece, I want to reflect on our obsession and squeamishness about the grotesqueness of death and to suggest some ways our current season of the year might reveal our deeper cultural preoccupations. In a follow-up article, I want to think about the practice of naming the dead, and the importance of measured and authentic memorial.” Reader Responses to ‘What We Know—and Cannot Know—About Elisabeth Elliot’s Sexuality’. articles.content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Zondervan . This article is taken from The Jesus Bible , from Passion Publishing and Zondervan. The Lord called Joshua to be strong and courageous as Joshua replaced Moses as Israel’s leader and led the people into the promised land. This calling was based on his obedience and submission to the Word of God. As the Creator, God knows how life is meant to be lived and the way for people to experience life to the full ( Jn 10:10). The gift of the law was a gracious act of God to instruct his people in his ways. It was never intended to be a moralistic plan to earn God’s favor. Rather, the law was given to those who had already experienced God’s redeeming grace. In the law, God provided instructions for how his children can love him and other people. This law is not a collection of arbitrary dictates from a malevolent deity, but instead it is the wisdom of God distilled in human language. It is a path to joy and life — the way people were meant to live. The Bible continually portrays the law of God in this fashion. For example, in the longest psalm in the Bible, Psalm 119, the author says that he loves, treasures, delights in and longs for the law. It is a source of hope, peace, joy and direction. In Psalm 19, the psalmist says the law refreshes the soul, makes wise the simple, gives joy to the heart and gives light to the eyes (Ps 19:7 – 8). The law is a beautiful gift from a gracious God. Jesus testified to the lasting value of the law when he said that he did not come to abolish the law (Mt 5:17). Instead, Jesus amplified the law, explaining the transformation that should result as a proper response to his work. In his masterful Sermon on the Mount in Matthew 5 through 7, Jesus called people to a far greater standard of obedience than mere conformity to external regulations. Instead of simply condemning murder, Jesus unmasked the anger that fueled this act. Adultery is not the prime culprit, but lust rooted in the human heart is the real problem. Jesus methodically outlined the heart-level change that the law relied upon. Rather than rendering the law obsolete, Jesus showed that the law continued to provide an authoritative standard and guidance for God’s people. Now, because of the finished work of Christ, believers have hope that the price for their disobedience of the law has been paid and that they have God’s Spirit dwelling within them, providing them the power to live the life God intends. 博客由Zondervan赞助, 这篇文章取自"耶稣圣经","激情出版"和"赞德凡". 耶和华召约书亚为强而勇敢,因为约书亚取代了摩西成为以色列领导人并带领人民进入所应许之地. 这个召唤是基于他的服从和顺从上帝之道.

作为造物主,上帝知道生命的本意,知道人们如何体验到生命的完全(Jn 10:10). 法律的天赋是上帝的恩惠行为,以指示他的人民如何行事. 这从来就没有打算成为赢得上帝恩惠的道德计划。 相反,法律是给予那些已经经历过上帝赎回恩惠的人的。

在法律中,上帝为他的孩子如何能爱他和其他人提供了指示. 这部法则并不是从邪恶的神灵中任意地指令的集合,而是用人类语言来提炼出上帝的智慧. 这是通往快乐和生活的道路——人们本该生活的方式。 圣经以这种方式不断地描绘出上帝的法则.

耶稣作证了法律的持久价值,他说他不是来废除法律的(Mt 5:17). 相反地,耶稣放大了律法,解释了应该因适当回应他的工作而导致的转变. 在他精通马太福音5号到7号的"山上赛蒙"中,耶稣把人们称为服从的标准远远高于单纯遵守外规.

耶稣不是简单地谴责谋杀,而是揭发了激起这一行为的愤怒. 通奸不是罪魁祸首,但植根于人心的欲望才是真正的问题. 耶稣有条不紊地概述了法律所依赖的心脏层面的变化. 耶稣没有使法律过时,而是表明法律继续为上帝的人民提供权威的标准和指导.

现在,由于基督的完成,信徒们希望他们违抗法律的代价已经付出,他们心中有上帝的精神,给他们以神想要的生活的力量。 另见12月自由聚会(Zondervan反省会)12月自由聚会(Zondervan反省会)自由聚会(Zondervan反省会)的基督教新书。

articles.title: Tips for Resolving Conflict in Marriage
articles.summary: Conflict in marriage is inevitable, but resolving it well is a skill. Here are 6 practical tips that range from examining your own sin first to a 10 p.m. rule. See Also Danger Signs of an Unhealthy Dating Relationship The Beginner’s Guide to Conflict Resolution Free Stuff Fridays
articles.summary_zh: 婚姻中的冲突是不可避免的，但妥善解决冲突是一项技能。这里有6个实用技巧，从先检查你自己的罪到晚上10点的规则。另请参阅不健康约会关系的危险迹象周五解决冲突的初学者指南免费内容
articles.title_zh: 解决婚姻冲突的技巧
articles.content: It is inevitable that lives lived in deep intimacy will generate conflict. We wish this weren’t so, but sadly, it is. Therefore, wise couples learn to anticipate conflict and learn to resolve it well. I was recently asked to provide some thoughts on conflict resolution, and thought I’d share what I came up with. Yet as I have sat with couples and tried to help them work through various issues, it has shocked me to find how many have never learned to settle conflict well. Many set habits and patterns in their early years that become hard to break or overcome. I have met with couples who have only ever tried to resolve conflict by raising their voices, and with others who have only ever tried to resolve it by going silent. I have met with some who have only ever relied on text messaging instead of speaking face to face, and with others who have long since given up and don’t even bother trying anymore. Much of this stems from their first years and their failure to get well grounded in conflict resolution. To that end, here are a few suggestions on resolving conflict well. First, borrowing from Robert Murray M’Cheyne, follow this pattern: For every one look at your spouse’s sin, take ten at your own. It’s easy enough to become an expert in the way your spouse sins against you, but it’s far more important to become an expert in the ways you sin against your spouse. It concerns me when I see someone who seems adamantly committed to his spouse’s holiness but seemingly not very interested in his own. Your first calling before the Lord is to deal with your own sin so you can put it to death and come alive to righteousness. Second, invite your spouse to identify your sin. Because of the sheer quantity of the time and intimacy you share, you will inevitably sin against your spouse more than you will sin against anyone else. Not only that, but married life lets your spouse see the kinds of sins that no one else will. Only he or she sees how you sin in the bedroom, for example, or when you’re running late and nobody else is around. What’s more, your spouse sees deeper into your soul than anyone else and, therefore, knows more about you. In a healthy marriage, if you are truly committed to holiness, it only makes sense that you will ask your spouse to speak into your life. It is wise to provide a safe setting to do this where you won’t be a baby or a bully, and won’t sulk or lash out. Set aside some time, tell your spouse that you’d like to hear what sins you are committing, then listen patiently and calmly, without showing anger or being defensive. Having done that, go away, think about it, pray about it, and don’t respond until a day later. This could be a great means of grace in your life. Third, identify times when you won’t try to resolve conflict. Aileen and I, for example, have a long-established 10 o’clock rule, which means we won’t try to fix anything after 10 p.m. We are well aware that Ephesians 4:26 says, “Do not let the sun go down on your anger,” but we have also learned that some issues simply cannot be neatly resolved by bedtime. (Married folk will know that some of the most common conflicts tend to happen between the time you get into bed together and the time you actually fall asleep.) The later the day gets, the more we tend to operate out of emotion rather than reason. And some things seem way worse in the evening when we’re tired than in the morning when we’re fresh. So if we haven’t worked it out by 10, we will call a halt, kiss one another, pray with one another, say something like “I love you and we are going to be all right,” and then go to sleep. Then we can try to work it out at a better time, when we are in a better frame of mind. And honestly, in the light of day, we often realize the situation wasn’t nearly as dire as we thought and that it can be covered by love (1 Peter 4:8). Fourth, invite others in when necessary. Sometimes the most helpful thing you can do in a time of conflict is invite some friends or so

生活在深深的亲密中的生活必然会引发冲突。 但可悲的是, 因此,明智的夫妇学会预测冲突并学会妥善解决冲突。 最近有人要求我提出一些解决冲突的想法,

然而,当我与夫妇们坐在一起,努力帮助他们解决各种问题时,我发现有多少人从未学会妥善解决冲突,这让我感到震惊。 许多人在早年就设定了难以打破或克服的习惯和模式.

我见过夫妇们,他们只试图通过提高声音来解决冲突,而其他人则只试图通过沉默来解决冲突。 我会见了一些只依靠短信而不是面对面发言的人,

其主要原因是他们最初的岁月和未能在解决冲突中扎根。 为此,我们提出一些关于妥善解决冲突的建议。 首先,向罗伯特·默里·姆谢恩借款,遵循这一模式: 每看一看配偶的罪孽,就自己拿十。

成为你配偶对你的罪过的专家是很容易的, 当我看到有人 似乎坚定致力于他的配偶的圣洁,

你第一次在主面前召唤是 处理你自己的罪过 这样你就可以把它死 并活到正义。 其次,请您的配偶 识别你的罪恶。 由于你所分享的时间和亲密关系,你不可避免地会对你的配偶犯下比对其他人犯下更严重的罪行。

不仅如此 婚姻生活让你的配偶看到 别人不会犯的罪 只有他或她看到你在卧室的罪过, 更何况,你的配偶比任何人都更深刻地看待你的灵魂,从而更了解你。

在一个健康的婚姻中,如果你真正致力于圣洁,那么你要求你的配偶在你的生活中说话就只有道理了. 最好提供安全的环境,

也不要发怒或防卫。 并且直到一天后才回应。 这可能是你生命中伟大的恩典手段. 第三,确定你何时不会试图解决冲突。

例如艾琳和我早就有十点的规则, 我们清楚地知道,以弗所4:26说,“不要让太阳落在你的愤怒上,”但我们也了解到,有些问题根本不能通过睡觉来彻底解决。

(结婚后人们会知道,一些最常见的冲突往往发生在你们上床睡觉的时间与实际入睡的时间之间. 一天越晚,我们就越倾向于出于情感而不是理性而行动. 有些事情在晚上比早上更糟糕,

因此,如果我们还没有在10点之前解决,我们将叫停,互相亲吻,相互祈祷,说出类似“我爱你,我们会没事的”的话,然后睡觉。 然后,我们可以尝试在更好的时间,当我们处于一个更好的思维框架时,解决它。

老实说,在白天,我们常常意识到,情况没有我们想象的那么糟糕,而且可以被爱所覆盖(1:彼得:8). 第四,在必要时邀请其他人参加。 有时候,在冲突时期,你能做的最有帮助的事 就是邀请一些朋友

articles.content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a lot of great books to start a new month. If all goes according to schedule, the list will include works on apologetics, singing, Karl Marx and D.L. Moody, missionaries who were recently martyred in Haiti, and much more. Enjoy the bounty! Logos users will want to take a look at this month’s free and nearly-free books. You’ll also find some early Black Friday deals that include some commentaries at up to 80% off. It’s also worth browsing the monthly sales . Recommended Reading A Candy Shop Owner, a Customs Officer, and a Beloved Family. I like this illustration. “Anyone traveling to another country knows that customs officers don’t mess around. They might grill you about what you are bringing into the country, who you are visiting, where you are going, and what your intentions are in the country. I’ve been asked all of those questions. I’ve never felt warmly welcomed by a customs officer. Currently our daughter lives in Southern California. We look forward to those sweet times she can come home. When she arrives home for Christmas, will we grill her? ‘What are the purposes of your stay at our home?’ ‘Who do you plan to visit?’ ‘What are you bringing into our home?’ Certainly not! We will throw the door open, wrap her in our arms, and welcome her in. She is family!” Your Definition of Blessing Is Too Small. “How do we square the Bible’s unblushing promises of blessing for the faithful with its theology of suffering? Put another way, how does Psalm 128 fit with a passage like Psalm 88, where the faithful one seems utterly abandoned to the darkness? One way to answer this question succinctly is to realize that the Bible, first, expands the meaning of blessing in this life, and second, eternalizes it.” These are helpful categories when we consider a difficult topic. 5 Ways Retirees Can Serve the Church. I am not yet a retiree, but when the time comes, this article lists some of the ways I will want to serve my church. “‘Retirement at last! Now I can sleep as late as I want to. Now I get to do nothing all day.’ Such is a popular description of how retirement looks to many people. I know some who would even add, ‘Now I get to play golf every day.’ Obviously, this does not reflect the Christian perspective of someone who understands that his chief end is ‘to glorify God and enjoy Him forever.’ This is not to say that sleeping later and playing golf are anti-Christian. However, there are some significant ways that retirees can still serve the church.” You Can See Everything: On Masks, Performing, and Holiness. You have probably heard at least something about the new film You Can See Everything . Joseph Whitenton explains that the movie provokes the question of whether you can ever truly know someone, then says “I can’t help but feel a deep sense of dread. Is this really all we can say about our relationships to one another? That it might be impossible to really know someone? To even know ourselves? Are our lives just a string of performances? I can’t help but think about how a social media centered age might further contribute to this feeling of constantly performing, as Bo Burnham, another comedian/prophet has observed.” The Straightest Path to Happiness. Randy Alcorn: “In God’s world, happiness is found in discovering what’s truly in our self-interest: loving God and our neighbor. This profound, paradigm-shifting concept, understood correctly, makes the false dichotomy obvious in the question, ‘Should I serve others, or should I act in my own best interests?'” The Danger of ‘No Enemies to the Right’. articles.title: Works & Wonders (November 1)
articles.summary: This week’s Works & Wonders: God’s power paired with his goodness, Wikipedia’s most-read page, weather photos, Anchor Hymns, a one-trick app, and men who sing. See Also Works & Wonders: October 25 Works & Wonders (Oct 11) Works & Wonders (August 2)
articles.summary_zh: 本周的作品与奇迹：上帝的力量与他的善良、维基百科阅读量最大的页面、天气照片、锚定赞美诗、单一技巧应用程序和唱歌的人相结合。另请参阅作品与奇观： 10月25日作品与奇观（ 10月11日）作品与奇观（ 8月2日）
articles.title_zh: 作品与奇观（ 11月1日）
articles.content: In my weekly Works & Wonders column, I combine a brief devotional with other interesting and uplifting bits and pieces I gleaned throughout the week. I hope you enjoy this week’s collection! It includes: When God Acts in Power Wikipop Weather Photographer of the Year Bring on the Dawn Big Words Men Sing 1. When God Acts in Power No element of God’s character can be separated from any other. You or I may use the power available to us recklessly, imperfectly, or sinfully—we may act forcefully yet unwisely, or authoritatively yet with evil motives and immoral outcomes. We may act impulsively, on the basis of false information, or in ways that foster prejudice or injustice. In this way, power can be used to bring about great good or great harm. But God never acts in such a way that he diminishes any part of his character. Hence, when God acts in power, he invariably exercises that power in ways that are wise, holy, just, good, and true. I think Jen Wilkin says this well: “The truth of God’s limitless power would be absolutely terrifying were it not paired with the truth of His limitless goodness.” God’s power separated from his other attributes would mean there is nothing that would withhold or restrain him. Yet God’s power paired with his other attributes is tremendously comforting, for we know he will use his power only in ways that are ultimately for our good and his glory. 2. Wikipop Wikipop is a microsite that offers the answer to just one question: What Wikipedia page was everyone looking at yesterday? You probably won’t be shocked to know that on Saturday, when I finalized this article, it told me that everyone had been looking for Patrick Stewart, who died a few days prior. (Note: I add this site with a bit of trepidation because I can’t predict what article will be featured on the day you click the link, so hopefully it’s nothing bad!) 3. Weather Photographer of the Year I know I keep sharing photography contests, but as I said last week, this is the time of year when many of them announce the winners. But this one is different from others I have shared since it features weather. In the Weather Photographer of the Year shortlist, you’ll find exactly what you’d expect—a stunning collection of photos of the weather. 4. Bring on the Dawn I know many people who have appreciated Douglas McKelvey’s Every Moment Holy books, which offer liturgies and prayers for all of life’s moments. Anchor Hymns recently collaborated with McKelvey on an album titled Bring on the Dawn that was inspired by his books. I’m pretty sure that if you appreciate the books, you’ll also like the music. 5. Big Words Sometimes the best apps are the simplest—the ones that do just one thing, but do it well. That’s the case with Big Words . What does it do? It lets you use your phone (or iPad or other screen) to display big words. “Make a full-screen sign, timer or message from a link. Hold up your phone at arrivals, put a countdown on the TV, or show the Wi-Fi password at the front desk. No account, no app, nothing stored on a server. The link is the whole display, so you can share it or bookmark it.” There is nothing to download, so you can just go ahead and bookmark it to use when the need arises. 6. Men Sing I love this delightfully countercultural “Men Sing” trend that’s happening among Dutch Reformed churches, and would love to see it spread. What is it? It’s just men getting together to sing hymns. I had hoped to attend the recent one in Hamilton, but was on the road at the time. Hopefully I can make it to the next one. You can find videos from churches in Hamilton , Grand Rapids , and Chilliwack . I assume it’s happening in other places where there are lots of Dutch Reformed churches. Well done, Dutch guys! See Also Works & Wonders: October 25 Works & Wonders (Oct 11) Works & Wonders (August 2)
articles.content_zh:
在每周的Works & Wonders专栏中,我把简短的奉献与我整个星期所收集的其他有趣而令人振奋的作品结合起来。 希望你们能欣赏这周的作品! 它包括: 当上帝在权力中的行为 维基百科中的相关条目: 天气摄影师 这一年带来黎明的大字眼 男人会唱歌 1 当上帝在权力中行事时,神性的任何要素都不能与任何其他要素相分离。
你或我可能会莽撞地、不完美地、或罪恶地使用我们所拥有的权力——我们可能会以邪恶的动机和不道德的结果,采取强而不明智或权威的行动。 我们可能根据虚假信息或以助长偏见或不公正的方式采取冲动行动。 这样,权力可以用来带来巨大的好坏.
但上帝从不以这样的方式行事,以致于削弱他性格的任何部分. 因此,当上帝行使权力时,他总是以明智、神圣、公正、善良和真实的方式行使这种权力。
我认为Jen Wilkin说得好 : “ 如果上帝无限力量的真理不与他无限善良的真理相配的话,那将是绝对可怕的。 ” 神的力量与他的其他属性相分离,将意味着没有任何东西可以扣留或约束他.
然而,上帝的力量与他的其他属性相配,是极为安慰的,因为我们知道,他只会以最终有利于我们及其光荣的方式使用他的力量。 2. Wikipop Wikipop是一个微站点,只回答一个问题:昨天大家看的维基百科页面是什么?
你可能不会惊讶地知道, 星期六我写完这篇文章时, (注:我加上这个网站有点惊慌, 因为我无法预测您点击链接当天会刊登什么文章, 3个
天气摄影师,我知道我一直 分享摄影比赛, 但正如我上周所说, 但这个与我分享的其他不同,因为它的特点是天气。 在年度天气摄影短名单中, 你会找到你所期望的,  4.四.
我认识很多人欣赏道格拉斯·麦克凯维的"每一分一秒"的书, Anchor Hymns最近与McKelvey合作, 我敢肯定,如果你欣赏这些书,你也会喜欢音乐。 5 (韩语).
大词 有时最好的应用最简单, 大字报就是这样。 这有什么用? 它让你使用手机(或iPad或其他屏幕)来显示大字. “从链接中制作全屏标志、定时器或信息。 电话在到达时暂停,在电视上倒计时,或在前台显示无线密码.
没有账户 没有应用 没有存储在服务器上 链接是整个显示,所以你可以分享它或者书签它。” 没有什么可以下载的,所以你可以继续去书签,以便在需要的时候使用. 六. 男子歌唱我爱这种令人愉快的反文化"男子歌"趋势, 这是什么?
只是男人聚在一起唱颂歌。 我本来希望参加最近在汉密尔顿的比赛 但当时还在路上 希望我能赶到下一个 在汉密尔顿、大拉皮兹和奇利瓦克的教堂, 我想这发生在其他地方, 干得好,荷兰人!

articles.content: October was a strong month for new Christian books. I tried to keep you in the loop week by week, but I also wanted to provide a roundup for the end of the month. Of all the books that came our way in October, here are the ones that most stood out to me, arranged in what I think is a nice new format. As always, I’ve included the publisher’s editorial description for each. Book of the Month Crossway · Hardcover · 736 pages The Westminster Confession of Faith: A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application Edited by J. V. Fesko, John R. Muether, and D. Blair Smith If I had to put one book on the top of the stack this month, it would probably be this commentary on the Westminster Confession of Faith—and I say that as a Baptist who respects, but does not hold to, the WCF. The contributors include Sinclair Ferguson, Chad Van Dixhoorn, and Kevin DeYoung. This is a reference work that pastors and serious readers will want to add to their libraries. “This essential collection of essays presents an accessible guide to the Westminster Confession of Faith for 21st-century readers. Each chapter is devoted to a section of the historic document, carefully studying its context, its significance to the faith, and its application, as well as any controversies.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books For Your Own Soul Books for any thoughtful Christian reader. Crossway · Hardcover · 264 pages Finally Home: The Christian Hope of Heaven Dane Ortlund In this book, Dane Ortlund ( Gentle and Lowly ) turns his attention to heaven. He draws on Scripture, of course, and also on writers like Thomas Goodwin, Jonathan Edwards, and C. S. Lewis. “If we are not in Christ, this life is the best we will ever experience. If we are in Christ, this life is the worst we will ever experience. … In Finally Home , Dane Ortlund plunges into the word of God and the wisdom of the saints to help us rightly think about heaven, and to draw strength from our coming future more deeply than we ever have before.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books IVP · Paperback · 192 pages Everyday Discipleship: How Faith Shapes the Most Practical Areas of Life Jeremy Treat This is a practical book that teaches how following Jesus extends into every part of life, including those that are very ordinary, like meals, work, rest, and technology. It includes a discussion guide for groups. “Pastor Jeremy Treat understands this disconnect. In Everyday Discipleship , he dismantles the harmful sacred-secular divide that leaves many Christians feeling spiritually compartmentalized, uncertain about how faith applies to ordinary life, and unable to fully enjoy Christ in the entirety of our lives.” Buy it at Amazon Banner of Truth · Clothbound · 248 pages God Is Our Refuge and Strength: 150 Devotionals Through the Psalms William Boekestein & Rob Ventura Every Banner of Truth release is noteworthy, isn’t it? This one offers a short devotional reading to accompany each of the 150 psalms. “You need the Psalms. The Psalms are the Bible’s devotional heart. … Through brief, practical expositions of all 150 psalms, this volume proclaims, explains, and applies each one in light of the New Testament and the finished work of Jesus Christ the Lord.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books Counseling & Care Resources to care for Christians. One Measure Ministries · Redemption Press · Paperback workbooks SoulCare Groups™ Workbooks: Anxiety, Grief, and Sexual Integrity Gary & Linda Baer I am excited about the SoulCare Groups™ workbooks, which came out this month. Each is a twelve-week group study meant to be used alongside a few trusted biblical counseling books. The first three volumes cover anxiety, grief, and sexual integrity. “SoulCare Groups™, a biblical counseling workbook series from One Measure Ministries, equips churches to offer groups-based care through structured twelve-week topical studies.” Buy them at Amazon: Anxiety · Grief · Sexual Integrity For the Church and Its History Books to u
articles.content_zh: 十月是基督教新书的强月. 我试图让你每周循环, 但我也想提供 一个回合的月底。 在10月我们走过来的所有书中, 这里有那些最突出的, 以我认为一种很好的新格式排列。 我总是把出版商的编辑描述都包括进去。 " 月之十字路口"一书 硬封面 736页 " 威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔:对其历史、神学和应用的综合评论 " 由J. V. Fesko、John R. Muether和D. Blair Smith编辑 如果这个月我不得不把一本书放在堆起的顶上,那很可能就是关于威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔书的评论——我说,作为一个尊重但不坚持周转基金的浸信会信徒。 撰稿人包括辛克莱·弗格森(Sinclair Ferguson),乍得·范迪克斯霍恩(Chad Van Dixhoorn)和凯文·德杨(Kevin DeYoung). 这是牧师和认真的读者想要加入他们的图书馆的参考作品. “这一系列重要的散文为21世纪的读者提供了一本《威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔指南》。 每一章都专门讨论历史文件的一节,仔细研究其背景、其对信仰的意义、其适用以及任何争议。” 在亚马逊购买, Crossway-Hardcover-264页 最后回家:天堂的基督教希望-丹麦奥特伦德 在这本书中,达尼·奥特伦德(英语:Dane Ortlund (Gentle and Lowly))将注意力转向了天堂. 他当然借鉴了"圣经",同时也借鉴了托马斯·古德温,乔纳森·爱德华兹和C·S·刘易斯等作家. “如果我们不是在基督中,这种生活是我们所经历的最好生活。 如果我们在基督, 这样的生活是我们所经历的最糟糕的。 . . . . . . . 最后,Dane Ortlund在“家园”中投入了上帝的言行和圣徒的智慧,帮助我们正确思考天堂,并比以往更深刻地汲取我们未来的力量。” 在亚马逊购买它 威斯敏斯特书 IVP 页面存档备份,存于互联网档案馆 192页 每日论文:信仰如何塑造最实用的生活领域 Jeremy对待 这是一本实用的书,教人们如何追随耶稣,如何延伸至生活的每一部分,包括那些非常平凡的,比如吃饭,工作,休息,以及技术等. 它包括为各团体编写的讨论指南。 “牧师Jeremy Treat理解这种脱节。 在日常的分歧中,他拆除了有害的神圣-世俗鸿沟,这些鸿沟使许多基督徒感到精神上的分化,对信仰如何适用于平凡的生活并不确定,无法在我们的一生中充分享有基督。” 248页《上帝是我们的庇护与力量》:150个通过诗人威廉·博克斯坦(William Boekestein)和罗布·文图拉(Rob Ventura)发行的《真理之行》值得注意, 这张是随150个诗歌的每个诗篇的简短的奉献读物。 “你需要诗歌。 圣诗是圣经的奉献之心。 . . . . . . . 通过对所有150个诗作的简短、实用的阐述,本卷根据《新约》和耶穌基督所完成的工作,宣布、解释和适用每个诗句。” 在Amazon 公司购买, 我对本月推出的“SoulCare Groups”工作手册感到兴奋。 每项研究都是为期12周的团体研究,目的是与一些值得信赖的圣经辅导书籍一起使用。 前三卷收录了焦虑,悲伤和性完整性. “SoulCare GroupsTM是《一个计量部》的一本圣经咨询工作手册系列,它使教会有能力通过结构化的12周专题研究提供基于群体的护理。” 在亚马逊购买:焦虑 · 悲伤 · 教会及其历史书籍的性正直

articles.content: Good morning. My gratitude goes to Ligonier Ministries for sponsoring the blog this week to ensure you know about the new Grow app . It’s a free download and offers a lot of great content. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a variety of deals spanning a bunch of different eras and genres. Recommended Reading Jessica Lee writes about the growing no contact movement in which people sever their relationships with people they find toxic or problematic. I think of the young women I mentor who are flooded with reels, encouraging them that the best way to deal with the strained relationship with their mom is to put up higher boundaries that limit contact, or to cut off contact altogether. Even if they don’t take these drastic measures, they cannot help being influenced by the ideas, and neither can we. We are steeped in a therapy culture that talks a lot more about self-care than self-sacrifice, and we would be naive if we didn’t acknowledge the formative influence it has on us. And so, when relationships (whether with a parent, sibling, or friend) get hard, as they inevitably will, our first impulse is often toward self-preservation (putting up higher boundaries) and not self-sacrificial presence and faithfulness. Read: Going No Contact?: Ruth and Faithful Presence. Madeline Livingston has been going through a time of deep sorrow, and from that perspective writes a meditation about grief and glory. In my grief, I can turn to a Savior who has known human frailty and deep suffering, a Savior who in his most desperate moment prayed, “Let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will” ( Matthew 26:39 ). I can trust in the goodness and provision of a Father who did spare his own Son, but gave him up to rescue us and make us his own ( Romans 8:32 ). I can rest in the compassion of a Maker who collects all my tears in his bottle ( Psalm 56:8 ), a Good Shepherd who carries me safely through the lowest valley and restores my soul ( Psalm 23 ). As Sorrow and Suffering take me by the hand, they invite me to run to the solid ground of God’s promises made yes and amen through Christ. They urge me on to seek solace in the only place it can truly be found, in a arms of a Father who is my “refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble” ( Psalm 46:1 ). Read: When Sorrow & Suffering Take You by the Hand. Sarah Eekhoff Zylstra did a lot of interviews to try to arrive at some best practices for churches that are evangelistically effective. Her article offers a lot of food for thought. Thirty years ago, evangelical churches leaned on programs like Evangelism Explosion or Continuous Witness Training to deliver evangelistic focus and training, church leader Thom Rainer said. Those structured initiatives fit well in a culture that was more Christian and more institutionalized—it took an average of 20 church members to reach one person for Christ per year. Today, it takes 50, Rainer said. “Evangelism efficacy, evangelism effectiveness, has definitely diminished.” That trend is likely to continue. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. Read: Best Practices from Evangelistically Effective Churches. Like Darryl Dash, I’ve been hearing and reading a lot of doom and gloom lately, much of it related to the rise of AI. But also like Darryl, I don’t feel particularly alarmed. I read quite a few predictions of doom over the weekend, including some from self-professed tech optimists. Supposedly, some infrastructure in the United States is under attack. The idea is that AI is becoming too powerful and will overwhelm whatever safeguards we have in place to protect things like our water systems and electricity. The proposed solution is to prepare for the disaster by buying generators, solar panels for generators, and stockpiling water and other basic supplies. However, the authors acknowledge that there is little we can do to truly protect ourselves from the da
articles.content_zh: 早上好,你好吗? 感谢利戈尼耶各部赞助本周的博客, 这是免费的下载, 今天的销售和交易包括一系列跨越不同时代和流派的交易。 建议阅读 Jessica Lee写道,人们与他们发现有毒或有问题的人们断绝关系,但这种接触运动却在不断增加。 我想到那些我辅导的年轻女性,她们被卷轴淹没,鼓励她们,处理与母亲的紧张关系的最佳方式是设置更高的界限限制接触,或者完全切断接触. 即使他们不采取这些激烈的措施,他们也受不了这些想法的影响,我们也不能这样做。 我们身处一种治疗文化中,谈论自我护理比自我牺牲要多得多,如果我们不承认它对我们的形成影响,我们就会天真。 因此,当关系(无论是与父母、兄弟还是朋友的关系)变得困难时,我们的第一个冲动是往往朝向自我保护(提出更高的界限),而不是自我神圣的存在和忠诚。 读:去去不接触? 鲁斯和忠实的存在。 马德琳·利文斯通经历了一段深深的悲痛时期,从这个角度看,他写了一篇关于悲痛和荣耀的冥想. 在我悲痛中,我可以求助于一个知道人类脆弱和深重苦难的救世主,一个在他最绝望的时刻祈祷的救世主,“让这个杯子从我身边流过。 然而,不是我愿意,而是你愿意”(Matthew 26:39.). 我可以相信一个父亲的善良和供养,他确实饶了自己的儿子,但为了拯救我们而放弃了他,使我们成为自己的父亲(罗马8:32. 我可以安心地忍受一个造物主的怜悯,他把所有的眼泪都收在他的瓶中(诗篇56:8),一个好牧人,他把我安全地带入最底层的山谷并恢复我的灵魂(诗篇23. 当悲伤和受苦将我牵上手时,他们邀请我跑到上帝通过基督许下的承诺的坚实地步。 他们敦促我在一个真正能找到的地方寻求安慰,在一个父亲的怀抱中,他是我的“抵抗和力量,在困难中非常现成的帮助”(第46:1段)。 读取:"悲伤"和"受苦受难"由"手取""你"时. Sarah Eekhoff Zylstra做了很多访谈,试图为福音派有效的教堂达成一些最佳做法. 她的文章为思考提供了很多食物. 教会领袖汤姆·赖纳(Thom Rainer)说, 这些结构化的倡议非常适合一种更加基督教化和更加制度化的文化——平均每年需要20名教会成员为基督而接触一个人。 今天,它需要50,雷纳说。 “福音会的功效,福音会的功效,肯定已经下降。” 这一趋势很可能继续下去。 由于社交媒体和AI填补了我们的时间并增加了我们的社会焦虑,甚至连关系福音派也越来越困难. 读取:Evangelistic 有效教会的最佳做法。 与达里尔·达什(Darryl Dash)一样, 我最近也听到并阅读了许多末日与忧郁, 但与达里尔一样, 我读到很多关于周末末日的预言, 包括一些自以为是的技术乐观主义者的预言。 假设美国的一些基础设施受到攻击。 这个想法是AI正在变得太强大,并且会压倒我们现有的保护诸如我们的供水系统和电力之类的东西的保障措施. 拟议的解决办法是通过购买发电机、发电机太阳能电池板以及储存水和其他基本用品来为灾难做好准备。 然而,作者们承认,我们无法真正保护自己,使其免受歧视。
