articles.title_zh: 点菜（ 10月30日）
articles.content: Good morning. I am making my way home from Colorado today after a productive series of meetings and video shoots. I’ll look forward to a more normal week next week! In the meantime, be sure to check in tomorrow for Weekend A La Carte and on Sunday for a favorite feature, Works & Wonders. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include lots of interesting books like an exposition of the London Baptist Confession, some brief biographies of Christians you should know, and Thaddeus Williams’s book on reverence. Some of my books are 50% off at ChurchSource in their print editions: Visual Theology , A Visual Theology Guide to the Bible , and Pilgrim Prayers . Recommended Reading Time Flies—and Death Comes Speedily. The older you get, the more you come to understand that time flies and death comes speedily. “As teenagers, my friends and I were awash with youthful pride, poking fun at weighty things we knew little about—completely ignorant that our life here below is ‘a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes.’ The dew was still afresh upon our heads; the road of life unfurling in a great spool before our feet, disappearing into the far-off horizon. We could quote you verses here and there from the Scriptures, all the while being completely unversed in this point: “It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting, for this is the end of all mankind, and the living will lay it to heart.” In our minds, we could afford to mock death because we were, at the time, so far removed from it.” Was Piper Unprepared? A little while ago, John Piper indicated that he may have been unprepared for pastoral ministry when he began it. In this episode of Ask Pastor John , he is asked to explain what he meant by that. Take Your Faith Deeper with Ligonier’s Grow App. During a time of spiritual decline, God used the Protestant Reformation to bring renewal to His church through the recovery of the biblical gospel. This Reformation Day, explore the truths that fueled renewed devotion to God and His Word in the Grow app from Ligonier. Discover hundreds of Reformation-themed articles, video teaching series, and conference messages to help strengthen your faith and deepen your walk with Christ. Download the Grow app today. (Sponsored) The Engineering Behind Every Heartbeat. This is a celebration of the engineering of the human heart. “The human heart does not beat like a perfect clock. The time between beats changes as the body breathes, moves, rests, and reacts to the world around it. New research shows that these changes are part of a feedback system linking the heart, brain, and nerves. The heart keeps a steady rhythm while remaining flexible when needed, much like a well-built control system.” When You Trick-or-Treat, Nod to Martin Luther. Daniel Hyde writes in a local paper to explain to its readers the Protestant contribution to Halloween. “So, by all means, dress up and hand out the candy. When the doorbell rings, remember: The principle that no authority may command conscience protects the civil liberty of the religious and nonreligious alike.” God’s Left Hand. Bryce Waller: “The most difficult part about politics is what happens after the elections. In Romans 13:1, God calls us to be subject to these governing authorities—to obey the laws they pass, to show them honor and respect, to give them our hard-earned money by paying taxes. Voting is one thing, but submitting my life to a politician, showing respect to that guy , paying taxes to those people —even the people I didn’t choose? That’s not so easy.” These are good things to work out before an election since it will shape your response, whether you are happy with the results or dismayed. 17 Exhortations For Christian Citizens. On a somewhat related note, here are 17 exhortations for Christian citizens. “Bad government and national decline grieve those who love their country and bring a kind of chaos—a hard providence for Christian citizens. Yet even worse form

articles.title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有“万能钥匙”
articles.content: The first of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. A question of major importance is ‘How am I to live as a Christian’? It is one thing to be certain on biblical grounds that I have life from Christ, now I must be clear as to how I am to live the life of Christ. My purpose in setting before you some of the major principles of living the Christian life is three-fold: —I wish to sketch in a biblical theology of the Christian life. My purpose is unashamedly one of indoctrination. I wish by God’s help, by Spirit and word, to indoctrinate you in a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. —I wish to inoculate you and to immunize you against the major false views of the Christian life. Some of us desperately wish we had received such an inoculation early in our Christian experience. We spent many years chasing rabbits that we could never catch. We went after experiences and states of mind and heart in the hope that somehow in so doing we would find what it really meant to live as a Christian. —I wish to purge you of any existing misconceptions which you may presently have. It may not be pleasant but it is in your own best interests. We now examine these major principles of the Christian life. Principle 1: There is No One ‘Master Key’ to Living the Christian Life The kind of teaching I am purposing to focus upon in this principle goes something like this: There is a Christian who for many years has found himself in the doldrums. He has had his sails hoisted but he goes nowhere. It seems that he knows little of the wind of the Spirit filling his sails and carrying him anywhere. Or, to change the analogy, he may have his sails hoisted but they seem for ever to be full of holes, and while all around him have hoisted sails and appear to be making progress he seems to be going nowhere. And then one day at a conference or while reading a book or in his own devotions he comes across a passage of Scripture, say John chapter 15, and there he reads in the words of our Lord Jesus that beautiful analogy of the Christian’s relationship to Christ as the relationship of a branch to a vine. This so ignites his own spiritual life that he is almost overnight lifted to an entirely new plateau of spiritual vitality. Either the holes in his sails get mended or it is as though a mighty zephyr from God himself fills his sails, causing them to billow out to the full. He makes more substantial progress in the Christian life in six months than he has made in the previous six years. This man says that the master key to the Christian life is understanding John 15 and if others will only come to understand the concept of Christ’s relationship to his people as the branch and the vine are related they too will come to an entirely new plateau of spiritual vitality and reality in their Christian walk. Another example could be someone who has been struggling with a certain besetting sin which leaves him continually bowed down and crippled with guilt. Here is a young Christian struggling with a certain area of besetting sin, unknown to others, and he is constantly bogged down. His wheels are up to the hub-caps in mud, and no matter how much he changes the gears and pushes down on the accelerator he is spinning his wheels and all he is doing is using up petrol and making a mess. He is in that position for weeks and months perhaps, and then one day at a conference or reading a book or in his own devotions he comes to Romans, chapter 6, and he reads the glorious truth that in union with Jesus Christ all that he was as old man has been put to death, and in union with Jesus Christ the totality of the old life has been buried in Christ’s tomb and he is now a new man in Jesus Christ and he sees that he is called upon to reckon it so, and in the light of that, present himself as alive from the dead. 阿尔伯特·N·马丁在1984年班纳青年大会上发表的六篇包含教学内容的文章中的一篇文章,介绍了基督教生活的基本圣经神学. 一个非常重要的问题是:我如何作为一个基督徒活下来? 从圣经上确定我的生命来自基督是一回事,现在我必须明白我如何活基督的生命.
在你们面前,我提出一些关于基督教生活的主要原则,目的有三个方面:——我想在圣经中描绘基督教生活的神学. 我的目的就是毫不羞愧地教化别人 我希望通过上帝的帮助,通过精神和文字,将你灌输到基督教生活的基本圣经神学中去.
我希望为你们接种疫苗,并为你们接种疫苗,反对基督教生活中的重大错误观点。 我们当中有些人非常希望我们早期在基督教经验中得到这样的接种。 我们花了很多年 追赶我们永远抓不到的兔子
我们追寻经验 和精神状态和心境, 希望能找到作为基督徒生活的真正意义。 我希望清除你目前可能存在的任何误解。 这也许不愉快,但符合你的最佳利益。 我们现在审查基督教生活的这些主要原则。
然后有一天,在会议中,或者在读到一本书时,或者在自己的奉献中,他穿过了圣经的一行,如约翰·第15章,他用我们的主耶稣的话来读到,把基督教与基督的关系比作树枝与藤条的关系。
这如此点燃了他自己的精神生活,以至于几乎一夜之间被抬到一个全新的精神活力高地. 要么他的帆上有洞被修补好 要么就好像上帝亲自放出一个强大的快活器 来灌入他的帆上 让他们满地找牙 他在6个月里在基督教生活中取得了比前6年更大的实质性进步.
这个人说,基督教生活的主要关键在于理解约翰·15,如果其他人只了解基督与其人民的关系概念,因为树枝和藤蔓是相连的,他们也会在基督教行走中来到一个精神活力和现实的全新的高地。
另一个例子是,有人一直在为某种困扰他的罪行而挣扎,使他不断屈从并因罪恶而致残。 这里有一个年轻的基督教徒在挣扎着 某些困扰的罪恶领域, 其他人不知道, 他经常陷入困境。
他的车轮在泥地上被吊起,无论他如何改变齿轮并推倒了加速器,他正在旋转他的车轮,他所做的就是用上汽油并制造一团糟。

articles.content: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include books about the Old Testament, Proverbs, faithful presence, the life and influence of Tim Keller, and a whole lot more. Westminster Books is continuing their Reformation sale by offering discounts on ESV Bibles as well as the tremendous new 500th anniversary edition of Tyndale’s New Testament. Recommended Reading How the Mainstream Recruits for the Manosphere. Aaron Renn explains how “asymmetric blame, hectoring lectures, and selectively revived norms are driving young men to the influencers the mainstream condemns.” How Mental Illness Became an Identity. Myles Werntz has an interesting review of a new book by Fredrik deBoer that explains how mental illness became an identity. “Mental illness in the 21st century is an expanding category—and one increasingly dominated by its most functional and therefore visible members. That displacement—in our collective imagination and public discourse—of the profoundly mentally ill by my college students didn’t happen all at once. And how did it happen? Was it because of the closure of traditional mental hospitals, like those of One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest ? Was it because of the internet-driven phenomenon of self-diagnosis by very functional influencers? The marginalization of psychiatry as a profession? Or denial, romanticization, and politics?” It Can Happen Here, Too. “As numerous countries in Europe experience riots, many in America are asking, ‘What on earth is happening on the continent that was, in many ways, the cradle of Western civilization?’ As historic buildings, places of worship, and commercial properties combust before our eyes on the nightly news, how are we to make sense of this?” Carl Trueman warns that what’s happening in Europe could also happen in the United States. 8 Ways to Help Your Kids Love the Church. Shiphrah Lakka offers a series of ways to help your kids learn to love the church. “While discipleship at home is extremely important and something every Christian parent should pursue, it can never replace the church. Reading Scripture together, praying as a family, and teaching our children about God within our homes are vital practices. Yet God’s design for believers extends beyond the walls of our homes. He calls us to belong to a community of believers who worship, serve, and do life together.” I Hate Your Halloween Decorations. Marc Sims writes about the reality of Halloween today. “The next time I am out, we will really slow down to take in the diorama you set up of black hooded figures encircling a pentagram-alter with a fake infant set in the middle of it, that way he can become familiar with Satanic rituals and child sacrifice. I mean, where else is he going to get this important cultural experience? Apparently, you are under the impression that becoming desensitized to violence and death is an important step for our whole neighborhood to take in—to celebrate, even. Here, frumpy old Marc ( boooo! ) was worried about why our culture seems ever more eager to relish death and the demonic—but you have shown me that this is really just fun! Save a fake a corpse for me!” Why Paper Books Endure. Daniel Darling explains his ongoing love for paper books (even while he’s not entirely opposed to electronic ones). “When I began my writing career in the early 2,000s, every single writing conference I attended featured speakers who issued grave warnings. E-books would eventually take over. Paper books would be a thing of the past. Libraries are nice relics of another era. Except that didn’t happen.” Something Worth Doing These words by Maltbie Davenport Babcock have often been a challenge to me, and I wouldn’t be surprised if they challenge you as well. articles.title_zh: 使用人工智能色情片是罪过吗？
articles.content: Over the past two decades, I have written a great deal about pornography . At many different times and in many different forms, I have urged people to consider a long list of arguments against it. I’m thankful to have interacted with many people who have come to see pornography as evil and who have committed themselves to sexual purity. Some of the strongest and most effective arguments against using pornography are based upon the humanity of the people who are involved in it. So, for example, in “ 7 Good Reasons To Stop Looking at Porn Right Now ,” I wrote that we need to consider the cost to those who make it. “Pornography exacts a high cost of those who create it—the cost to their bodies, to their souls, to their mental well-being, to their dignity, to their future. A vast amount of the pornography you enjoy is created by people against their wills. The simple fact is, by watching porn, you are watching rape and deriving pleasure from it. You become a willing participant in sexual violence and you allow that actor on the screen to suffer for your pleasure.” Even if some pornography is consensual, a great deal of pornography is not, and the viewer cannot know which is which. Similarly, in “ 8 Sins You Commit Whenever You Look at Porn ,” I said that those who watch it are guilty of sexual assault. “A person who drives a getaway car for a band of bank robbers will rightly be charged with murder for anyone who is killed in committing that crime. The person who voluntarily watches sexual assault for purposes of titillation is rightly guilty of that sexual assault. And a nauseating quantity of pornography is violent in nature, displaying men taking advantage of women. Sometimes these women have volunteered for such degradation and sometimes they are forced or raped into it. To watch such horrifying smut is to be a participant in it and to bear the moral blemish of it.” While these are far from the only arguments against pornography, I believe they are especially effective ones. But what happens when the characters involved in pornography are no longer people? What happens when they no longer exist at all, but are merely generated by AI? Could AI allow us to create “ethical pornography” that solves one of the foremost concerns that come with “real” pornography? In other words, is it a sin to look at AI-generated porn ? (For our purposes, we will assume that we are already rejecting deepfake porn—using the likeness of an existing person—as morally repugnant and both immoral and illegal. Instead, we are considering images of people who are generated entirely by AI.) The simple answer is yes: it is as sinful to look at AI-generated porn as it is to look at human-created porn. While some of the arguments may not be as relevant, the majority are unchanged. Before I explain how and why, I want you to listen to a warning: we are all experts at circumventing the spirit of the law by abiding within the strict letter of the law. There is something deep within us that wants to defy the rules that are given to us, and we become skilled at justifying the ways we do this. Often this involves reducing morality to a strict binary, then convincing ourselves that because we have not blatantly broken the law, we have abided by it. This was exactly the sin of the Pharisees of Jesus’s day who would strictly tithe the spices they grew in their gardens, yet fail to live according to the higher principles of justice, mercy, and faithfulness. There is something of the Pharisee in each one of us. With that in mind, here are reasons why it is a sin to use pornography that has been generated by AI. You are still lusting , even if you are lusting after a person who exists only on a screen. To lust is to long for an illicit sexual pleasure, and to long for an illicit sexual pleasure is to find satisfaction in what God has forbidden. articles.content_zh: 在过去20年里,我写了很多关于色情的内容。 在许多不同的时刻,我以许多不同的形式敦促人们考虑一长串反对它的论点。 我很感激与许多人互动, 一些强烈而最有效的反对使用色情作品的论据是基于参与其中的人的人道. 因此,例如,在“停止看色情电影的7个好理由”中,我写道,我们需要考虑制作者的成本。 " 色情制品的制作者付出了高昂的代价 -- -- 他们的身体、灵魂、精神健康、尊严、未来的代价。 你所欣赏的大量色情作品都是由人们违背自己的意愿所创造的. 简单的事实是,通过看色情片, 你正在看强奸,并从中获得乐趣。 你成为性暴力的自愿参与者,你允许屏幕上那个演员为取悦而受苦。” 即使有些色情作品是合意的,但大量的色情作品却不是,观众也无法知道哪个是. 同样,在“每当你看到色情制品时,你就会犯下八起罪行”中,我说,观看色情制品的人犯有性侵犯罪。 “为一帮银行劫匪驾驶逃跑的汽车的人,将因犯下这种罪行而被杀害的人受到谋杀的指控。 自愿观看性攻击以达到抚慰目的的人理应犯有性攻击罪。 而令人恶心的色情作品数量在性质上是暴力的,展现出男性利用女性. 有时,这些妇女自愿从事这种有辱人格的工作,有时她们被迫或被强奸。 目睹这种令人发指的一团糟,就是参与其中,并承担其中的道德污点。” 虽然这些与反对色情制品的唯一论点相去甚远, 但是当参与色情的人物不再是人时会怎样呢? 当它们不再存在,而只是由AI产生时会发生什么? 大赦国际能否允许我们制造出“道德色情制品”,解决与“真正的”色情制品有关的最主要关切之一? 换句话说,看AI生成的色情片是不是罪过? (为了我们的目的,我们将假定,我们已经在拒绝利用像现有个人那样的深层假色情,认为这种色情在道德上是令人厌恶的,既不道德又非法。) 相反,我们正在考虑完全由大赦国际创造的人的形象。 ) 简单的回答是:看AI生成的色情片和看人造色情片一样罪恶. 虽然有些论点可能并不那么相关,但大多数论点没有改变。 在我解释方式和原因之前,我要你们聆听一个警告:我们都是通过遵守严格的法律条文来规避法律精神的专家。 我们内心深处有些东西想藐视赋予我们的规则,我们变得有技巧为我们这样做的方式辩护。 这往往涉及将道德降低为严格的二进制,然后说服自己,因为我们没有公然违法,我们遵守了法律。 这恰恰是耶稣时代的法利赛人的罪过,他们严格地说要将自己在花园所种的调味品的两倍之多,但却未能按照正义、慈悲和忠诚的更高原则活下来。 我们每个人都有法利赛人 考虑到这一点,以下是使用大赦国际制作的色情制品的罪责。 你仍然在贪欲, 即使你在贪欲 一个人只存在于屏幕上。 性欲是渴望非法的性快感,而渴望非法的性快感是寻求上帝所禁止的满足. 是为了让上帝之外的东西成为你欢乐的必备之物——在这种情况下,是性释放,而这种性释放会伴随着对一个...

articles.content: Good morning. May the Lord be with you and bless you today, my friends. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include lots of good books from New Growth Press and other publishers. Among them you’ll find several good options from Jared Wilson. Recommended Reading Goodbye, ‘Sam’s Club’ Megachurch. Hello, Stained Glass. Christianity Today reports on what I consider a welcome trend: church buildings that look like churches instead of warehouses. It begins this way: “Trinity Presbyterian finally has a church building of its own. That building has arches. And carved hammerbeams that tell the story of the Bible.” 3 Reasons Why Christians Should Lay “R.I.P.” to Rest. Nick Batzig thinks it would be best for Christians to lay R.I.P. to rest. “I’ve noticed something of a concerning trend over the past several years. It is the way in which believers speak about culture-impacting individuals at their deaths. Instead of simply expressing appreciation for their life and achievements, it has become commonplace for Christians to use the shorthand ‘R.I.P.’ (rest in peace) on social media when speaking of individuals in whose lives there was no evidence of saving grace at their death. At the risk of sounding ill-tempered, I wish to set out several reasons why I am troubled by this occurrence.” Go Deeper with Ligonier’s Grow App. Looking to put down roots in God’s Word? The Grow app from Ligonier Ministries gives you clear Bible teaching and guides your daily study for a deeper walk with Christ. Ministry Partners can also access the verse-by-verse notes from the Reformation Study Bible directly in the app and get reliable answers to their theological questions with the Ask Ligonier intelligent assistant. Not a Ligonier Ministry Partner yet? Try these features for 30 days when you download Grow and sign in. (Sponsored) Beauty Demands to Be Noticed. Michael Jensen is right: beauty demands to be noticed. He tells about people who understand the connection between beauty and transcendence and says, “Clearly, the reductive and polemical explanation of the atheists isn’t proving to be compelling. People can’t square their deeply felt experience of the world with that. To the people I’ve been speaking with, at least, the world simply cannot be reduced to its material components, nor can its coherence be explained by resorting to chance.” Aslan Sane: The Bowiefication of Narnia. I’ve got a pair of articles to share that comment on the forthcoming Narnia movies, each taking a different perspective. In the first, the writer remembers the old Narnia series from her childhood and bridges from there to what we know of the new one. She’s not impressed with it. Aslan and the Christians Who Can’t Be Enchanted. In the second, the author rebukes people like me (and the previous author) who have expressed concerns. He reminds us that it’s a movie for kids and that we don’t really know much about it yet. (I’d say he writes with some degree of exaggeration when he accuses me of losing my mind, but I’m glad to consider what he says nonetheless.) The Day of Pioneer Missions Is Not Over. Writing for Desiring God, my friend Tim Keesee wants us to know that the day of pioneer missions is not over. “Pioneer missionaries are still needed today because there are vast territories and high-rise megacities where the gospel message has yet to reach.” Videos Worth Watching Here are several brief videos that are worth your time. 5 Signs Your Church Might Be Too Seeker Sensitive. Adriel Sanchez explains seeker sensitivity and offers signs your church might lean too much in that direction and become seeker driven. How to Leave a Church Well. Hershael York speaks specifically to pastors to explain how and when to leave a church well. The Enduring Word. This short film from Crossway celebrates God’s providence through the history of Bible translation. Flashback What’s The Point Of Family Devotions? articles.title_zh: 本周基督教书籍（ 2026年10月27日）
articles.content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. This week brings a substantial new commentary on the Westminster Confession of Faith from a whole team of Reformed scholars, an updated edition of a well-known apologetics book, a couple of books for kids, and a new edition of the ESV. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. (This is a new feature I trialed last week. The response was positive, so I’m going to keep it going. I have tried to improve the format and layout to make it easier to read.) Books for Everyone Crossway The Westminster Confession of Faith A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application Edited by J. V. Fesko, John R. Muether, and D. Blair Smith Endorsed by: Joel R. Beeke, Michael Horton, Keith A. Mathison, Robert Letham, and Jonathan L. Master Publisher’s description What is Reformed theology? In 1646, a group of theologians composed what is arguably the most comprehensive statement of faith, the Westminster Confession. Their efforts to preserve Protestant theology against opposing beliefs endured. Today, amid growing interest in Reformed Christianity, the Westminster Confession remains an indispensable guide for living out doctrine, worship, and church governance sola Scriptura, “by Scripture alone.” This essential collection of essays presents an accessible guide to the Westminster Confession of Faith for 21st-century readers. Each chapter is devoted to a section of the historic document, carefully studying its context, its significance to the faith, and its application, as well as any controversies. Clear, thorough explanations of principles, including the Trinity, creation, providence, baptism, last judgment, and more, make this the definitive guide on Reformed Christian doctrine. The essays are written by faculty from Reformed Theological Seminary in their areas of expertise, ensuring a trustworthy and high-quality text for church leaders, teachers and students of theology, and laypeople. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . Crossway I Don’t Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist Updated Edition Norman L. Geisler and Frank Turek Endorsed by: Gavin Ortlund, Sean McDowell, Gregory Koukl, Alisa Childers, and Josh Howerton Publisher’s description To some, the concept of having faith in a higher power or a set of religious beliefs is nonsensical. Indeed, many view religion in general, and Christianity in particular, as unfounded and unreasonable. Frank Turek and Norman Geisler argue, however, that Christianity is not only more reasonable than all other belief systems but is indeed more rational than unbelief itself. With conviction and clear thinking, Turek and Geisler guide readers through some of the traditional, tested arguments for the existence of a creator God. They move into an examination of the source of morality and the reliability of the New Testament accounts concerning Jesus. The final section of the book deals with a detailed investigation of the claims of Christ. This updated volume with fresh arguments will be an interesting read for those skeptical about Christianity, as well as a helpful resource for Christians seeking to articulate a more sophisticated defense of their faith. Buy it at Amazon . Baker Books Giver of All Good God as the Beginning and End of Ethics Chase R. Kuhn Publisher’s description Where do our ethics come from? Are they based on unchanging realities or subject to revision as human culture develops and changes? What distinguishes Christian ethics from other moral claims? And how can Christians engage these questions with clarity and confidence—without either abandoning their convictions or abandoning the conversation? In Giver of All Good , Chase R. Kuhn argues that the answer begins not with ourselves—our feelings, our culture, our moral intuitions—but with God. What we believe about God shapes how we live. Our theology guides
articles.content_zh: 星期二是大多数出版商发行新书的一天,所以每周我都会告诉你,我最密切地关注的出版商刚刚给我们带来了什么。 本周来自整群改革派学者对"威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔"(Westminster Confession of Faith)提出了实质性的新评论,并更新了一出名作"通俗小说"(Apologetics Book),一出给孩子们的几本书和一出"ESV"的新版本. 每一次,我都包括出版商的描述。 (这是上星期我试演的新节目) 回应是积极的, 我努力改进格式和布局,使其更容易阅读。 ) 由J. V. Fesko、John R. Muether和D. Blair Smith编辑, 乔尔·R·比克、Michael Horton、Keith A. Mathison、Robert Letham和Jonathan L. Master Publishers对改革神学的描述。 1646年,一群神学家组成了可以说是最全面的信仰声明"威斯敏斯特忏悔". 他们努力保护新教神学,反对对立的信仰。 如今,在对改革后的基督教越来越感兴趣的情况下,威斯敏斯特忏悔仍然是“仅靠圣经”活出学说、崇拜和教会治理的不可或缺的指南。 这份重要的散文集为21世纪的读者提供了威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔的可获取指南. 每一章都专门讨论历史文件的一节,仔细研究其背景、其对信仰的意义、其应用以及任何争议。 对原则,包括"三一","创造","天赐","受洗","最后的判断"等进行明确,彻底的解释,使这成为"改革后基督教学说"的决定性指南. 论文由改革神学院的教师在其专业领域撰写,确保教会领导人、神学教师和学生以及外行者能够获得可靠和高质量的文本。 在亚马逊或威斯敏斯特书店买的 Crossway I don't have enough Faith to be an Atheist 更新版 Norman L. Geisler and Frank Turek 由加文·奥尔特伦德,肖恩·麦克道威尔,格雷戈里·库克尔,艾莉莎·柴尔德斯和乔什·豪尔顿出版商的描述认可 对一些人来说,对更高权力或一套宗教信仰有信仰的概念是没有意识的. 事实上,许多人认为,一般宗教,特别是基督教,是毫无根据和不合理的。 然而,弗兰克·图雷克和诺曼·盖斯勒(Norman Geisler)认为,基督教不仅比所有其他信仰体系更合理,而且确实比不信本身更合理. 以信念和清晰的思考,图雷克和盖斯勒指导读者通过一些传统的,经过考验的关于创造出神存在的论点. 他们开始研究道德渊源和"新约"中有关耶稣的叙述的可靠性. 该书的最后一节详细论述对基督的主张的调查. 这本附有新论点的增订本,对于那些对基督教持怀疑态度的人来说,将是一个有趣的读物,也是基督教徒寻求更尖端地捍卫其信仰的有用资源。 在亚马逊买的 Baker Books of All Good God的出品人作为伦理学的开始和结束 Chase R. Kuhn出版社的描述 我们的道德从何而来? 它们是建立在不断变化的现实基础上,还是随着人类文化的发展和变化而需要加以修改? 基督教道德与其他道德主张有什么区别? 基督徒如何以明确和自信的方式处理这些问题,而不放弃他们的信念或放弃对话? Chase R. Kuhn指出,答案不是从我们自己开始的——我们的感情、我们的文化和我们的道德直觉——而是从上帝开始的。 我们对上帝的信仰 塑造了我们的生活 我们的神学指南

articles.title_zh: 九十五条论点是什么？
articles.content: On October 31, 1517, Martin Luther, now in his mid-thirties, made his way to the Castle Church in Wittenberg and posted his Ninety-Five Theses on the church door. Originally intended as propositions for public debate, the theses were written in Latin—the language of the scholar, not of the street. Luther could have had no idea that they would echo around Europe and become the catalyst for a spiritual revolution. Many of those who saw the papers on the Castle Church door—which seems to have served as a public notice board—would not have been able to read Latin. But soon the theses were translated into German and thereafter spread throughout Europe like wildfire—indeed, like an “act of God.” What were the Ninety-Five Theses? They were statements aimed directly at specific corruptions in the church of Luther’s day, many of them related to issues of pardon, purgatory, and the power of the pope. The first of them was particularly startling: By saying “Repent,” our Lord and Master Jesus Christ willed that the whole of the life of believers should be repentance. (Dominus et magister noster Iesus Christus dicendo “Poenitentiam agite etc.” omnem vitam fidelium poenitentiam esse voluit.) Luther had grasped that the Vulgate translation of “Repent” ( poenitentiam agite ) was open to the misinterpretation “Do penitence (or penance).” And he had also grasped a principle that John Calvin would later expound with great clarity: penitence or repentance is not the action of a moment; it is the turning around of a life—the rejection of sin effected by the gracious work of the Holy Spirit. It cannot therefore be a single act completed in a moment; it is a style of life that lasts until glory. Luther led a full and adventurous life that only an extensive biography can well describe. He was a remarkable man with enormous God-given energy. His speech was direct and plain and not infrequently earthy. He was a teacher of theology, a preacher of the gospel, and an author of some of the most important books in the Reformation period. Notable among his early publications was his On the Babylonian Captivity of the Church , which exposed the church’s failures, while in On the Freedom of a Christian he explained how in Jesus Christ believers are set free both to love God and to serve their neighbor. Thus he wrote in a beautifully crafted sentence that captures the paradox of the gospel-centered life: “A Christian man is the most free lord of all, and subject to none; a Christian man is the most dutiful servant of all, and subject to everyone.” By his preaching, by writing, and especially by his influence in the explanation of salvation by grace through faith in Christ, Luther was used by God to transform the Christian church. The leading Reformers in England and Scotland were influenced by his writings, often smuggled in by merchant sailors. In Scotland in particular, the martyrs of St. Andrews, Patrick Hamilton and George Wishart (whose bodyguard John Knox had been), were disciples of Luther’s teaching. Likewise in England, the heroic William Tyndale left a legacy not only in his English translation of the Bible but in an entire body of literature that echoed the German Reformer’s work. But what did Luther teach? His chief emphases are aptly summarized in the well-known Reformation solas: (1) sola Scriptura : we come to know God through Scripture alone, not through the traditions of the church as such; (2) sola gratia : we come to receive forgiveness by God’s grace alone, not because we are able to earn merit; (3) sola fide: we receive justification by faith alone, and not by faith plus something else; (4) solus Christus : all of God’s riches are given to us in Christ alone; (5) soli Deo gloria: the goal of all of life is the glory of God alone. These principles simply underlined the emphases Luther found in Scripture. But in context, what is most significant about them is not only what they stressed but what they bypassed. Neither Luther nor the other mag
articles.content_zh: 1517年10月31日,现在已30多岁的马丁·路德(Martin Luther)前往维滕贝格的城堡教堂并把他的"九十五部曲"张贴到教堂门上. 这些论文最初是打算作为公众辩论的命题,是用拉丁文写的——学者的语言,而不是街上的语言。 路德根本不知道他们会在欧洲周围呼应,成为精神革命的催化剂. 许多人在城堡教堂门上看到报纸, 但很快,这些论文被翻译成德文,然后像野火一样传遍了欧洲,事实上,就像“上帝的行为 ” 。 "九五传"是什么? 这些言论直接针对路德节教堂的具体腐败,其中许多涉及赦免、炼狱和教宗权力等问题。 其中第一个特别令人吃惊:我们的主和耶稣基督大师说“忏悔”,希望信士们的一生都能悔过。 (Dominus et magister noster Iesus Christus dicendo “Poenitentiam angite等”。 Poenitiam intentium sese voluit。) 路德已经明白,“悔改”的Vulgate译文(poenitentiam angite)对“悔改(或忏悔)”的错误解释持开放态度。 他还理解了约翰·卡尔文后来将非常明确地阐明的原则:忏悔或忏悔不是一瞬间的行动;而是生命的转折——圣灵的慷慨工作对罪恶的拒绝。 因此,它不能是一个在一瞬间完成的单一行为;它是一种直到荣耀的生活方式。 路德过着充实而冒险的生活,只有广泛的传记才能很好地描述. 他是一个了不起的人 拥有巨大的上帝赐予的能量。 他的演讲是直截了当的,而且并非经常是土生土长的。 曾任神学教师,"福音"传道人等职,并出自"改革时期一些最重要的著作". 在他早期的著作中,著名的是他的《关于教会的巴比伦式控制》,该书揭露了教会的失败,而在《基督教自由》中,他解释了耶稣基督信徒如何获得自由,既爱上帝,又为邻居服务。 因此,他用一个精心设计的句子写道:“一个基督教徒是所有人中最自由的领主,不受任何人支配;一个基督教徒是所有人中最忠诚的仆人,服从每一个人。” 通过他的传道,写作,特别是他通过对基督的信仰,对恩典解释救赎的影响,路德被上帝用来改造基督教会. 英格兰和苏格兰的主要改革者受到他所著作的影响,经常被商船水手偷运入去. 特别是在苏格兰,圣安德鲁斯,帕特里克·汉密尔顿和乔治·怀克特(他的保镖约翰·诺克斯曾是)的烈士是路德教的门徒. 同样,在英国,英勇的威廉·廷达勒不仅在圣经的英文译本中留下了遗产,而且在与德国改革者著作相呼应的整个文献中也留下了遗产. 但路德教的是什么? 他的主要重心在著名的"改革"(Reformation solas)中得到了恰当的总结:(1) sola Scriptura:我们通过《圣经》,而不是通过教会的传统来了解上帝;(2) sola 惠给:我们通过上帝的恩惠来获得宽恕,而不是因为我们能够获得功绩;(3)  sola 敬畏:我们通过信仰获得理由,而不是信仰获得其他的东西;(4) Solus Christus:神的所有财富都只由基督给予我们;(5) Soli Deo Gloria:所有生命的目标都是上帝的光荣. 这些原则只是强调《圣经》中路德的强调。 但就背景而言,它们最重要的不仅是它们强调的内容,而且是它们所绕过的内容。 无论是路德还是其他的弹匣

articles.title_zh: 退休人员为教会服务的5种方式
articles.content: “Retirement at last! Now I can sleep as late as I want to. Now I get to do nothing all day.” Such is a popular description of how retirement looks to many people. I know some who would even add, “Now I get to play golf every day.” Obviously, this does not reflect the Christian perspective of someone who understands that his chief end is “to glorify God and enjoy Him forever” (see Westminster Shorter Catechism 1; 1 Cor. 10:31; Rom. 11:36). This is not to say that sleeping later and playing golf are anti-Christian. However, there are some significant ways that retirees can still serve the church. 1. Be a volunteer. Retirees have valuable practical and professional experience that can be used in service to others. For example, some of you may have skill sets and expertise that enable you to erect a building or a cabin at a camp from the ground up in very little time. One organization I’m familiar with travels to camps and other locations, bringing their own living accommodations, tools, and know-how to be a blessing to other ministries. Some may volunteer in maintenance of a church’s lawns and gardens to keep them looking tidy. Volunteers can save churches and various ministries a great deal of money and provide much encouragement to them. The church where I attend has many volunteers (both retired and pre-retired) who help at the annual church youth camps. They serve in the kitchen and dining hall, as cabin staff and counselors, as camp nurses and in technical positions, and pay their own way to camp. While not everyone can serve in such physical ways, everyone can volunteer in some way according to their abilities and gifts: “As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another . . . in order that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ” (1 Peter 4:10–11). 2. Show the younger generations a model of an older person who still walks with the Lord. The youth in our churches need models of older believers who are faithful in their daily walk with the Lord. What might this example look like? We can show that we have not waned in faithfulness in our older years, that we are active and unashamed to belong to God’s people, and that we continue to radiate joy in our relationship with the Lord. We can model what it looks like to have no hesitation to speak about Christ in the doctor’s office, store, or when traveling, and that we are not reluctant to share Scripture with other people. Paul wrote to the saints in Philippi: “Brothers, join in imitating me, and keep your eyes on those who walk according to the example you have in us” (Phil. 3:17). Note these words from the psalmist: O God, from my youth you have taught me, and I still proclaim your wondrous deeds. So even to old age and gray hairs, O God, do not forsake me, until I proclaim your might to another generation. (Ps. 71:17–18) 3. Regularly attend worship services and wholeheartedly participate. Not only should retirees maintain a faithful walk with the Lord, but they ought to remain consistent in their attendance at the regular worship services of the church. It is a testament to the Lord’s faithfulness when they are seen in the pews, not just taking up space or putting in their time, but wholeheartedly and enthusiastically singing, listening, and note-taking. This is important because it seems that many young people today view church as optional rather than a joyful habit. Granted, this should begin with the influence of godly parents, but it is reinforced and aided when the testimony of the older generation displays undiminished love for corporate worship, viewing it not as drudgery but delight. Hebrews 10:23–25 instructs us in this way: Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who promised is faithful. And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near. 4. Teach or assist thos
articles.content_zh: “终于退休了! 瞷и何眔边 现在我整天什么都不做。” 这是许多人对退休的看法的流行描述。 我知道有些人甚至会说,“现在我每天都要打高尔夫。” 显然,这并没有反映基督教的观点,即有人理解,他的主要目的就是“颂扬上帝,永远享受他”(见Westminster Shorter Catechism 1; 1 Cor. 10:31; Rom. 11:36)。 这不是说睡觉后打高尔夫是反基督教的。 然而,退休人员仍然可以有一些重要的方式为教会服务. 1. 志愿工作。 退休人员具有宝贵的实践和专业经验,可用于为他人服务. 例如,你们中有些人可能拥有技能和专门知识,能够在极短的时间内从地上建起一座建筑物或一个小木屋。 我熟悉一个组织前往营地及其他地点, 有些人会自愿维护教堂的草坪和花园, 志愿者可以挽救教会和各部一大笔钱,并为它们提供很大的鼓励. 我所在的教堂有许多志愿者(既有退休的,也有退休前的),他们在每年的教堂青年营中提供帮助. 他们在厨房和餐厅服务,担任木屋工作人员和咨询员,担任营地护士和技术职务,并支付自己去营地的方式。 虽然并非每个人都能以这样的身体方式服务,但每个人都能根据自己的能力和天赋以某种方式自愿: " 由于每个人都收到礼物,利用礼物互相服务,以使上帝在一切事情上都能被耶稣基督所赞美" (1 Peter 4:10-11). 2. 向年轻一代展示仍然与主同道的老年人的模范. 我们教会中的青年需要老信徒的模范,他们在每天与上帝一起行走时是忠实的。 这个例子会是什么样子? 我们可以表明,我们年事已高,在忠诚中并不衰弱,我们积极而且毫不羞愧地属于上帝的子民,而且我们继续在与上帝的关系中放出欢乐。 我们可以在医生的办公室、商店或旅行时, 以毫不犹豫的方式谈论基督, 保罗在Philippi给圣徒们写了一封信:“兄弟们,一起模仿我,并注意那些按照你们在我们身上的榜样行走的人”(Phil. 3:17)。 请注意,这些话来自诗人:上帝啊,你从我的青春中教我的,我仍然宣布你的奇事。 所以,上帝啊,即使老去和灰发,也不要抛弃我,直到我向另一代人宣告你的力量。 3. 定期参加礼拜仪式并全心全意地参加。 退休人员不仅应当与主保持忠实的行走,而且他们应当始终如一地参加教会的定期礼拜服务. 这证明了上帝的忠诚,当人们看到他们出现在树上时,他们不仅占据了空间或投入了时间,而且全心全意地歌唱、聆听和记事。 这一点很重要,因为今天许多年轻人似乎将教堂视为可选的习惯,而不是令人高兴的习惯. 当然,这应该从上帝父母的影响入手,但是当年长者的证词显示对企业崇拜的爱不减时,它得到了加强和帮助,认为它不是劳累,而是快乐。 希伯来人10:23-25这样教导我们:让我们不动摇地坚持我们的希望的忏悔,因为承诺的人是忠实的。 让我们考虑一下如何相互激起爱和善行,而不是像有些人的习惯那样忽视相会,而是相互鼓励,正如你们看到的日子临近的时候一样。 4. 教育或援助托斯人

articles.title_zh: 这五个唯独对今天的教会仍然重要吗？
articles.content: The five solas (Latin for “alone”) of the Reformation—Scripture alone, grace alone, faith alone, Christ alone, to the glory of God alone—are indispensable for the church in any era. They will always be relevant because they summarize the biblical gospel, which is the church’s lifeblood in every age. They are particularly significant today because even professing evangelicals, to say nothing of the culture around us, are being tempted to abandon the gospel. Therefore, the church must recognize the dire need of not only defending the five solas but also celebrating them. The five solas are important for us today for at least three reasons. 1. The five solas set apart the true gospel from every other religion, worldview, or philosophy. Every day, the world calls out its siren song of spiritual compromise. Satan loves to negotiate the nonnegotiables of biblical truth. He whispers the lie that we don’t need to have strong convictions about the Bible as our only standard of truth or hold firm to the teaching that only those who trust Christ alone for salvation are right with God. The temptation to downplay doctrine is unceasing. A winsome but unyielding grasp of the five solas can help us resist these attractive lies. 2. The five solas provide us with unspeakable comfort in a chaotic world. The pace of modern life is unsustainable. It colors our understanding of “the normal Christian life.” We tend to equate busyness in ministry with productiveness for Jesus. But the two must not be confused. Knowing that we are saved by God’s grace alone through faith alone gives us rest from an exhausting world. We leave behind a performance mindset in our relationship with God and embrace a life of trusting, resting grace. Safe in the arms of our Savior, we are set free to let go of trying to earn what God freely gives us—Christ Himself. 3. The five solas remind us that our salvation is secure. Only when we are assured of the love of God will we live out the commands of God. The five solas enable us to say with David, “Oh how I love your law! It is my meditation all the day” (Ps. 119:97). Following Jesus, obeying Him by the Spirit, and killing sin become our joy. So many Christians drift, unconsciously most of the time, to the belief that God loves them when they obey. But the true gospel of the five solas pulls us back to the bedrock scriptural truth that God loves us and therefore we obey. The difference is subtle, but it makes all the difference in our daily lives. Your Father loves you! He is pleased with you in Christ. When those realities come home, John’s words become our delightful creed: “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments. And his commandments are not burdensome” (1 John 5:3). In sum, nothing is more urgent for the church than protecting, propagating, and passing on the true gospel encapsulated by the five solas . It is our only hope, our greatest comfort, and our supreme joy. Most of all, these biblical teachings will always be important because they bring us to Christ, who is our life. 1 Footnotes Editor's Note: This article was originally published January 19, 2022. ↩
articles.content_zh: 改革的五所索拉斯(拉丁语为“单独”)——光是文字、光是恩典、光是信仰、光是基督、光是上帝的光荣——在任何时代,对教会都是不可或缺的。 因为他们总结了圣经福音, 它们今天特别重要,因为甚至宣称福音派教徒 -- -- 更不用说我们周围的文化 -- -- 被诱惑放弃福音。 因此,教会必须认识到,不仅迫切需要捍卫五个独奏会,而且迫切需要庆祝它们。 五个索拉斯今天对我们很重要,至少有三个原因。 1. 这五所索拉斯将真正的福音与所有其他宗教、世界观或哲学分开。 世界每天都在呼唤着它的精神妥协之歌。 撒旦喜欢商议圣经中不可谈判的真理. 他低语地说,我们不需要对《圣经》作为我们唯一的真理标准抱有坚定的信念,也不要坚持这样的教导,即只有那些只相信基督的人才能与上帝同在。 轻描淡写理论的诱惑是不停的。 能够帮助我们抵制这些有吸引力的谎言。 2. 在一个混乱的世界中,这五相声给我们带来了难以形容的安慰。 现代生活的步伐是不可持续的。 它体现了我们对“正常的基督教生活”的理解。 我们往往把部长的繁忙与耶稣的生产力等同起来。 但两者不可混淆. 仅凭信仰,我们就能从一个疲惫的世界中安息。 在与上帝的关系中,我们留下了一种表现的心态,并拥抱一种信任和安息的恩典的生活。 在我们的救世主的怀抱中,我们被放任去试图获得上帝给我们的自由——基督。 3. 五相声提醒我们,我们的救赎是安全的。 只有当我们得到上帝的爱的保证时,我们才会遵守上帝的命令。 这五相相声使我们能够和大卫说:“我多么爱你的律法! 我一整天都在冥想”(临119:97)。 顺从耶稣,顺从他的精神,杀戮罪孽成为了我们的喜悦. 如此多的基督徒在无意识中大部分时间漂移到相信上帝在他们服从时爱他们. 但是,五相声的真正福音让我们回到上帝爱我们,因此我们服从的基础性文字真理. 区别是微妙的,但它使我们日常生活中的一切不同。 你父亲爱你! 他在基督里对你感到高兴 当这些现实回到故乡时,约翰的话成了我们令人愉快的信念:“这是上帝的爱,我们遵守他的戒律。 他的戒律不是累赘的"(1 John 5:3). 总而言之,对教会来说,最紧迫的莫过于保护、宣传、传递由五所索拉斯所封印的真正福音。 这是我们唯一的希望,我们最大的慰藉,和我们最大的快乐。 最重要的是,这些圣经教义将永远是重要的,因为它们把我们带到基督那里,而基督是我们的生命. 1 脚注编辑注:本文章最初于2022年1月19日发表. .

articles.title_zh: 黑暗之后，光明
articles.content: In the old city of Geneva, Switzerland, there is a large park on the grounds of the University of Geneva that commemorates the Reformation. That park is adorned with a huge wall, called the International Monument to the Reformation or simply the Reformation Wall. In statues and bas-reliefs, the wall depicts figures from the Reformation including John Calvin, John Knox, William Farel, and Theodore Beza. Surrounding these and other statues, the motto of the Reformation is inscribed on each side: post tenebras lux —after darkness, light. This phrase refers not only to the unveiling and liberation of the Scriptures—which were made available to the common people during the Reformation—but also to the loss and recovery of the most important biblical doctrine there is: the doctrine of justification by faith alone. This was the primary and central issue of the Protestant Reformation. During the dispute between the Protestants and the Roman Catholics, both sides saw that justification was so important that no compromise was possible. Both sides were convinced that what was at stake in the doctrine of justification was the very essence of the biblical gospel. When the gospel is at stake, everything is at stake, because the gospel tells us how we can be right with God. In Galatians 1:6–9, Paul writes about the importance of getting the gospel right: I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting him who called you in the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel—not that there is another one, but there are some who trouble you and want to distort the gospel of Christ. But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach to you a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be accursed. As we have said before, so now I say again: If anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to the one you received, let him be accursed. This Apostle was a man who was constantly extolling the virtues of patience, gentleness, meekness, charity, and tolerance; who, conversely, constantly rebuked the sins of contentiousness, divisiveness, quarrelsome spirits, belligerence, and so on. This man said that we ought to strive as much as we possibly can to live at peace with all men; he was known as the Apostle of peace and unity. Yet suddenly he came to a point over a doctrine where he said, “There can be no toleration here. To tolerate the distortion of the gospel into another gospel is to tolerate the intolerable.” The first thing that Paul did was express his amazement—not that the people had left the gospel that he had preached to them, but that they had done it so quickly. He was hardly gone from their midst before they wanted to listen to the teachings of the Judaizers, who insisted that one cannot be saved by faith in Christ alone but must also have good works and obedience to the law in order to be saved. This “other gospel” was no gospel at all—there is only one gospel, the gospel of God, revealed in and through Christ and proclaimed and expounded by the Apostles. The stakes are so high when it comes to this point that Paul pronounced a curse on anyone who teaches otherwise. The Greek work translated “accursed” is anathema —damned. The Apostle understood that the issue of justification was no mere academic issue, but one that touches every person’s life ultimately. It can be summed up in one question: How are we saved? It is a life-and-death matter, an eternal life matter. The New Testament makes it clear that each of us will be called into account before God, and that God is righteous while we’re not. The doctrine of justification addresses the solution to that problem, declaring how we, as unjust people, can be reconciled to a just and holy God. So if there’s anything in the essence of the Christian faith, of the good news of the gospel, it’s this doctrine. Martin Luther, building on Paul’s assessment, called the doctrine of justification the article on which the church stands or falls. Luther understood that theology is syste
articles.content_zh: 在瑞士日内瓦老城区,日内瓦大学地上有一座大型公园来纪念"改革". 那个公园的装饰有一堵巨大的墙,被称作"改革国际纪念碑"或"改革墙". 在雕像和堡垒救济中,墙上描绘了来自改革派的人物,包括约翰·卡尔文,约翰·诺克斯,威廉·法雷尔和西奥多·贝扎. 围绕这些和其他雕像,"改革"的座右铭被刻在了每一边:后倒行奢侈——在黑暗后,光辉. 这一短语不仅指《圣经》的揭幕和解放(在改革期间提供给普通人民),而且还指最重要的圣经学说 -- -- 仅以信仰为理由的学说 -- -- 的丧失和复苏。 这是新教改革的首要和核心问题。 在新教徒和罗马天主教徒之间的纠纷中,双方认为这种辩解非常重要,不可能妥协. 双方都相信,辩护理论的关键在于圣经福音的精髓。 当福音受到威胁时,一切都处于危险之中,因为福音告诉我们,我们如何能够与上帝对齐。 在加拉提亚1:6-9中,保罗写道正确福音的重要性:我感到惊讶的是,你如此快地抛弃了以基督之恩召唤你并转向另一个福音的人,而不是另一个福音,但有些人烦恼你并想歪曲基督的福音。 即使我们或从天上降下的天神,为你们传福音,与我们所传教你们的福音相悖,教他受诅咒。 正如我们以前说过的,现在我再说一遍: 如果有人向你们宣扬与你们所接受的福音相悖的福音,你们就应当诅咒他。 这名使徒是一个不断赞颂耐心、温和、温柔、慈善和宽容等美德的人;相反,他不断斥责争议、分裂、争吵、好战等罪恶。 这位先生说,我们应该尽我们所能地同所有人和平相处;他被称为和平与团结的使者。 然而,他突然想到一个理论,他说,“在这里是不能容忍的。 容忍将福音歪曲为又一福音就是容忍不能容忍的福音。” 保罗做的第一件事是表达他的惊叹——不是说人民已经离开了他向他们所宣扬的福音,而是他们如此快地做到了. 在他们想听犹太教的教义之前,他几乎没有离开他们中间,犹太教坚持一个人不能只靠信仰基督而得到救赎,为了得到救赎,他还必须有善行并服从法律. 这种 " 其他福音 " 根本不是福音 -- -- 只有一种福音,即上帝的福音,在基督中和通过基督揭示,并由使徒们宣布和阐述。 此时此刻,利害攸关,以致于保罗对教别的人发出诅咒. 希腊翻译的作品“被诅咒了”是令人厌恶的。 使徒们明白,理由问题不仅仅是学术问题,而是一个最终触及每个人生活的问题。 它可以概括为一个问题:我们如何得到拯救? 这是生死攸关的 永生攸关的 《新约》明确指出,在上帝面前,我们每一个人都将受到重视,上帝是善良的,而我们不是正义的。 辩解的理论涉及这个问题的解决,宣布我们作为不公正的人民如何能够与一个公正和神圣的上帝相协调。 因此,如果有基督教信仰的本质,福音的好消息,那就是这个学说。 马丁·路德(Martin Luther)根据保罗的评估,称教会所立足或倒下的文章为辩解理论. 路德知道神学是循环的

articles.summary_zh: 西奥多·贝扎（ Theodore Beza ）今天在福音派世界中是一个陌生的人物。他受到许多历史学家和神学家的诽谤，他们创造了一个严肃的人的形象，他将加尔文的神学变成了一个干旱的学术体系。这张照片实际上与事实相去甚远。那么西奥多·贝扎到底是谁？他于1519年出生于法国韦泽莱，是一个富裕的法国小贵族家庭。他的一生几乎跨越了整个十六世纪，他于1605年去世，享年八十多岁。
articles.title_zh: 西奥多·贝扎是谁？
articles.content: Theodore Beza is an unfamiliar figure today in the evangelical world. He has been much maligned by many historians and theologians who created the image of an austere man who turned Calvin’s theology into an arid scholastic system. This image is actually very far from the truth. So who was Theodore Beza really? He was born in Vézelay, France, in 1519 in an affluent family of the minor French nobility. His life spanned almost the whole sixteenth century, and he died in 1605 at the age of eighty-six. By God’s providence, there were two clear turning points in his life. The first occurred at the age of nine when he was placed as a lodger with a Lutheran scholar, Melchior Wolmar, who became his preceptor. He spent seven years with Wolmar, who taught him law, Latin, and Greek. Interestingly, one of Wolmar’s other students during that time was none other than Calvin, who was just ten years older than Beza. Wolmar gave Beza a first-rate education, and, like Calvin, Beza was likely more fluent in Latin than in French. More importantly, Wolmar was instrumental in his journey toward the new Reformed faith. It was through Wolmar that, sometime around 1535, Beza read a book by the Swiss Reformer Heinrich Bullinger and was converted. Years later, Beza wrote to Bullinger: “You made known to me true piety, and its purest source: The Word of God.” 1 However, Beza had a lot to lose if he disclosed his newfound faith. He received substantial ecclesiastical incomes through one of his uncles, who was an abbot, and this allowed him to enjoy a life of pleasure in Paris, dedicating himself to poetry and humanistic studies. For several years, he kept his faith secret, and he secretly married Claudine Denosse, the daughter of a Parisian Protestant merchant. Beza promised he would marry her publicly whenever they could find a truly Reformed church. The second turning point of his life came in 1548 when he contracted the plague and came close to death. He took it as a clear warning from God and came out openly about his faith. Shortly after, he fled to Geneva. Theodore and Claudine were publicly married by Calvin himself, and they remained devoted to each other and to the cause of Christ until Claudine’s death in 1588. After teaching Greek in Lausanne for a few years, Beza settled in Geneva permanently in 1558, mainly because of his admiration for Calvin. He lived there until his death, faithfully serving alongside Calvin and assuming his mantle as leader of the French Reformed church after Calvin’s death in 1564. Beza’s legacy is immense and multifaceted, and it is difficult to summarize it in a few words. He was first and foremost a man of letters. One of his first tasks in Geneva was to complete the translation of the Psalms from Hebrew into French for the Huguenot psalter, a translation left unfinished by another Reformed poet at his death. Beza also published a critical edition of the Greek New Testament that was influential on the Textus Receptus, from which the King James Bible was translated. In fact, the 1565 edition was dedicated to Queen Elizabeth I. In many ways, this was Beza’s lifetime project. He tirelessly corrected and improved the text and published several editions, with the last major revision appearing in 1598. In 1559, he published a “Confession of the Christian Faith,” addressed to his father, to explain why he had embraced the Reformed faith. Although it was penned in a few days, it was hugely popular, as it was published at least thirty-five times during his lifetime and translated into Latin, English, German, and Dutch. He consolidated Calvin’s legacy in Geneva by preaching regularly and teaching theology for forty years. We know from several sources that his teaching was greatly appreciated. For example, an alumnus wrote in 1578: We listened to you with so much admiration and pleasure. Apart from your own personality traits, you combined Melanchthon’s penetrating insights, Calvin’s solid and direct common sense, and Vermigli’s
articles.content_zh: 西奥多·贝扎是今天福音世界中不熟悉的人物. 他深受许多历史学家和神学家的污蔑,他们创造了一个把加尔文神学变成干旱学术体系的紧缩人的形象。 这个形象实际上与事实相去甚远. 谁是西奥多·贝萨? 他于1519年生于法国韦泽莱的一个小法国贵族富裕家庭. 他的生平几乎跨越了整个16世纪,他于1605年以86岁之多去世. 上帝保佑,他的人生有两个明显的转折点。 第一个发生在9岁时,他被安置在路德会学者梅尔奇奥尔·沃尔马尔(Melchior Wolmar)的住处,他成为他的受体. 他与沃尔玛共事了七年,沃尔玛教他法律,拉丁语,希腊语. 有趣的是,当时沃尔玛的其他学生中只有一个是加尔文,他刚刚比贝扎大了十多岁. 沃尔玛给予贝扎一流的教育,而同加尔文一样,贝扎在拉丁语中可能比法语更流利. 更重要的是,沃尔玛在走向新的改革后信仰的旅程中起到了推动作用. 正是通过沃尔玛,在1535年左右的某个时候,贝扎阅读了由瑞士改革者海因里希·布林格所著的一出书并被皈依. 多年后,贝扎写信给布林格:"你让我知道真正的虔诚,以及它最纯洁的来源:上帝之道". 1 然而,贝扎如果透露出他新发现的信仰,就会损失很多. 他通过他的一位叔父获得了大量的教会收入,他是一位方丈,这使得他能够在巴黎享受快乐的生活,专心于诗歌和人文研究. 几年来,他保守了信仰的秘密,他秘密地嫁给了一位巴黎新教商人的女儿克洛丁·德诺塞. 贝扎答应他只要找到真正改革的教堂 就会公开娶她 他生命的第二个转折点是1548年他感染了瘟疫并接近死亡. 他认为这是从真主发出的明确的警告,并且公开地阐明他的信仰。 不久,他逃到日内瓦. 西奥多和克洛丁由加尔文本人公开出嫁,两人始终致力于彼此和基督的事业,直到克洛丁于1588年去世. 在洛桑教希腊语几年后,贝扎于1558年在日内瓦永久定居,这主要是因为他对加尔文的钦佩. 他在那里一直活到去世,忠实地与加尔文并肩服役,并在加尔文于1564年去世后担任法国改革会会长. 贝萨的遗产是巨大的和多方面的,很难用几句话概括一下。 他最先是写信的人 他在日内瓦的最初任务之一是完成将"诗经"从希伯来语翻译成法语,为"胡盖诺特诗人"(Huguenot psalter)所翻译,这是另一位改革诗人死后留下的未完成的译作. 贝扎还出版了"希腊新约"的批判版,该版对"特特鲁斯受体"有影响,从中翻译出"国王詹姆斯圣经". 事实上,1565年版是献给伊丽莎白一世女王. 在很多方面,这是贝扎的一生项目. 他不懈地纠正并改进了文本,并出版了多本版本,最后一出重大修订于1598年. 1559年,他发表了一份致其父亲的“基督教信仰的承认”,以解释他为什么接受改革后的信仰。 虽然短短几天就被收录了,但极受欢迎,因为在他的生平中至少出版了35次并被翻译成了拉丁语,英语,德语和荷兰语. 他通过定期传教和教授神学四十年,巩固了加尔文在日内瓦的遗产. 我们从几个来源知道,他的教学受到极大的赞赏。 例如,一位校友在1578年写道:我们非常钦佩和愉快地聆听了你们的发言. 除了你自己的个性特征,你结合了梅兰希通的洞察力,加尔文的坚实而直接的常识,和弗米利的常识.

articles.title_zh: 点菜（ 10月27日）
articles.content: Good morning from somewhere in rural Colorado. I’m here for the next few days for meetings and training, as well as a bit of hiking and photography and, best of all, some quiet times of writing. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include O. Palmer Robertson’s two-part Christ of the Consummation , which was commended by, among others, D.A. Carson, Sinclair Ferguson, and Joel Beeke. You’ll also find lots of great deals from Zondervan from books that are related to Protestant theology. Recommended Reading Can a Christian Be Demon-Possessed? I know there are many people who are concerned that, even though they are Christians, they may still be possessed by demons. Anthony Faggiano explains why that is not a legitimate fear. “Desire entices us; yielding gives birth to sin; sin grows toward death. Satan can tempt us, but we remain responsible for our desires and decisions. We cannot blame an indwelling demon for what Scripture traces to our sinful hearts. Yet God hasn’t left believers powerless. Through his Holy Spirit, we can begin to put sin to death and walk in obedience.” 7 Keys for Thriving in Lifelong Ministry. I enjoyed reading Joel Beeke’s keys for thriving in pastoral ministry. “Looking back over my ministry over the long term is much more encouraging than looking at it in the short term. A long-term perspective helps me see those who have been saved by the Spirit through my sermons, those marriages that have been strengthened, and even the fruitfulness of elders and deacons who were unsaved when I arrived at my church 40 years ago but have since come to know the Lord personally, vibrantly, and experientially.” Why Does Everyone Else’s Life Seem Better Than Mine? There are some good insights in Zachary Conover’s article on comparison and envy. “Comparison has a way of making us dissatisfied with things we once received with gratitude. We can be thankful for our homes, our families, our work, and the opportunities God has given us. But then we see someone else’s life. We scroll through reel after reel, and suddenly our own begins to feel inadequate. Their opportunities seem greater. Their accomplishments seem more significant. Their circumstances seem more desirable. Am I the only one who doesn’t have it all together? Why don’t I have what they have? And without realizing it, we begin to measure the goodness of God toward us against what He has given to someone else.” Put the Destination in the Frame. John Seel has a guest piece on Aaron Renn’s Substack that offers some helpful points on the way we talk about young men. “We are talking about men incorrectly. We frame discussions of men in terms of problems – the ‘crisis of boys and men’ or ‘failure to launch’ – rather than the destination we want men to arrive at. If we want a different outcome, we need to change the frame of our discussions about men to center on the new reality we want to create. We need a frame that naturally leads us to answer the key question: What kind of men do we want our boys to become?” Welcome to the Valley of Pain. This article from The Atlantic points out, correctly, that the “safe internet” is shrinking and that we need to be more vigilant than ever. “For the next year or two, if not longer, the internet is going to feel a bit touch and go, and more dangerous than we’ve come to expect. ‘It’s going to feel like the sky is falling’ for a while, Prince said. There’s a decades-long backlog of bugs in software written without much review or scrutiny—which was more or less fine so long as there was a very small number of skilled hackers. Over the past two decades, companies, governments, and individuals have been lulled into a false sense of security: Most people don’t think twice about punching credit-card numbers into the website of a local restaurant or gift shop, or forking over a home address and phone number in just about any customer survey. But the internet was always a dangerous place. We’re just waking up from a trance.” Adoption Is Not a T

articles.title_zh: 在婚姻中培养亲密感
articles.content: I recently spent a couple of weeks preparing a great deal of fresh material for a weekend-long marriage seminar. Along the way, I often found myself convicted by the content I was preparing. As I readied myself to teach others, I had to consider the ways in which I needed to be a student before I should be a teacher. One area this proved true was intimacy in marriage—but a kind of intimacy I think many of us seldom consider. There is no doubt that marriage is meant to involve a husband and wife baring their bodies before one another, so that marriage is the context in which a man and woman can experience what it is to be naked and unashamed—to be fully bared, yet fully accepted. And because marriage is meant to be the deepest kind of unity two human beings can experience, it makes sense that there is a physical component to it through which two bodies are literally joined together. This is usually what we mean when we discuss intimacy in marriage. It is my understanding that this kind of intimacy, while real, is also in a way representative or symbolic. It is a demonstration of a unity between two people that is not merely body-deep , but fully soul-deep. Physical intimacy is both significant and essential to marriage, but it is not meant to be the sum total of the intimacy shared between a husband and wife. Yet as Aileen and I have interacted with other couples, we have observed that many husbands and wives find it easier to bare their bodies than their souls. Even as they routinely give themselves to one another physically, they can withhold a great deal relationally and emotionally. Even as they give themselves in free and joyful lovemaking, they can stop short of a greater baring, which is the baring of their souls and the revealing of the deep recesses of their hearts. As Aileen and I discussed this together, we had to conclude that this is something we are prone to as well. It’s not that we hold back shocking secrets or scandalous sins that would cause the other to recoil in dismay or disgust. It’s that we are both reserved people who find it hard to let another person in. We are both wounded people who have been hurt by those who have misused information we have revealed to them. And then I suppose we are both prideful or distrustful people who hold back the pieces of ourselves that we think might cause the other person to lower their respect for us. But by holding back, we are failing to live with full transparency and, therefore, failing to live with full intimacy. The baring of our bodies exceeds the baring of our souls. There is an irony to this, because I am convinced there is a deep longing within each of us to be known. We want someone else to know us as we truly are and to still love us and give us their approval. But even while we want it on one level, we resist it on another, because we wonder what that other person will think of us if they know our deep thoughts, our secret longings, and our hidden fears. We wonder if they will still respect us if they know what causes us to feel shame or express remorse. Perhaps we doubt they’ll still love us if they know who we are far beneath the surface. Still, there is this longing to be known, to be as bare emotionally as we can be physically—and still to be loved and accepted. It is this longing that we never address when we hold back from revealing who and what we truly are, when we refuse to foster a deep soul intimacy—an intimacy that is then represented by, rather than superseded by, sexual intimacy. So how can we foster this kind of baring? By letting our spouse really know us, which may mean creating times and contexts for lengthy, deep, and uninterrupted conversation. This will involve asking good questions and then listening attentively so we can come to a correct rather than trite or hasty understanding of what is being communicated. articles.content_zh: 我最近花了几周时间 准备了大量的新材料 为周末的婚姻研讨会。 一路走来,我常常发现自己被我准备的内容定罪. 当我准备去教别人时,我不得不在做教师之前考虑我需要成为学生的方式。 婚姻中的亲密关系是事实, 毫无疑问,婚姻意味着丈夫和妻子在彼此面前禁止其身体,因此,婚姻是男女能够体验裸体和无羞无耻——被完全禁止,但却被完全接受的背景。 因为婚姻是两个人类能够经历的最深层次的团结,所以它有一个物理成分,通过它,两个身体可以真正结合在一起。 这通常是我们讨论婚姻亲密关系时的意思. 我的理解是,这种亲密关系虽然是真实的,但在某种程度上也是有代表性的或象征性的。 它表明两个人之间的团结 不仅仅是身体深处,而且是灵魂深处 肉体亲密关系对婚姻既重要又重要,但并非夫妻共有亲密关系的总和。 然而,随着艾琳和我与其他夫妇的互动,我们观察到,许多丈夫和妻子发现露出自己的身体比灵魂更容易. 即使在他们习惯上互相施舍的时候,他们也可以在感情上和感情上保持相当的克制。 即使在他们自由而欢快地做爱时,他们也可以停止更大的禁酒,这就是他们的灵魂被束缚,以及他们内心深处的沉睡。 正如我和艾琳一起讨论的那样,我们不得不得出结论,这也是我们容易看到的。 并不是我们隐瞒令人震惊的秘密或可耻的罪恶, 我们都是有保留的人, 我们都是被滥用我们所透露的信息的人所伤害的受伤者。 然后我想,我们都是骄傲或不信任的人,他们屏蔽着我们自己的碎片,我们认为这可能会使他人降低对我们的尊重. 但是,通过阻挠,我们没有完全透明地生活,因此,没有完全亲密地生活。 身体的阻断 超过了灵魂的阻断 这一点具有讽刺意味,因为我相信,我们每个人都有很深的渴望要知道。 我们希望其他人了解我们的真实身份,仍然爱我们,并给予我们批准。 但是,即使我们希望在一个层次上,我们抵制另一个层次,因为我们想知道,如果其他人知道我们的深思熟虑,我们的秘密渴望,以及我们隐藏的恐惧,我们会怎么想。 我们想知道,如果他们知道是什么使我们感到羞愧或表示悔恨,他们是否仍然尊重我们。 也许我们怀疑如果他们知道我们是谁, 然而,人们仍渴望知道这一点,希望我们能像身体上那样裸露出情感——仍然希望得到爱和接受。 正是这种渴望,当我们不愿透露我们真正是谁和什么时,当我们拒绝培养一种深厚的灵魂亲密关系时,我们从未谈到这种渴望——这种亲密关系由性亲密关系而不是取而代之。 那么,我们如何促进这种酒吧? 通过让我们的配偶真正了解我们,这可能意味着为冗长、深入和不间断的对话创造时间和背景。 这将涉及提出好的问题,然后认真倾听,以便我们能够对所传达的内容有一个正确而不是老练或仓促的理解。 真正知道和被了解是一生的工作。 这是工作,但值得致力于工作。 互相保证不会

articles.content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals If all goes well, today’s Kindle deals should include several important books that deal with a Christian understanding of science. Westminster Books is offering a deal this week on the two-part John Calvin’s Illustrated Institutes , which drives the price as low as 50% off. Recommended Reading This Is Roman Catholicism. Here’s a tremendous new project from the Reformanda Initiative—a free documentary series that “offers a firsthand look at often-overlooked yet integral aspects of Roman Catholic theology and practice, challenging idealized perceptions of Rome and encouraging informed, biblical discernment—particularly among those drawn to it. This docuseries is made primarily for Protestant Christians who want to understand what Rome teaches and practices. Featuring: Leonardo De Chirico, Mark Dever, Kevin DeYoung, Albert Mohler, Lauren Montenegro, and Michael Reeves.” Three Ways to Walk With Those Who Grieve. Kirsten Black outlines three ways that any of us can walk faithfully and compassionately with those who are in a time of deep grief. “Often, we do not know how to step into spaces of loss. There is a beautiful and godly desire to bring comfort, yet when facing the reality of walking with the grieving, we are also confronted with the limits of the comfort we can actually offer. This holy work often brings with it an acute awareness of how easy it is to say the wrong thing and unintentionally add more pain to the one who is already suffering.” Explore the Reformation in Ligonier’s Grow App . The Protestant Reformation was not a minor theological dispute—it was a recovery of the biblical gospel. With Reformation Day coming this Saturday, you can explore a variety of free Reformation-themed teaching series with R.C. Sproul in the Grow app from Ligonier Ministries. Download the app and study the five solas , the life of Martin Luther, and much more. (Sponsored) 5 Ways Men Can Serve the Church & 5 Ways Women Can Serve the Church. A pair of articles from Ligonier Ministries offers distinct and meaningful ways that both men and women can serve within the local church. Christian Universalism Is Alive (Just Go to a Funeral). Yes, I have observed as well that funerals are the events where we are most likely to see evidence of Christian universalism. “I’ve been to many funerals and memorial services in my life, and through the years, I’ve encountered religious people who give off the impression that they believe everyone goes to heaven. Culture gives the same impression. Words reveal worldviews. The deceased person may not have received Christ by faith, may not have gone to church, may have even lived an unrepentant and selfish life, and some people still seem to assume they went to a ‘better place’ or went to heaven. Might Christian Universalism be more prevalent than we think?” Stinginess and the Generosity of God. Randy Alcorn contrasts the stinginess of human beings—and even Christian human beings—with the generosity of God. “A life characterized by greed and stinginess is neither Spirit-filled nor Christlike — nor is it happy. If we know Jesus, we will become more and more like our generous God.” Unclear Evangelism Leads to Unclear (And False) Conversions. Writing for 9Marks, John Lee explains how unclear evangelism can lead to false conversions. “When we are unclear about the urgency of conversion, the cost of conversion, or the accountability that should accompany conversion, we risk leaving people deceived about their eternal state. Ultimately, our job is simply to proclaim the gospel clearly, trust God to open people’s hearts to the truth, and provide ongoing discipleship to those who respond in repentance and faith.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. articles.content: “Who is God?” This is the most important question we can ask, yet many people in the United Kingdom are unsure of how to answer it. In this year’s State of Theology survey , 39% of UK adults responded “not sure” to the statement, “There is one true God in three persons: God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit.” The doctrine of the Trinity is fundamental to the Christian faith, because what we believe about God shapes our entire lives. This uncertainty extends beyond the Trinity. This year’s survey results reveal that many UK adults are also unsure about other core Christian beliefs: 39% are unsure of whether Jesus is God 46% are unsure if the Holy Spirit is a personal being 33% are unsure if the Bible is literally true These findings reveal a significant need for clear, faithful Bible teaching. Many people simply do not know what Scripture teaches about God and the Christian faith, and new believers need to be firmly grounded in the truth amid a society that has forgotten many of its biblical roots. articles.title_zh: 马丁·路德是谁？
articles.content: As a doctoral student, Martin Luther finally had access to the university library. Here, for the first time in his life, he held a complete Bible in his hands. The Bible was venerated in the medieval church, and portions of it were read from the lectionary used in worship services. But Bibles had to be copied by hand, so they were very expensive. Many churches did not even own one. And if they did, most people were illiterate, so they could not read it anyway. No wonder the church had drifted from the Word of God. Yes, the medieval church taught that Jesus died for our sins, a salvation applied at baptism. But if you sinned after that, you had to pay. Each sin that you confessed before a priest could be forgiven, as long as you performed some kind of penance. Even forgiven sins, though, required a temporal punishment, if not in this life, then in purgatory. In the meantime, to be saved, a Christian needed to accumulate enough merit through good works and acts of devotion in order to deserve God’s grace and to earn a place in heaven. Young Luther was no rebel. He took the church’s teaching seriously. Church vocations, with their vows of celibacy and other ascetic disciplines, were thought to be more spiritual and more likely to lead to heaven than the worldly lives of the laity. So Luther became a monk, then a priest. Still, he would agonize over his sins. Once he had access to a Bible, he read it voraciously, and a new picture of God, of Christ, and of salvation started to become clear. The University of Wittenberg was one of the new Renaissance schools that stressed going back to the original sources. The medieval universities taught theology through the method known as scholasticism , using authoritative textbooks and rationalistic disputations. But the original source for Christianity is the Bible. And since Renaissance-style, classical education also taught Greek and Hebrew, it became possible to study the Bible in its original languages, whereas previously it had only been available in a Latin translation. When Luther earned his doctorate, the university put him on faculty and gave him the responsibility of teaching the Bible. In preparing a lecture on the book of Romans, Luther struggled to understand this passage: “The righteous shall live by faith” (Rom. 1:17). Suddenly it hit him: We are justified by grace through faith in the atoning work of Jesus Christ! Luther said, “Here I felt that I was altogether born again and had entered paradise itself through open gates.” Meanwhile, it became clearer that the medieval church thought otherwise. It was sponsoring a sale, promising to release Christians from purgatory if they would buy a certificate called an indulgence . People had been taught that they would suffer in penitential fire for seven years for every sin they committed, including those that had been forgiven. Christians were expecting to be in purgatory for thousands of years before they could enter heaven. Of course, they gladly bought indulgences. For Luther, not only was this a cynical scam that exploited the poor (an indulgence cost workers about a week’s wages), it was a monstrous violation of God’s saving Word. On October 31, 1517, Luther nailed to the church door a list of Ninety-Five Theses against the sale of indulgences, which he was willing to debate. Someone, using the newly invented printing press, printed hundreds of copies. Someone else translated them from scholarly Latin into popular German, selling thousands. They soon spread through all of Germany. They were then translated into French, Italian, and English. The Ninety-Five Theses, as we would say today, went viral. The Vatican responded with treatises of its own, which Luther answered. The controversy escalated into other issues. Luther said that the Bible gives no support for indulgences. articles.content_zh: 作为博士生,马丁·路德终于可以进入大学图书馆. 在这里,他一生中第一次手持完整的"圣经". 中世纪的教堂中尊奉了"圣经",其中部分内容取自于礼拜服务中使用的词典. 但"圣经"必须用手抄取,所以非常昂贵. 许多教堂甚至没有一座教堂。 如果他们这样做,大多数人都是文盲,所以他们不能读它。 难怪教堂从上帝的言语里漂了出来 是的,中世纪的教会教诲耶稣为我们的罪而死,这是在受洗时应用的救赎. 但是,如果你有罪 之后,你必须支付。 你向牧师忏悔的每一起罪 都可以被赦免 只要你做了某种忏悔 即使赦免了罪过, 也需要暂时的处罚, 如果在今世没有, 然后在炼狱。 与此同时,为了得到拯救,一个基督教徒需要通过善行和献身行为来积累足够的功绩,以便获得上帝的恩惠和在天堂得到一席之地。 年轻的路德不是反叛者。 他认真对待教会的教义. 教会的教义,以独身和其他醋酸盐学科的誓言,被认为比贵族的世界生活更具有精神,更可能通向天堂. 于是路德成为了道士,后又成为了牧师. 但是,他会为自己的罪孽而痛苦。 一旦他有机会读出圣经,他就非常贪婪地阅读了它,对上帝,基督,救赎的新画面开始变得清晰. 维滕贝格大学是新文艺复兴时期的学校之一,强调要回到原来的来源. 中世纪的大学通过被称为学术主义的方法教授神学,使用权威的教科书和理性的争论. 但基督教的原始来源是"圣经". 而从文艺复兴风格起,古典教育也教授了希腊语和希伯来语,因此可以以原文来研究"圣经",而以前只有拉丁文译本. 当路德获得博士学位后,大学把他安排在教职员上,并赋予他教授"圣经"的责任. 在准备关于罗马人著作的讲座时,路德竭力想理解这一段:“正义者应当以信仰为生”(1:17). 它忽然袭击了他:我们凭着对耶稣基督所行的善行的信念,是被恩典证实的。 路德说,“我在这里感到,我再次出生,并通过开放的大门进入了天堂。” 同时,中世纪的教会也越来越清楚地认为并非如此. 它赞助了一次销售,承诺如果基督徒购买一份名为"宽恕"的证明,他们就会从炼狱中释放出. 人们被告知,他们因犯下的每一项罪行,包括那些被宽恕的罪行,将在忏悔火中受苦七年。 基督徒期望在炼狱中被囚禁了几千年,然后才能入天堂. 当然,他们很高兴 买了宽大。 对路德来说,这不仅是一个剥削穷人的玩世不恭的骗局(允许工人花一周的工资),而且是对上帝拯救言语的粗暴违反。 1517年10月31日,路德在教堂门上钉上一张反对出售放纵品的"九五通"名单,他愿意对此进行辩论. 有人利用新发明的印刷机印刷了上百份. 有人把它们从学术拉丁语翻译成了流行德语,卖出上千个. 它们很快会扩散到整个德国. 随后被翻译成了法语,意大利语和英语. 正如我们今天要说的那样,九十五部曲是病毒性的。 梵蒂冈以自己的论文回应,路德对此作出了回答. 争议升级为其他问题. 路德说圣经不支持宽恕 梵蒂冈回答说,他们得到了教皇的授权. 路德回应道"圣经"是比教皇更高的权威. 梵蒂冈问路德如何

articles.title_zh: 新教改革的原因是什么？
articles.content: What was the matter with the Protestant Reformation? It might seem like a strange question. Some might say that there was nothing the matter with the Reformation, that it was the acme of spiritual recovery of biblical Christianity in church history and therefore was a sort of golden age of biblical faith. Others might say that the matter with the Reformation was that there was one at all, since it produced the largest schism in church history. That’s not what I mean, however, when I ask about what was the matter with the Protestant Reformation. I’m not using the word matter in the normal way, which typically indicates that something is wrong. When we ask, “What’s the matter with you?” we are assuming that something is wrong or that we’re looking for fault. What I mean, by contrast, is this: What was the essence, the substance, or what is called in philosophy the material cause of the Protestant Reformation? Another way to ask it would be this: What was the chief issue that provoked such massive consequences as this split that occurred in the sixteenth century? When historians consider the causes of the Protestant Reformation, they often use distinctions originally set forth by the philosopher Aristotle, and they distinguish between the formal cause and the material cause . The formal cause, the intellectual background to the issue, was a dispute over the seat of final authority that binds the Christian conscience. We’ll look at that under the heading of sola Scriptura . The material cause , however, the substantive issue that was the core point of dispute, was the doctrine of justification. The Protestant view of this matter is expressed in the shorthand of the Latin phrase sola fide . This is the first of the Latin slogans of the Reformation known as the five solas . They are sola fide , justification is by faith alone; sola gratia , salvation is by grace alone; solus Christus , salvation is through Christ alone; sola Scriptura , the sole authority that binds the conscience of the Christian is the Bible alone; and then, finally, soli Deo gloria , to God alone belongs the glory. Sola fide is shorthand for the central issue of the Reformation, the material cause, which was the question of justification. The Protestant Reformers set forth a doctrine that our justification is by faith and by faith alone without any mixture of good works or merit on our part. To understand sola fide in its historical context, we have to understand something about the theological dispute based on the Roman Catholic understanding of justification. At the heart of this dispute was not a tangential debate over how many angels can dance on the head of a pin or a needless controversy over pedantic points of theology that only academics care about. Rather, this issue touched the very heart of the Christian faith because the question of justification is designed to answer this deeper question: How can an unjust person possibly survive the judgment of a just and holy God? In our day, the doctrine of justification has been degraded in terms of its perceived importance. Historically, the differences among churches over how we obtain a right standing before God were considered significant; those differences have now been minimized as having no great weight. We’re living in a time of relativism, which says that there is no objective truth, and pluralism, which declares that there are many different approaches to truth and views of truth. Therefore, people assert, doctrinal issues should never divide us because what really counts are personal relationships, not doctrine. That notion is propounded even though the New Testament is replete with Apostolic concern about correct doctrine. Sadly, that’s not where the church is in this day and age, and sometimes we have to ask, Why? Some people are in church Sunday after Sunday, are continually exposed to the preaching of the gospel, and are members of the church but have never really committed their lives to Christ. S
articles.content_zh: 新教改革有什么问题? 这似乎是一个奇怪的问题。 有人可能会说"改革"没有问题,它是圣经基督教在教会历史上的精神恢复的一环,因此是某种圣经信仰的黄金时代. 其他人可能会说,改革派的问题是,它完全是一个问题,因为它产生了教会历史上最大的分裂。 我问新教改革有什么问题, 我并不以正常方式使用这个词, 当我们问:“你怎么了? ”我们假设有些事情是错的,或者我们在找错。 我的意思是,反之,这是: 什么是实质,实质,或者哲学中所谓的"新教改革的物质事业"? 另一种方式是问: 十六世纪这种分裂造成如此巨大后果的主要问题是什么? 当历史学家考虑新教改革的原因时,他们经常使用哲学家亚里士多德最初提出的区别,并且区分了形式原因和物质原因. 正式的原因,即问题的知识背景,是对约束基督教良知的最终权威所在地的争议. 我们将在索拉·斯克里普图拉(Sola Scriptura)的标题下审视这一点。 然而,实质原因,即作为争议核心问题的实质性问题,是理由理论。 新教徒对此事的看法用拉丁语中的"sola refine"的简写来表达. 这是改革派的拉丁口号中的第一个, 他们都是虔诚的,只有信仰才是正当的;索拉恩典,只有恩典才有救赎;索卢斯·克赖斯,只有基督才有救赎;索拉·斯克利普图拉,将基督教良知捆绑的唯一权威就是《圣经》;最后,索利·德奥·克罗里亚,光靠上帝才是荣耀。 Sola true是改革这一中心问题的简称,即物质原因,即理由问题。 新教改革者提出了一种理论,即我们的理由仅靠信仰和信仰,而没有任何好的工作和功绩。 为了在历史背景中理解 sola true,我们必须根据罗马天主教对理由的理解来理解神学争议. 这场争论的核心不是一场关于有多少天使可以在一针头上跳舞的微小争论,也不是一场关于只有学者关心的神学的教条点的不必要的争论. 相反,这个问题触动了基督教信仰的核心,因为辩解问题旨在回答这个更深层的问题: 一个不公正的人怎么能活过一个公正和神圣的上帝的判断呢? 在我们这个时代,正当理论在被认为的重要性方面已经退化。 历史上,各教会在如何在上帝面前获得权利问题上的分歧被认为是重大的;这些分歧现在已最小化,因为没有很大的分量。 我们生活在相对主义的时代, 说没有客观的真理, 因此,人们断言,理论问题绝不应该分裂我们,因为真正重要的是个人关系,而不是理论。 尽管《新约》充满了使徒对正确学说的关切,但这一概念还是被提出来。 可悲的是, 教堂现在不是这个时代, 有时我们不得不问, 为什么? 有些人周日后在教堂礼拜,不断被传出福音的传道,并且是教堂的成员,但从未真正为基督献出生命. 页:1
